      **Exit criteria:** In test mode, a new visitor can: browse, pick a variant, add to cart, check out as guest with `4242 4242 4242 4242`, see confirmation; register, buy again, see both orders in history; admin sees the orders and can fulfill one. No console errors; `npm run build` passes on both apps.
      
      ### PHASE 2 — Commerce Completeness
      **Tasks:** E1–E3 → K6, K7 → A3, A4 → C6, C7 → SEO baseline (§4) → sitemap/robots/JSON-LD.
      
      **Exit criteria:** emails delivered in test; promo code works; search returns typo-tolerant results; reset-password flow works; structured data validates.
      
      ### PHASE 3 — Differentiators & Polish
      **Tasks:** implement ≥2 options from §5.5 (start with Reviews) → accessibility pass → performance pass (Lighthouse Performance/Accessibility/SEO ≥ 90 on home, listing, product) → dark mode (optional).
      
      **Exit criteria:** custom modules have tests; admin extension works; Lighthouse targets met.
      
      ### PHASE 4 — Testing & Deployment
      **Tasks:**
      - P4.1 Backend tests for custom modules/workflows/routes.
      - P4.2 Playwright E2E: (1) guest purchase, (2) register+login+order history, (3) search, (4) failed payment.
      - P4.3 CI runs lint, types, tests, build; E2E on main or nightly.
      - P4.4 Production config: backend (server + worker mode if applicable per Medusa docs), DB migrations on deploy, Redis, S3 storage, CORS, Stripe webhook URL, domains.
      - P4.5 Deploy storefront to Vercel; backend to chosen host; run production seed; smoke-test full purchase.
      - P4.6 Write `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` with exact steps and a rollback note.
      
      **Exit criteria:** live URLs work end-to-end in Stripe test mode.
      
      ### PHASE 5 — Documentation
      **Tasks:** generate `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (diagram + module/workflow/subscriber inventory), `docs/DECISIONS.md` (key choices and why), `docs/TESTING.md`, and a **separate human-facing `README.human.md`** (pitch, screenshots placeholders, live links, setup, features). Do this only when asked.
      
      ---
      
      ## 10. ARCHITECTURE REFERENCE
      
      ```
      Browser → Next.js Storefront (Vercel)
                    │  Medusa JS SDK (Store API, publishable key)
                    ▼
               Medusa Backend (Node) ──► PostgreSQL
                    │                 ──► Redis (events, workflows, cache)
                    │                 ──► Stripe (payments; webhook → backend)
                    │                 ──► Resend (notifications)
                    │                 ──► Meilisearch (search index)
                    │                 ──► S3/R2 (files)
               Medusa Admin Dashboard (served by backend at /app)
      ```
      
      **Checkout sequence (must be preserved):**
      1. Create/retrieve cart (region-aware) → add line items.
      2. Set email + shipping/billing address.
      3. List and set shipping method.
      4. Initiate payment session (Stripe) → get `client_secret`.
      5. Confirm payment client-side with Stripe Elements.
      6. Complete cart server-side → order created.
      7. `order.placed` event → subscriber sends confirmation email.
      8. Stripe webhook acts as an idempotent safety net.
      
      **Event → handler map (target):**
      | Event | Handler |
      |-------|---------|
      | `order.placed` | send confirmation email |
      | `product.created/updated/deleted` | update Meilisearch index |
      | `fulfillment.created` (or shipment event per docs) | send shipment email |
      | `auth.password_reset` | send reset email |
      
      (Verify exact event names against Medusa docs/installed version before implementing.)
      
      ---
      
      ## 11. CODE QUALITY STANDARDS
      
      - TypeScript `strict`; no `any` unless justified in a comment.
      - Validate all external input (API bodies, query params) with Zod.
      - Small functions, descriptive names, no dead code, no commented-out blocks.
      - Handle and log errors; never swallow them silently. Side-effect failures (email, search) must not break core commerce flows.
      - No secrets, tokens, or personal data in logs.
      - Prefer existing utilities/components over new ones. Keep UI components reusable and in the storefront's `modules/` convention.
      - Comments explain *why*, not *what*.
      
      ---
      
      ## 12. SECURITY & PERFORMANCE CHECKLIST (apply continuously)
      
      - CORS restricted to known origins in production.
      - Secure cookies, strong `JWT_SECRET`/`COOKIE_SECRET` in production.
      - Stripe webhook signature verified.
      - Authenticated routes check customer ownership of resources (orders, addresses, reviews).
      - `npm audit` clean of high/critical issues (or documented).
      - Images optimized; product pages cached/revalidated sensibly; avoid N+1 API calls on listing pages.
      
      ---
      
      ## 13. DEFINITION OF DONE (project)
      
      - [ ] All 🟢 features pass AC.
      - [ ] Phase 1–4 exit criteria met.
      - [ ] CI green; tests cover custom modules and the main purchase flow.
      - [ ] Lighthouse ≥ 90 (Performance, Accessibility, SEO) on key pages.
      - [ ] Deployed; live full purchase works in Stripe test mode.
      - [ ] `.env.template`, `docs/SETUP.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` are accurate.
      - [ ] No secrets in repo history.
      
      ---
      
      ## 14. FIRST ACTION
      
      Begin with **P0.1**: 
      Read the frontend-design skill. Propose a design plan for this store (subject and audience, 4–6 named hex colors, typefaces and roles, layout concept, principles). Save it as docs/DESIGN.md. Wait for my approval before building any page.

      4. What is missing or differs from this spec.
      5. Any risks or questions.

      /**
       * Demo data only — creates 50 published products so the store page's
       * pagination and option facets have something to work with. Safe to delete
       * along with the products it creates; nothing in the app depends on it.
       *
       *   npx medusa exec ./src/scripts/seed-demo-products.ts
       *
       * Re-running it is a no-op for anything it already created: every product uses
       * a deterministic handle, and existing handles are skipped.
       */
      import {
        createCollectionsWorkflow,
        createProductOptionsWorkflow,
        createProductTagsWorkflow,
        createProductsWorkflow,
      } from '@medusajs/medusa/core-flows'
      import {
        ContainerRegistrationKeys,
        MedusaError,
        Modules,
        ProductStatus,
      } from '@medusajs/framework/utils'
      import type { ExecArgs } from '@medusajs/framework/types'
      
      const PRODUCT_COUNT = 50
      const HANDLE_PREFIX = 'demo'
      /** Products are created in batches so one failure doesn't roll back all 50. */
      const BATCH_SIZE = 10
      /** Caps the variant count per product, since options multiply. */
      const MAX_VARIANTS = 12
      /** Products per awaited search-ingestion call. */
      const INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE = 25
      
      /**
       * Deterministic PRNG (mulberry32). Keeps re-runs identical, so the same handle
       * always describes the same product.
       */
      function makeRandom(seed: number) {
        let state = seed
      
        return () => {
          state = (state + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0
          let t = Math.imul(state ^ (state >>> 15), 1 | state)
          t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t
          return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
        }
      }
      
      const ADJECTIVES = [
        'Vintage', 'Classic', 'Relaxed', 'Tailored', 'Oversized',
        'Everyday', 'Heritage', 'Essential', 'Cropped', 'Lightweight',
      ]
      const MATERIALS = ['Cotton', 'Linen', 'Merino', 'Denim', 'Fleece', 'Twill']
      const TYPES = [
        'Tee', 'Hoodie', 'Sweatshirt', 'Shorts', 'Joggers',
        'Overshirt', 'Cap', 'Socks', 'Tote', 'Beanie',
      ]
      
      const COLLECTIONS = ['Summer Essentials', 'Winter Layers', 'Everyday Basics', 'Limited Run']
      const TAGS = ['sale', 'new-arrival', 'organic', 'unisex', 'bestseller', 'last-chance']
      
      /**
       * Extra shared options, so the store page's option facet shows more than the
       * Size and Color the initial seed creates.
       */
      const EXTRA_OPTIONS = [
        { title: 'Material', values: ['Cotton', 'Linen', 'Merino', 'Fleece'] },
        { title: 'Fit', values: ['Regular', 'Slim', 'Relaxed'] },
        { title: 'Sleeve', values: ['Short', 'Long'] },
      ]
      
      /** Real Medusa demo images, so the grid isn't full of placeholders. */
      const IMAGES = [
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/tee-black-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/tee-white-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/sweatshirt-vintage-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/sweatpants-gray-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/shorts-vintage-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/coffee-mug.png',
      ]
      
      type SharedOption = { id: string; title: string; values: string[] }
      
      export default async function seedDemoProducts({ container }: ExecArgs) {
        const logger = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LOGGER)
        const query = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY)
        const random = makeRandom(20260831)
      
        const pick = <T>(items: T[]): T => items[Math.floor(random() * items.length)]
        const pickSome = <T>(items: T[], max: number): T[] => {
          const count = Math.floor(random() * (max + 1))
          return [...items].sort(() => random() - 0.5).slice(0, count)
        }
      
        // ---- Prerequisites that already exist in the project ----------------------
      
        const { data: salesChannels } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'sales_channel',
          fields: ['id', 'name'],
        })
        const { data: shippingProfiles } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'shipping_profile',
          fields: ['id'],
        })
        const { data: categories } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_category',
          fields: ['id', 'name'],
        })
        const { data: stores } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'store',
          fields: ['id', 'supported_currencies.currency_code'],
        })
      
        const salesChannel = salesChannels[0]
        const shippingProfile = shippingProfiles[0]
      
        if (!salesChannel || !shippingProfile) {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
            'No sales channel or shipping profile found. Run the initial data seed first.'
          )
        }
      
        const currencyCodes: string[] = (
          stores[0]?.supported_currencies ?? []
        )
          .map((currency) => currency?.currency_code)
          .filter((code): code is string => Boolean(code))
      
        if (!currencyCodes.length) {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
            'The store has no supported currencies.'
          )
        }
      
        logger.info(
          `Seeding into "${salesChannel.name}" with currencies: ${currencyCodes.join(', ')}`
        )
      
        // ---- Collections, tags and extra options --------------------------------
      
        const { data: existingCollections } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_collection',
          fields: ['id', 'title'],
        })
        const missingCollections = COLLECTIONS.filter(
          (title) => !existingCollections.some((collection) => collection.title === title)
        )
      
        if (missingCollections.length) {
          await createCollectionsWorkflow(container).run({
            input: { collections: missingCollections.map((title) => ({ title })) },
          })
          logger.info(`Created ${missingCollections.length} collection(s)`)
        }
      
        const { data: allCollections } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_collection',
          fields: ['id', 'title'],
        })
      
        const { data: existingTags } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_tag',
          fields: ['id', 'value'],
        })
        const missingTags = TAGS.filter(
          (value) => !existingTags.some((tag) => tag.value === value)
        )
      
        if (missingTags.length) {
          await createProductTagsWorkflow(container).run({
            input: { product_tags: missingTags.map((value) => ({ value })) },
          })
          logger.info(`Created ${missingTags.length} tag(s)`)
        }
      
        const { data: allTags } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_tag',
          fields: ['id', 'value'],
        })
      
        // Shared (non-exclusive) options, the way the initial seed defines them.
        const { data: existingOptions } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_option',
          fields: ['id', 'title', 'values.value'],
          filters: { is_exclusive: false },
        })
      
        const missingOptions = EXTRA_OPTIONS.filter(
          (option) => !existingOptions.some((existing) => existing.title === option.title)
        )
      
        if (missingOptions.length) {
          await createProductOptionsWorkflow(container).run({
            input: { product_options: missingOptions },
          })
          logger.info(`Created ${missingOptions.length} shared option(s)`)
        }
      
        const { data: optionRows } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_option',
          fields: ['id', 'title', 'values.value'],
          filters: { is_exclusive: false },
        })
      
        const sharedOptions: SharedOption[] = optionRows
          .map((option) => ({
            id: option.id as string,
            title: option.title as string,
            values: (option.values ?? [])
              .map((value) => value?.value)
              .filter((value): value is string => Boolean(value)),
          }))
          .filter((option) => option.values.length > 0)
      
        const sizeOption = sharedOptions.find((option) => option.title === 'Size')
      
        if (!sizeOption) {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
            'No shared "Size" option found. Run the initial data seed first.'
          )
        }
      
        // ---- Build the products -------------------------------------------------
      
        const { data: alreadySeeded } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product',
          fields: ['handle'],
        })
        const takenHandles = new Set(
          alreadySeeded.map((product) => product.handle).filter(Boolean)
        )
      
        const products: Record<string, unknown>[] = []
      
        for (let index = 0; index < PRODUCT_COUNT; index++) {
          // Derived from the index, never from the PRNG. Skipping a product consumes
          // fewer random numbers than building one, so a handle that depended on the
          // PRNG would shift after the first skip and the script would create
          // duplicates instead of recognising its own products.
          const type = TYPES[index % TYPES.length]
          const handle = `${HANDLE_PREFIX}-${index + 1}-${type.toLowerCase()}`
      
          if (takenHandles.has(handle)) {
            continue
          }
      
          const title = `${pick(ADJECTIVES)} ${pick(MATERIALS)} ${type}`
      
          // Size is always present; the rest vary so the facet has uneven counts.
          const chosenOptions = [
            sizeOption,
            ...pickSome(
              sharedOptions.filter((option) => option.title !== 'Size'),
              2
            ),
          ]
      
          // Cartesian product of the chosen options' values, capped.
          let combinations: Record<string, string>[] = [{}]
      
          for (const option of chosenOptions) {
            const next: Record<string, string>[] = []
      
            for (const combination of combinations) {
              for (const value of option.values) {
                if (next.length >= MAX_VARIANTS) {
                  break
                }
                next.push({ ...combination, [option.title]: value })
              }
            }
      
            combinations = next
          }
      
          const collection = pick(allCollections)
          const chosenTags = pickSome(allTags, 3)
          const chosenCategories = pickSome(categories, 2)
          const thumbnail = pick(IMAGES)
          const basePrice = 10 + Math.floor(random() * 90)
      
          products.push({
            title,
            handle,
            subtitle: `${type} — demo data`,
            description: `A ${title.toLowerCase()} generated to fill out the demo catalogue. Not a real product.`,
            status: ProductStatus.PUBLISHED,
            thumbnail,
            images: [{ url: thumbnail }],
            weight: 300 + Math.floor(random() * 500),
            shipping_profile_id: shippingProfile.id,
            collection_id: collection?.id,
            tag_ids: chosenTags.map((tag) => tag.id as string),
            category_ids: chosenCategories.map((category) => category.id as string),
            sales_channels: [{ id: salesChannel.id }],
            options: chosenOptions.map((option) => ({ id: option.id })),
            variants: combinations.map((combination) => ({
              title: Object.values(combination).join(' / '),
              sku: `${handle.toUpperCase()}-${Object.values(combination).join('-').toUpperCase()}`,
              options: combination,
              prices: currencyCodes.map((currency_code) => ({
                amount: basePrice,
                currency_code,
              })),
            })),
          })
        }
      
        if (!products.length) {
          logger.info('Every demo product already exists. Nothing to do.')
          return
        }
      
        // ---- Create them --------------------------------------------------------
      
        let created = 0
      
        for (let start = 0; start < products.length; start += BATCH_SIZE) {
          const batch = products.slice(start, start + BATCH_SIZE)
      
          await createProductsWorkflow(container).run({
            input: { products: batch as never },
          })
      
          created += batch.length
          logger.info(`Created ${created}/${products.length} demo products`)
        }
      
        // ---- Make sure the search index caught up -------------------------------
      
        // `product.created` is emitted on the local event bus and handled
        // asynchronously, so a short-lived `medusa exec` process can exit before the
        // last batch is ingested. Replaying the ingestion here is awaited, and
        // `consume` upserts, so it is safe to run over every product.
        const search = container.resolve(Modules.SEARCH)
        const { data: allProducts } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product',
          fields: ['id'],
        })
      
        for (let start = 0; start < allProducts.length; start += INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE) {
          const chunk = allProducts.slice(start, start + INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE)
      
          await search.ingest({
            name: 'product.created',
            data: chunk.map((product) => ({ id: product.id })),
          } as never)
        }
      
        logger.info(`Search index caught up for ${allProducts.length} product(s).`)
        logger.info('Done. Open the store page to see the new products.')
      }

      export default async function initial_data_seed({

        const logger = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LOGGER);

          },

        const {

          input: {

                created_by: "",

            ],
          },
        });
      
        await linkSalesChannelsToApiKeyWorkflow(container).run({
          input: {

            add: [defaultSalesChannel.id],

        const {

          input: {

- path: apps/storefront/src/lib/data/regions.ts
  content: |
      "use server"
      
      import { sdk } from "@lib/config"
      import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
      import { getCacheOptions } from "./cookies"
      
      export const listRegions = async () => {
        const next = {
          ...(await getCacheOptions("regions")),
        }
      
        return await sdk.client
          .fetch<{ regions: HttpTypes.StoreRegion[] }>(`/store/regions`, {
            method: "GET",
            next,
            cache: "force-cache",
          })
          .then(({ regions }) => regions)
      }
      
      export const retrieveRegion = async (id: string) => {
        const next = {
          ...(await getCacheOptions(["regions", id].join("-"))),
        }
      
        return await sdk.client
          .fetch<{ region: HttpTypes.StoreRegion }>(`/store/regions/${id}`, {
            method: "GET",
            next,
            cache: "force-cache",
          })
          .then(({ region }) => region)
      }
      
      const regionMap = new Map<string, HttpTypes.StoreRegion>()
      
      export const getRegion = async (countryCode: string) => {
        if (regionMap.has(countryCode)) {
          return regionMap.get(countryCode)
        }
      
        const regions = await listRegions()
      
        if (!regions) {
          return null
        }
      
        regions.forEach((region) => {
          region.countries?.forEach((c) => {
            regionMap.set(c?.iso_2 ?? "", region)
          })
        })
      
        const region = countryCode
          ? regionMap.get(countryCode)
          : regionMap.get("us")
      
        return region
      }

      # DevCart — Design Plan
      
      Status: **proposal, awaiting owner approval.** No page is built from this yet.
      
      ## 1. Subject, audience, and job
      
      The spec names the store **DevCart** but does not define what it sells, so this is a proposal.
      
      - **Subject:** a small direct-to-consumer brand selling merchandise for people who build software — apparel (tees, hoodies, caps, totes) plus desk objects (mugs, keycaps, notebooks, stickers). Everything is drawn from software-making culture: version numbers, changelogs, compiler and terminal culture, hardware and keyboards.
      - **Audience:** developers, computer-science students, and engineering teams buying personal items or small team swag. They read Latin text in English, know what a keyboard shortcut is, and are unimpressed by generic tech-bro marketing. They buy on the strength of the joke, the typography, and the print quality.
      - **Primary job:** make it easy to find one product, understand exactly what it is and what it costs, and check out in a few steps. Personality lives in the catalogue, not in the checkout.
      
      The seed data in this repository is already apparel (tee, sweatshirt, sweatpants, shorts) with generic "Medusa" titles. The demo catalogue will be rewritten to fit the DevCart brand in Phase 1; the item types stay the same.
      
      ## 2. Colour — riso inks on uncoated stock
      
      DevCart's catalogue is printed merchandise, so the palette is built from actual risograph ink behaviour: flat, slightly translucent inks, limited to one or two per impression, misregistering by a hair against each other. That constraint is the identity. It is also deliberately not the warm-cream-plus-terracotta look, and not near-black-plus-acid-green.
      
      | Token | Hex | Role |
      |-------|-----|------|
      | `stock` | `#E8E9E3` | Page background. Cool uncoated paper, not a warm cream. |
      | `ink` | `#17181B` | Body text, rules, plate borders. The "black" plate. |
      | `riso-blue` | `#006DAE` | Primary brand colour: links, primary buttons, focus ring. |
      | `riso-pink` | `#FB008E` | The accent. Large display text on stock, fills, markers. |
      | `riso-yellow` | `#FFD400` | Fill only. Highlight behind ink text, used rarely. |
      | `riso-green` | `#007942` | State: in stock, order confirmed. Text or fill. |
      
      **AA adjustment.** `riso-blue`, `riso-pink` and `riso-green` are darkened from the raw riso ink values (`#0078BF`, `#FF48B0`, `#00A95C`) so that every permitted text usage meets WCAG AA. Hue is preserved in each case. §2.1 records the measurements; `stock`, `ink` and `riso-yellow` are unchanged.
      
      Rules of use:
      
      - **Two inks per view, maximum.** `ink` + `riso-blue` is the default impression. `riso-pink` is the second ink, and it earns its place by marking something specific (an on-sale price, the current filter, the hero headline).
      - **Overprint, not shadow.** Where two inks meet, use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` so the overlap darkens like real ink. This replaces drop shadows entirely — no soft grey card shadows anywhere.
      - Yellow and green never carry meaning on their own; they always sit next to a word that says the same thing.
      
      ### 2.1 Contrast, measured
      
      Ratios are WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance contrast ratios against the token pairs actually used. AA needs 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (24px+, or 19px+ bold) and for non-text markers and boundaries.
      
      | Foreground | Background | Ratio | AA normal text | AA large text / markers |
      |---|---|---|---|---|
      | `ink` | `stock` | 14.54:1 | pass | pass |
      | `stock` | `ink` | 14.54:1 | pass | pass |
      | `ink` | `riso-yellow` | 12.40:1 | pass | pass |
      | `ink` | `riso-pink` | 4.64:1 | pass | pass |
      | `riso-blue` | `stock` | 4.53:1 | pass | pass |
      | `stock` | `riso-blue` | 4.53:1 | pass | pass |
      | `riso-green` | `stock` | 4.51:1 | pass | pass |
      | `stock` | `riso-green` | 4.51:1 | pass | pass |
      | `riso-pink` | `stock` | 3.13:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `stock` | `riso-pink` | 3.13:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `ink` | `riso-green` | 3.22:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `ink` | `riso-blue` | 3.21:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `riso-green` | `ink` | 3.22:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `blue` | `ink` | 3.21:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `riso-yellow` | `stock` | 1.17:1 | **fail** | **fail** |
      
      Rules that follow from the table, and which the base components enforce:
      
      - **`riso-pink` is never text below 24px.** It passes AA only as large display type, as a fill, or as a marker (3:1 for non-text). No body copy, no links, no form labels, no button labels.
      - **Never `stock` on `riso-pink`** (3.13:1). Text on a pink fill is `ink` (4.64:1).
      - **Never `ink` on `riso-blue`** (3.21:1). Text on a blue fill is `stock` (4.53:1).
      - **Never `ink` on `riso-green`; use `stock` on green** (4.51:1). `riso-green` as text on `stock` is fine.
      - **`riso-yellow` is a fill, never text**, and only ever behind `ink` (12.40:1).
      - `riso-blue` and `riso-green` as text on `stock` both clear normal-text AA, so links and state labels may use them directly.
      
      ## 3. Typography
      
      Two families plus one data face. Not Inter, not Space Grotesk, not a system stack.
      
      - **Display — Bricolage Grotesque** (variable, Google Fonts). Headlines, the hero, product titles, category names. It has a slightly irregular poster-grotesque character that suits printed merchandise and looks unlike a default UI font. Used at large sizes with tight tracking, and only at large sizes.
      - **Body / UI — IBM Plex Sans.** Paragraphs, labels, buttons, forms, navigation. Engineering heritage that fits the subject and stays legible at 14–16px, which is where a store's real reading happens.
      - **Data — IBM Plex Mono.** Reserved for content that is genuinely machine data: SKUs, spec tables ("100% cotton / 240 gsm"), order numbers, and code-like product names. Not used for eyebrows, nav labels, or decorative captions.
      
      Type scale (1.25 ratio, base 16px): 14 / 16 / 20 / 25 / 31 / 39 / 49 / 61. Body line length capped at ~72 characters; display lines at ~40.
      
      Weights: Bricolage Grotesque 700 for display; IBM Plex Sans 400 for body, 600 for buttons and labels. Normal sentence case everywhere — no all-caps labels.
      
      ## 4. Layout — the press sheet
      
      The page is treated as a print sheet, not a stack of floating cards. A visible hairline grid and small corner registration marks define the content area; every element is aligned to that grid.
      
      - Content is **left-aligned** on a centred max-width column of 1280px, with a lopsided editorial rhythm: the 12-column grid is divided roughly 7/5 rather than 6/6, so nothing sits dead centre.
      - Product cards are **plates**: square corners, a hairline `ink` border, the image on `stock`, and the title/price set below in a fixed type block. No border-radius, no shadow, no gradient. One consistent square edge is the system; rounded corners are never introduced.
      - **No numbered markers** except where something really is a sequence — order status (placed → paid → shipped) and checkout steps. Product plates are not numbered.
      - Sections are separated by rules and whitespace, not by alternating background colours.
      - Mobile (360 / 768 / 1280) collapses the grid to one and two columns; the alignment stays left.
      
      ### Home
      
      ```
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      | DevCart        Shop  Collections  About      Search  Cart |
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      |                                                          |
      |  Merch for                                               |
      |  people who        [ hero: product photo with            |
      |  build software    riso-pink and riso-blue plates        |
      |                    offset against it ]                   |
      |  [ Shop new ]  [ Browse all ]                             |
      |                                                          |
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      |  New this drop                                            |
      |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+           |
      |  | plate  |  | plate  |  | plate  |  | plate  |           |
      |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+           |
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      |  Collections:  Everyday  /  Desk  /  Limited Run          |
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      ```
      
      ### Listing (`/store`, category, collection)
      
      ```
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      |  All products                 [ search ]                  |
      +---------------+------------------------------------------+
      | Sort          |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+       |
      |  Newest       |  | plate  |  | plate  |  | plate  |       |
      | Category      |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+       |
      |  [x] Shirts   |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+       |
      | Price         |  | plate  |  | plate  |  | plate  |       |
      |  |----o----|  |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+       |
      +---------------+------------------------------------------+
      |                    <  1 2 3  >                            |
      ```
      
      ### Product
      
      ```
      +-------------------------------+--------------------------+
      |  [ gallery: main image ]      |  Hoodie                  |
      |  +----+ +----+ +----+         |  EUR 45.00   in stock    |
      |  |    | |    | |    |         |                          |
      |  +----+ +----+ +----+         |  Size  [S] [M] [L] [XL]  |
      |                               |  Colour [ink] [pink]     |
      |                               |  [ Add to cart ]         |
      |                               |  ---------------------   |
      |                               |  Specs (mono table)      |
      |                               |  SKU  DC-HOOD-INK-M      |
      +-------------------------------+--------------------------+
      ```
      
      ## 5. Principles
      
      1. **Ink is scarce.** Two colours per screen, one of them loud. If a third appears, something above it gets removed.
      2. **The grid is visible and load-bearing.** Rules, registration marks, and plate edges carry real structure; they are not decoration. Removing them should break the layout's legibility, not just its mood.
      3. **Type is the image.** Display headlines are content and are set as such. No stock-photo hero collages, no gradient washes, no icon-and-heading card trios.
      4. **Products are editions.** Specs, SKUs and print details are shown as plain, useful facts — an honest product page is the brand's tone, not a marketing one.
      5. **Motion is mechanical and rare.** Motion answers a click: adding to cart, opening the cart drawer, switching a variant image. No scroll-triggered fade-up on every section, no hover lift on every card. See §5.1.
      
      ### 5.1 Deferred polish
      
      Three visual devices are **optional polish, built last** — after the pages and the commerce flows work, and only if they still earn their place:
      
      1. **Registration marks** — small corner crop marks on plates and page sections.
      2. **Overprint** — `mix-blend-mode: multiply` where two inks overlap.
      3. **Settle-into-register** — the single page-load animation where plates align, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`.
      
      Until then, plates use plain hairline borders and no blend modes. The base components must look finished without any of these, so none of them may be load-bearing.
      6. **Copy is plain.** Sentence case, active voice, one job per string. The button says "Add to cart", the toast says "Added to cart". Empty cart says what to do next; an error says what failed and how to fix it. No filler, no exclamation marks.
      
      ## 6. Review against the brief
      
      Checked against the common generated-design defaults before building:
      
      - **Changed:** the original pass used a warm cream `#F4F1EA` background with a serif display and a clay accent. That is the single most recognisable generated palette, so the ground moved to a cool uncoated `stock` `#E8E9E3`, the display face to Bricolage Grotesque, and the accent to riso pink — a colour that comes from the subject's actual production method rather than from a mood board.
      - **Changed:** an early layout used rounded cards with soft shadows (the SaaS-card kit). Replaced with square hairline plates and multiply overprint, which is what printed merchandise actually looks like.
      - **Changed:** mono was initially going to label nav items and eyebrows. Cut back to machine data only, since mono-for-labels is a template tell and this brief does not need it.
      - **Changed:** the raw riso inks were kept for shape but darkened where they failed AA. Blue and green moved just far enough to clear 4.5:1 on `stock`; pink moved to 3.13:1 on stock while holding 4.64:1 for `ink` text on a pink fill. The exact riso values survive only as the hue reference in §2.
      - **Kept, because the brief justifies it:** tight display typography and hard grid edges — this is a print catalogue, and those are its real conventions, not a stylistic costume.
      
      ## 7. Decisions confirmed by the owner
      
      1. **Subject:** developer merchandise, as described in §1.
      2. **Name:** DevCart.
      3. **Mode:** light mode only for now; dark mode deferred (Phase 3 marks it optional).
      4. **Headlines:** sentence case everywhere, including the wireframes above.
      5. **Accessibility:** `riso-pink` and `riso-blue` must meet WCAG AA for any text usage; see §2.1.
      6. **Polish:** registration marks, overprint and the settle animation are deferred to last; see §5.1.

      "use client"
      
      import { usePathname, useRouter, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation"
      import { useCallback, useMemo } from "react"
      
      import {
        OPTION_VALUE_QUERY_KEY,
        parseOptionValueIds,
      } from "@lib/util/product-option-filters"
      import OptionsPicker from "./options-picker"
      import SortProducts, { SortOptions } from "./sort-products"
      
      type RefinementListProps = {
        sortBy: SortOptions
        search?: boolean
        hideOptionsPicker?: boolean
        "data-testid"?: string
      }
      
      const RefinementList = ({
        sortBy,
        hideOptionsPicker = false,
        "data-testid": dataTestId,
      }: RefinementListProps) => {
        const router = useRouter()
        const pathname = usePathname()
        const searchParams = useSearchParams()
      
        const updateQueryParams = useCallback(
          (updater: (params: URLSearchParams) => void) => {
            const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString())
            updater(params)
      
            params.delete("page")
      
            const queryString = params.toString()
            const currentQuery = searchParams.toString()
            const nextPath = queryString ? `${pathname}?${queryString}` : pathname
            const currentPath = currentQuery
              ? `${pathname}?${currentQuery}`
              : pathname
      
            if (nextPath !== currentPath) {
              router.push(nextPath)
            }
          },
          [pathname, router, searchParams]
        )
      
        const setQueryParams = (name: string, value: string) =>
          updateQueryParams((params) => params.set(name, value))
      
        const selectedOptionValueIds = useMemo(
          () => parseOptionValueIds(searchParams),
          [searchParams]
        )
      
        const setOptionValueIds = (valueIds: string[]) =>
          updateQueryParams((params) => {
            params.delete(OPTION_VALUE_QUERY_KEY)
            valueIds.forEach((valueId) =>
              params.append(OPTION_VALUE_QUERY_KEY, valueId)
            )
          })
      
        return (
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-12 py-4 mb-8 small:px-0 pl-6 small:min-w-[250px] small:ml-[1.675rem]">
            <SortProducts
              sortBy={sortBy}
              setQueryParams={setQueryParams}
              data-testid={dataTestId}
            />
            {!hideOptionsPicker && (
              <OptionsPicker
                selectedValueIds={selectedOptionValueIds}
                setOptionValueIds={setOptionValueIds}
              />
            )}
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default RefinementList
      
  referencedBy: {}

index.tsx
"use client"

import * as Accordion from "@radix-ui/react-accordion"
import { useEffect, useState } from "react"

import { ChevronDownMini } from "@medusajs/icons"
import { sdk } from "@lib/config"
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
import clsx from "clsx"

type OptionsPickerProps = {
  selectedValueIds: string[]
  setOptionValueIds: (valueIds: string[]) => void
}

const OptionsPicker = ({
  selectedValueIds,
  setOptionValueIds,
}: OptionsPickerProps) => {
  const [options, setOptions] = useState<HttpTypes.StoreProductOption[]>([])
  const [openItems, setOpenItems] = useState<string[]>([])

  useEffect(() => {
    const fetchOptions = async () => {
      try {
        const response = await sdk.client.fetch<{
          product_options?: HttpTypes.StoreProductOption[]
        }>("/store/product-options", {
          method: "GET",
          query: {
            is_exclusive: false,
            fields: "*values",
          },
        })

        if (response?.product_options) {
          setOptions(response.product_options)
        }
      } catch (error) {
        console.error("Failed to fetch product options", error)
      }
    }

    fetchOptions()
  }, [])

  useEffect(() => {
    if (options.length) {
      setOpenItems(options.map((option) => option.id))
    }
  }, [options])

  if (!options.length) {
    return null
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-y-4">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between px-1">
        <span className="txt-compact-small-plus text-ui-fg-subtle">
          Options
        </span>
      </div>
      <Accordion.Root
        type="multiple"
        value={openItems}
        onValueChange={(values) => setOpenItems(values as string[])}
        className="flex flex-col gap-y-3 pr-6"
      >
        {options.map((option) => {
          const values =
            option.values
              ?.map((value) => ({
                id: value.id,
                label: value.value,
              }))
              .filter(
                (value): value is { id: string; label: string } =>
                  !!value.id && !!value.label
              ) || []

          if (!values.length) {
            return null
          }

          const toggleValue = (valueId: string) => {
            const isSelected = selectedValueIds.includes(valueId)
            const nextSelections = isSelected
              ? selectedValueIds.filter((id) => id !== valueId)
              : [...selectedValueIds, valueId]

            setOptionValueIds(Array.from(new Set(nextSelections)))
          }

          const isOpen = openItems.includes(option.id)
          const selectedCount = values.filter((value) =>
            selectedValueIds.includes(value.id)
          ).length

          return (
            <Accordion.Item
              key={option.id}
              value={option.id}
              className="overflow-hidden"
            >
              <Accordion.Header>
                <Accordion.Trigger className="flex w-full items-center justify-between py-3 text-left">
                  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
                    <span className="txt-compact-small-plus text-ui-fg-base">
                      {option.title || "Option"}
                    </span>
                    <span className="txt-compact-small-plus text-ui-fg-muted">
                      ({selectedCount})
                    </span>
                  </div>
                  <span
                    className={clsx(
                      "flex h-7 w-7 items-center justify-center text-ui-fg-muted transition-transform duration-150",
                      {
                        "rotate-180": isOpen,
                      }
                    )}
                  >
                    <ChevronDownMini />
                  </span>
                </Accordion.Trigger>
              </Accordion.Header>
              <Accordion.Content className="pb-4 pt-1">
                <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
                  {values.map((value) => {
                    const isSelected = selectedValueIds.includes(value.id)

                    return (
                      <button
                        key={value.id}
                        onClick={() => toggleValue(value.id)}
                        className={clsx(
                          "border-ui-border-base border text-small-regular h-10 rounded-rounded px-3 flex items-center transition-colors duration-150",
                          {
                            "border-ui-border-interactive text-ui-fg-base":
                              isSelected,
                            "text-ui-fg-muted hover:text-ui-fg-base":
                              !isSelected,
                          }
                        )}
                        aria-pressed={isSelected}
                      >
                        {value.label}
                      </button>
                    )
                  })}
                </div>
              </Accordion.Content>
            </Accordion.Item>
          )
        })}
      </Accordion.Root>
    </div>
  )
}

export default OptionsPicker

     * @returns {Promise<SearchReindexResult>} The ID of the job performing the

     * @example
     * To rebuild a single index:
     *
     * ```ts
     * const { job_id } = await searchModuleService.reindex({
     *   index: "product",
     * })

     *
     * To rebuild part of an index in place:

     *   strategy: "in_place",
     *   filters: {

     * state has drifted past what a reindex can repair.
     *
     * The index definition itself is untouched — it lives in your code, not in the

      import type {
        RemoteQueryFunction,
        SearchTypes,
      } from "@medusajs/framework/types";
      
      const RESOLVE_BATCH_SIZE = 200;
      
      // Core emits either a single `{ id }` or a batch of them.
      function payloadIds(data: unknown): string[] {
        return (Array.isArray(data) ? data : [data])
          .map((entry) => (entry as { id?: string } | undefined)?.id)
          .filter((id): id is string => Boolean(id));
      }
      
      /**
       * The products behind rows of another entity, read through `query.graph`.
       * Deleted rows are soft-deleted, so they're still readable with `withDeleted`,
       * which is how a deleted variant or category still leads back to its products.
       */
      async function relatedProductIds(
        query: RemoteQueryFunction,
        entity: string,
        fields: string[],
        ids: string[],
        pick: (row: Record<string, any>) => (string | null | undefined)[],
        withDeleted: boolean,
      ): Promise<string[]> {
        const { data } = await query.graph({
          entity,
          fields,
          filters: { id: ids },
          withDeleted,
        });
      
        return (data as Record<string, any>[])
          .flatMap(pick)
          .filter((id): id is string => Boolean(id));
      }
      
      /**
       * Deleting a sales channel removes its product links, so the products can no
       * longer be found through `query.graph`. The index still holds the channel on
       * each document, which is what's searched here.
       */
      async function productIdsInSalesChannels(
        query: RemoteQueryFunction,
        salesChannelIds: string[],
      ): Promise<string[]> {
        const ids: string[] = [];
        let skip = 0;
      
        while (true) {
          const { search_result: result } = await query.search({
            entity: "product",
            fields: ["id"],
            filters: { sales_channel_ids: salesChannelIds },
            pagination: { skip, take: RESOLVE_BATCH_SIZE },
          });
      
          ids.push(...result.hits.map((hit) => hit.id));
      
          if (result.hits.length < RESOLVE_BATCH_SIZE) {
            return ids;
          }
      
          skip += RESOLVE_BATCH_SIZE;
        }
      }
      
      /**
       * The products an event affects. A product event carries them directly; an
       * event about a variant, option, tag, category or sales channel is mapped to
       * the products behind it.
       */
      export async function resolveProductIds(
        event: { name: string; data: unknown },
        { container: { query } }: SearchTypes.SearchIngestionContext,
      ): Promise<string[]> {
        const ids = payloadIds(event.data);
      
        if (!ids.length) {
          return [];
        }
      
        const [entity] = event.name.split(".");
        const deleted = event.name.endsWith(".deleted");
      
        switch (entity) {
          case "product":
            return ids;
          case "product-variant":
            return relatedProductIds(
              query,
              "product_variant",
              ["product_id"],
              ids,
              (row) => [row.product_id],
              deleted,
            );
          case "product-option":
            return relatedProductIds(
              query,
              "product_option",
              ["product_id"],
              ids,
              (row) => [row.product_id],
              deleted,
            );
          case "product-option-value":
            return relatedProductIds(
              query,
              "product_option_value",
              ["option.product_id"],
              ids,
              (row) => [row.option?.product_id],
              deleted,
            );
          case "product-tag":
            return relatedProductIds(
              query,
              "product_tag",
              ["products.id"],
              ids,
              (row) => (row.products ?? []).map((product: any) => product?.id),
              deleted,
            );
          case "product-category":
            return relatedProductIds(
              query,
              "product_category",
              ["products.id"],
              ids,
              (row) => (row.products ?? []).map((product: any) => product?.id),
              deleted,
            );
          case "sales-channel":
            return productIdsInSalesChannels(query, ids);
          default:
            return [];
        }
      }
      
  referencedBy: {}

Tee and mug, boxed, black only.\",\n    category: \"Kits\",\n    collections: [\"Desk & Debug\", \"Limited Run\"],\n    tags: [\"new-arrival\", \"unisex\"],\n    images: KIT_IMAGES,\n    options: [SIZE],\n    price: KIT_PRICE,\n    weight: 800,\n    stock: 5,\n  },\n]\n\n// --- Helpers -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\ntype SeedContext = {\n  container: ExecArgs[\"container\"]\n  query: ExecArgs[\"container\"][\"resolve\"] extends never ? never : any\n  logger: ReturnType<ExecArgs[\"container\"][\"resolve\"]>\n  link: ReturnType<ExecArgs[\"container\"][\"resolve\"]>\n}\n\nconst createContext = (container: ExecArgs[\"container\"]) => ({\n  container,\n  query: container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY),\n  link: container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LINK),\n  logger: container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LOGGER),\n})\n\nconst context = (container: ExecArgs[\"container\"]) => createContext(container)\n\ntype PlannedVariant = {\n  title: string\n  sku: string\n  options: Record<string, string>\n  quantity: number\n}\n\n/**\n * One variant per combination of option values. Option order comes from the\n * catalogue, so titles and SKUs are stable across runs.\n */\nfunction planVariants(item: CatalogueItem): PlannedVariant[] {\n  let combinations: Record<string, string>[] = [{}]\n\n  for (const option of item.options) {\n    combinations = combinations.flatMap((combination) =>\n      option.values.map((value) => ({ ...combination, [option.title]: value }))\n    )\n  }\n\n  return combinations.map((combination) => {\n    const title = Object.values(combination).join(\" / \")\n    const sku = [\n      item.sku,\n      ...Object.values(combination).map((value) =>\n        value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]+/g, \"-\")\n      ),\n    ].join(\"-\")\n\n    return {\n      title,\n      sku,\n      options: combination,\n      quantity: item.soldOut?.includes(title)\n        ? 0\n        : item.stock ?? DEFAULT_STOCK,\n    }\n  })\n}\n\n/** Every variant the catalogue describes, keyed by SKU, for the stock pass. */\nfunction planStock(): Map<string, number> {\n  const stock = new Map<string, number>()\n\n  for (const item of CATALOGUE) {\n    for (const variant of planVariants(item)) {\n      stock.set(variant.sku, variant.quantity)\n    }\n  }\n\n  return stock\n}\n\n// --- Infrastructure ----------------------------------------------------------\n\nasync function ensureSalesChannel(ctx: SeedContext) {\n  const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({\n    entity: \"sales_channel\",\n    fields: [\"id\", \"name\"],\n  })\n  const existing = data.find(\n    (channel: { name: string }) => channel.name === SALES_CHANNEL_NAME\n  )\n\n  if (existing) {\n    ctx.logger.info(`Sales channel \"${SALES_CHANNEL_NAME}\" already exists.`)\n    return existing.id as string\n  }\n\n  const {\n    result: [channel],\n  } = await createSalesChannelsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({\n    input: {\n      salesChannelsData: [\n        { name: SALES_CHANNEL_NAME, description: \"DevCart storefront\" },\n      ],\n    },\n  })\n\n  ctx.logger.info(`Created sales channel \"${SALES_CHANNEL_NAME}\".`)\n  return channel.id\n}\n\nasync function ensureStore(ctx: SeedContext, salesChannelId: string) {\n  const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({\n    entity: \"store\",\n    fields: [\"id\", \"name\", \"supported_currencies.currency_code\"],\n  })\n\n  if (data.length) {\n    return data[0] as { id: string; supported_currencies?: { currency_code?: string }[] }\n  }\n\n  const {\n    result: [store],\n  } = await createStoresWorkflow(ctx.container).run({\n    input: {\n      stores: [\n        {\n          name: STORE_NAME,\n          supported_currencies: CURRENCIES.map((currency_code) => ({\n            currency_code,\n            is_default: currency_code === DEFAULT_CURRENCY,\n          })),\n          default_sales_channel_id: salesChannelId,\n        },\n      ],\n    },\n  })\n\n  ctx.logger.info(`Created store \"${STORE_NAME}\".`)\n  return store as { id: string; supported_currencies?: { currency_code?: string }[] }\n}\n\nasync function ensurePublishableApiKey(ctx: SeedContext, salesChannelId: string) {\n  const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({\n    entity: \"api_key\",\n    fields: [\"id\", \"title\", \"type\"],\n  })\n  const existing = data.find(\n    (key: { type: string }) => key.type === \"publishable\"\n  )\n\n  if (existing) {\n    ctx.logger.info(`Publishable API key \"${existing.title}\" already exists.`)\n    return\n  }\n\n  const {\n    result: [key],\n  } = await createApiKeysWorkflow(ctx.container).run({\n    input: {\n      api_keys: [\n        {\n          title: \"DevCart Storefront\",\n          type: \"publishable\",\n          created_by: \"\",\n        },\n      ],\n    },\n  })\n\n  await linkSalesChannelsToApiKeyWorkflow(ctx.container).run({\n    input: { id: key.id, add: [salesChannelId] },\n  })\n\n  ctx.logger.info(\n    \"Created a publishable API key. Copy its token from Admin → Settings → API keys into NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDUSA_PUBLISHABLE_KEY.\"\n  )\n}\n\nasync function ensureRegion(ctx: SeedContext) {\n  const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({\n    entity: \"region\",\n    fields: [\"id\", \"name\"],\n  })\n\n  if (data.some((region: { name: string }) => region.name === REGION_NAME)) {\n    ctx.logger.info(`Region \"${REGION_NAME}\" already exists.`)\n    return\n  }\n\n  await createRegionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({\n    input: {\n      regions: [\n        {\n          name: REGION_NAME,\n          currency_code: DEFAULT_CURRENCY,\n          countries: COUNTRIES,\n          payment_providers: [\"pp_system_default\"],\n        },\n      ],\n    },\n  })\n\n  ctx.logger.info(`Created region \"${REGION_NAME}\".`)\n}\n\nasync function ensureTaxRegions(ctx: SeedContext) {\n  const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({\n    entity: \"tax_region\",\n    fields: [\"id\", \"country_code\"],\n  })\n  const missing = COUNTRIES.filter(\n    (country) =>\n      !data.some(\n        (region: { country_code: string }) => region.country_code === country\n      )\n  )\n\n  if (!missing.length) {\n    ctx.logger.info(\"Tax regions already exist.\")\n    return\n  }\n\n  await createTaxRegionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({\n    input: missing.map((country_code) => ({\n      country_code,\n      provider_id: \"tp_system\",\n    })),\n  })\n\n  ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missing.length} tax region(s).`)\n}\n\nasync function ensureStockLocation(ctx: SeedContext) {\n  const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({\n    entity: \"stock_location\",\n    fields: [\"id\", \"name\", \"fulfillment_providers.id\"],\n  })\n  const existing = data.find(\n    (location: { name: string }) => location.name === STOCK_LOCATION_NAME\n  )\n\n  if (existing) {\n    const linked = (existing.fulfillment_providers ?? []).some(\n      (provider: { id: string }) => provider.id === FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID\n    )\n\n    if (!linked) {\n      await ctx.link.create({\n        [Modules.STOCK_LOCATION]: { stock_location_id: existing.id },\n        [Modules.FULFILLMENT]: {\n          fulfillment_provider_id: FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID,\n        },\n      })\n    }\n\n    return existing.id as string\n  }\n\n  const {\n    result: [location],\n  } = await createStockLocationsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({\n    input: {\n      locations: [\n        {\n          name: STOCK_LOCATION_NAME,\n          address: { city: \"Copenhagen\", country_code: \"DK\", address_1: \"\" },\n        },\n      ],\n    },\n  })\n\n  await ctx.link.create({\n    [Modules.STOCK_LOCATION]: { stock_location_id: location.id },\n    [Modules.FULFILLMENT]: { fulfillment_provider_id: FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID },\n  })\n\n  ctx.logger.info(`Created stock location \"${STOCK_LOCATION_NAME}\".`)\n  return location.id\n}\n\nasync function ensureFulfillmentSet(ctx: SeedContext, stockLocationId: string) {\n  const [fulfillmentSet] = (\n    await ctx.container\n      .resolve(Modules.FULFILLMENT)\n      .listFulfillmentSets({ name: FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME })\n  ).filter(() => true)\n\n  let serviceZoneId: string\n\n  if (fulfillmentSet) {\n    serviceZoneId = fulfillmentSet.service_zones?.[0]?.id as string\n  } else {\n    const created = await ctx.container\n      .resolve(Modules.FULFILLMENT)\n      .createFulfillmentSets({\n        name: FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME,\n        type: \"shipping\",\n [])\n    .map((currency) => currency?.currency_code)\n    .filter((code): code is string => Boolean(code))\n\n  if (!currencyCodes.length) {\n    ctx.logger.warn(\"The store has no supported currencies; prices were skipped.\")\n  }\n\n  await ensurePublishableApiKey(ctx, salesChannelId)\n  await ensureRegion(ctx)\n  await ensureTaxRegions(ctx)\n\n  const stockLocationId = await ensureStockLocation(ctx)\n  const serviceZoneId = await ensureFulfillmentSet(ctx, stockLocationId)\n  const shippingProfileId = await ensureShippingProfile(ctx)\n  await ensureShippingOptions(\n    ctx,\n    serviceZoneId,\n    shippingProfileId,\n    currencyCodes\n  )\n\n  const refs = await ensureCatalogueRefs(ctx, salesChannelId, shippingProfileId)\n  const deletedProductIds = await removeLegacyProducts(ctx)\n\n  await ensureProducts(ctx, refs, currencyCodes)\n  await ensureInventoryLevels(ctx, stockLocationId)\n  await reindexSearch(ctx, deletedProductIds)\n\n  ctx.logger.info(\n    `Done. ${CATALOGUE.length} DevCart products across ${CATEGORIES.length} categories and ${COLLECTIONS.length} collections.`\n  )\n}\n"

> _Reasoning_
> Interesting — `query.graph` results ARE typed (not any), so my inline callback param annotations conflict with the actual DTO types. Better approach: drop the explicit parameter annotations and let TS infer the row types from the query result. Then `Maybe<>` nullability must be handled.
> 
> Errors:
> 1. `stockLocation = location` — type mismatch: query rows are `StockLocation` (from graph) while workflow result is `StockLocationDTO`. Fix: use a narrower local variable structure. Instead of assigning, restructure: create the location first (if missing) and then re-query; or track `stockLocationId` and a flags object.
> 
> Cleaner approach: 
> ```ts
> async function ensureStockLocation(ctx, salesChannelId) {
>   const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({ entity: "stock_location", fields: [...] })
>   let location = data.find((row) => row.name === STOCK_LOCATION_NAME)
> 
>   if (!location) {
>     const { result: [created] } = await createStockLocationsWorkflow(...).run(...)
>     ctx.logger.info(...)
>     // Re-read so the created row has the same shape as a found one.
>     const { data: created_rows } = await ctx.query.graph({ entity: "stock_location", fields: [...], filters: { id: created.id } })
>     location = created_rows[0]
>   }
> 
>   if (!location) throw ...
> ```
> Hmm, that's clunky but type-safe and simple. Alternative: work with ids and query links separately:
> 
> ```ts
> async function ensureStockLocation(ctx, salesChannelId) {
>   const { data: existing } = await ctx.query.graph({ entity:"stock_location", fields:["id","name"] })
>   let stockLocation = existing.find((row) => row.name === STOCK_LOCATION_NAME)
> 
>   if (!stockLocation) {
>     const { result: [created] } = await createStockLocationsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({...})
>     stockLocation = { id: created.id, name: created.name }  // narrowing local
>     ...
>   }
> 
>   // links
>   const { data: links } = await ctx.query.graph({ entity:"stock_location", fields:["id","fulfillment_providers.id","sales_channels.id"], filters: { id: stockLocation.id } })
>   const row = links[0]
>   if (!row) throw new MedusaError(...)
>   if (!(row.fulfillment_providers ?? []).some(p => p?.id === FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID)) { link }
>   if (!(row.sales_channels ?? []).some(c => c?.id === salesChannelId)) { link }
>   return row.id
> }
> ```
> Using a separate query for links after creation handles both cases with one code path — no union type issue. Good.
> 
> 2. Fulfillment set: same pattern. Query `fulfillment_set` from graph gives FulfillmentSet (graph type). The service returns FulfillmentSetDTO. Fix: after creating, re-query the fulfillment set by id (or list via query graph filters) and use that row's service_zones.
> 
> ```ts
> async function ensureFulfillmentSet(ctx, stockLocationId) {
>   const { data: sets } = await ctx.query.graph({ entity: "fulfillment_set", fields: ["id","name","service_zones.id"] })
>   let fulfillmentSetId = sets.find((set) => set.name === FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME)?.id
> 
>   if (!fulfillmentSetId) {
>     const created = await ctx.container.resolve(Modules.FULFILLMENT).createFulfillmentSets({...})
>     fulfillmentSetId = created.id
>     log
>   }
> 
>   const { data: setsWithZones } = await ctx.query.graph({ entity: "fulfillment_set", fields: ["id","service_zones.id"], filters: { id: fulfillmentSetId } })
>   const fulfillmentSet = setsWithZones[0]
>   if (!fulfillmentSet?.service_zones?.length) throw new MedusaError(NOT_FOUND, ...)
>   const serviceZoneId = fulfillmentSet.service_zones[0]!.id
> 
>   const { data: locations } = await ctx.query.graph({ entity: "stock_location", fields: ["id","fulfillment_sets.id"], filters: { id: stockLocationId } })
>   const location = locations[0]
>   if (!(location?.fulfillment_sets ?? []).some((set) => set?.id === fulfillmentSetId)) { link }
>   return serviceZoneId
> }
> ```
> Need `MedusaError` import — or just throw a plain Error. Use MedusaError from framework utils for consistency (import it).
> 
> 3. Callbacks with explicit param types: remove annotations and rely on inference. E.g. `data.find((row) => row.name === ...)` — the element type is query-result typed, so `.name` works. For `.some((p) => p?.id === X)` with Maybe, use `?.`.
> 
> 4. `inventory_item` filter: `items.filter((item) => !(item.location_levels ?? []).some((level) => level?.location_id === stockLocationId))` — inference should work: location_levels is Maybe<Maybe<InventoryLevel>[]>, so `?? []` gives Maybe<InventoryLevel>[] and `level?.location_id` works. Good.

      async function ensureRegion(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "region",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
        const existing = data.find(
          (region: { name: string }) => region.name === REGION_NAME
        )
      
        if (existing) {
          ctx.logger.info(`Region "${REGION_NAME}" already exists.`)
          return existing.id as string
        }
      
        const {
          result: [region],
        } = await createRegionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: {
            regions: [
              {
                name: REGION_NAME,
                currency_code: DEFAULT_CURRENCY,
                countries: COUNTRIES,
                payment_providers: ["pp_system_default"],
              },
            ],
          },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created region "${REGION_NAME}".`)
        return region.id as string
      }
      
      async function ensureTaxRegions(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "tax_region",
          fields: ["id", "country_code"],
        })
        const missing = COUNTRIES.filter(
          (country) =>
            !data.some(
              (region: { country_code: string }) => region.country_code === country
            )
        )
      
        if (!missing.length) {
          ctx.logger.info("Tax regions already exist.")
          return
        }
      
        await createTaxRegionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: missing.map((country_code) => ({
            country_code,
            provider_id: "tp_system",
          })),
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missing.length} tax region(s).`)
      }
      
      async function ensureStockLocation(ctx: SeedContext, salesChannelId: string) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "stock_location",
          fields: [
            "id",
            "name",
            "fulfillment_providers.id",
            "sales_channels.id",
          ],
        })
        const existing = data.find(
          (location: { name: string }) => location.name === STOCK_LOCATION_NAME
        )
      
        let stockLocation = existing
      
        if (!stockLocation) {
          const {
            result: [location],
          } = await createStockLocationsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: {
              locations: [
                {
                  name: STOCK_LOCATION_NAME,
                  address: { city: "Copenhagen", country_code: "DK", address_1: "" },
                },
              ],
            },
          })
      
          stockLocation = location
          ctx.logger.info(`Created stock location "${STOCK_LOCATION_NAME}".`)
        }
      
        const hasFulfillmentProvider = (stockLocation.fulfillment_providers ?? []).some(
          (provider: { id: string }) => provider.id === FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID
        )
      
        if (!hasFulfillmentProvider) {
          await ctx.link.create({
            [Modules.STOCK_LOCATION]: { stock_location_id: stockLocation.id },
            [Modules.FULFILLMENT]: {
              fulfillment_provider_id: FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID,
            },
          })
        }
      
        // A sales channel can only sell what its stock locations hold.
        const hasSalesChannel = (stockLocation.sales_channels ?? []).some(
          (channel: { id: string }) => channel.id === salesChannelId
        )
      
        if (!hasSalesChannel) {
          await linkSalesChannelsToStockLocationWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: { id: stockLocation.id, add: [salesChannelId] },
          })
        }
      
        return stockLocation.id as string
      }
      
      async function ensureFulfillmentSet(ctx: SeedContext, stockLocationId: string) {
        const { data: sets } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "fulfillment_set",
          fields: ["id", "name", "service_zones.id"],
        })
        let fulfillmentSet = sets.find(
          (set: { name: string }) => set.name === FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME
        )
      
        if (!fulfillmentSet) {
          fulfillmentSet = await ctx.container
            .resolve(Modules.FULFILLMENT)
            .createFulfillmentSets({
              name: FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME,
              type: "shipping",
              service_zones: [
                {
                  name: REGION_NAME,
                  geo_zones: COUNTRIES.map((country_code) => ({
                    country_code,
                    type: "country" as const,
                  })),
                },
              ],
            })
      
          ctx.logger.info(`Created fulfillment set "${FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME}".`)
        }
      
        const { data: locations } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "stock_location",
          fields: ["id", "fulfillment_sets.id"],
        })
        const location = locations.find(
          (row: { id: string }) => row.id === stockLocationId
        )
        const alreadyLinked = (location?.fulfillment_sets ?? []).some(
          (set: { id: string }) => set.id === fulfillmentSet.id
        )
      
        if (!alreadyLinked) {
          await ctx.link.create({
            [Modules.STOCK_LOCATION]: { stock_location_id: stockLocationId },
            [Modules.FULFILLMENT]: { fulfillment_set_id: fulfillmentSet.id },
          })
        }
      
        return fulfillmentSet.service_zones[0].id as string
      }
      
      async function ensureShippingProfile(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "shipping_profile",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
      
        if (data.length) {
          return data[0].id as string
        }
      
        const {
          result: [profile],
        } = await createShippingProfilesWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: {
            data: [{ name: DEFAULT_SHIPPING_PROFILE_NAME, type: "default" }],
          },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created shipping profile "${DEFAULT_SHIPPING_PROFILE_NAME}".`)
        return profile.id
      }
      
      async function ensureShippingOptions(
        ctx: SeedContext,
        serviceZoneId: string,
        shippingProfileId: string,
        currencyCodes: string[],
        regionId: string
      ) {

  content: |
      import {
        createInstantSearchAdapter,
        type MedusaSdkLike,
      } from "@medusajs/instantsearch-adapter"
      
      import { sdk } from "@lib/config"
      
      export const PRODUCT_INDEX_NAME = "product"
      
      /**
       * The currencies the product index holds prices in, one field set each. Keep
       * in sync with `PRICE_CURRENCIES` in the backend's `src/search/product.ts`.
       */
      export const SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES = ["eur", "usd"]
      
      export type PriceField =
        | "min_price"
        | "max_price"
        | "original_price"
        | "on_sale"
      
      /**
       * The indexed currency to read prices in for a region. A region whose currency
       * the index doesn't hold falls back to the first one, so the listing still
       * shows a price rather than none.
       */
      export const indexedCurrency = (currencyCode: string) => {
        const code = currencyCode.toLowerCase()
        return SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES.includes(code)
          ? code
          : SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES[0]
      }
      
      export const priceAttribute = (field: PriceField, currencyCode: string) =>
        `${field}_${indexedCurrency(currencyCode)}`
      
      /**
       * Shared by the navbar search drawer and the store listing. An empty query
       * searches rather than short-circuiting, which is what the listing needs to
       * show every product before anything is refined.
       */
      export const { searchClient } = createInstantSearchAdapter({
        sdk: sdk as unknown as MedusaSdkLike,
        path: "/store/search",
        additionalSearchParameters: {
          search_options: {
            match_strategy: "last",
          },
        },
        // Range widgets read `facets_stats`, which the adapter only produces for
        // fields listed here. The price fields are declared with a `stats` facet on
        // the index, which is what makes the stats available at all.
        numericAttributes: SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES.flatMap((currency) => [
          `min_price_${currency}`,
          `max_price_${currency}`,
        ]),
      })
      
  referencedBy: {}

 * A query run against one of the store's search indexes by `POST /store/search`.

 * `context` shapes a hydration the endpoint never runs, and `provider_options`

};
/**
 * The body of `POST /store/search`: a batch of queries, or a single one. A batch
 * runs in one round-trip to the search engine.
 */
export type StoreSearch = {
    queries: StoreSearchQuery[];
} | StoreSearchQuery;

      The storefront will not build without a publishable key — it fails the env check with a clear

      ## 7. Start the storefront
      
      ```bash
      pnpm run storefront:dev
      ```
      
      - Storefront: <http://localhost:8000> (redirects to `/{country}`, e.g. `/dk`)
      - Design system reference: <http://localhost:8000/dk/design>
      
      Or run both apps together from the root:
      
      ```bash
      pnpm run dev
      ```
      
      ## 8. Seed data
      
      The database needs a store, region, shipping options and a publishable key before the storefront can
      show anything. Two scripts exist today:
      
      ```bash
      cd apps/backend
      pnpm exec medusa exec ./src/migration-scripts/initial-data-seed.ts
      pnpm exec medusa exec ./src/scripts/seed-demo-products.ts
      ```
      
      > **Run `initial-data-seed.ts` once, on an empty database.** It creates a store, region and
      > publishable key unconditionally, so a second run duplicates them. `seed-demo-products.ts` is safe
      > to re-run: it skips products whose handles already exist.
      
      Phase 1 replaces both with one re-runnable `src/scripts/seed.ts` and a `pnpm run backend:seed`
      command. See `ROADMAP.md`.
      
      ## Verification checklist
      
      With both apps running:
      
      1. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:9000/health` prints `200`.
      2. <http://localhost:9000/app> loads the admin dashboard and the login succeeds.
      3. <http://localhost:8000> loads the storefront, with the store name in the navigation and browser tab.
      4. <http://localhost:8000/dk/design> renders the design system reference.
      5. The admin dashboard lists products under Products.
      
      ## Quality checks
      
      ```bash
      pnpm run lint        # both apps
      pnpm run typecheck   # both apps
      pnpm run build       # both apps
      ```
      
      These are the same commands CI runs. A storefront build without a reachable backend logs a
      `fetch failed` warning while generating product paths and still succeeds — the affected pages render
      on demand instead.

      /**
       * DevCart demo seed.
       *
       * Brings a Medusa instance from empty to a browsable store: store currencies,
       * a region with tax regions, a sales channel with a publishable key, a
       * warehouse with a fulfillment set and shipping options, then the DevCart
       * catalogue itself (categories, collections, tags, options and 23 products
       * with variants, prices and stock).
       *
       *   pnpm run backend:seed                  # from the repository root
       *   npx medusa exec ./src/scripts/seed.ts  # from apps/backend
       *
       * Re-runnable. Every step looks for what it is about to create first, so
       * running it twice leaves the same data behind. Products are matched by handle,
       * and every handle is fixed in the catalogue below, so new products can be
       * added to the catalogue later and a re-run will create only those.
       *
       * It also deletes the placeholder products the Medusa starter seeds
       * (`LEGACY_HANDLES`), which still carry starter branding. That deletion is
       * skipped when the store already has orders, so order history is never
       * affected.
       */

        createApiKeysWorkflow,
        createCollectionsWorkflow,
        createInventoryLevelsWorkflow,
        createProductCategoriesWorkflow,
        createProductOptionsWorkflow,
        createProductTagsWorkflow,
        createProductsWorkflow,
        createRegionsWorkflow,

        createShippingProfilesWorkflow,
