```
      // --- Helpers -----------------------------------------------------------------
      
      const createContext = (container: ExecArgs["container"]) => ({
        container,
        query: container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY),
        link: container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LINK),
        logger: container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LOGGER),
      })
      
      type SeedContext = ReturnType<typeof createContext>
      
      type PlannedVariant = {
        title: string
        sku: string
        options: Record<string, string>
        quantity: number
      }
      
      /**
       * One variant per combination of option values. Option order comes from the
       * catalogue, so titles and SKUs are stable across runs.
       */
      function planVariants(item: CatalogueItem): PlannedVariant[] {
        let combinations: Record<string, string>[] = [{}]
      
        for (const option of item.options) {
          combinations = combinations.flatMap((combination) =>
            option.values.map((value) => ({ ...combination, [option.title]: value }))
          )
        }
      
        return combinations.map((combination) => {
          const title = Object.values(combination).join(" / ")
          const sku = [
            item.sku,
            ...Object.values(combination).map((value) =>
              value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]+/g, "-")
            ),
          ].join("-")
      
          return {
            title,
            sku,
            options: combination,
            quantity: item.soldOut?.includes(title)
              ? 0
              : item.stock ?? DEFAULT_STOCK,
          }
        })
      }
      
      /** Every variant the catalogue describes, keyed by SKU, for the stock pass. */
      function planStock(): Map<string, number> {
        const stock = new Map<string, number>()
      
        for (const item of CATALOGUE) {
          for (const variant of planVariants(item)) {
            stock.set(variant.sku, variant.quantity)
          }
        }
      
        return stock
      }
      
      // --- Infrastructure ----------------------------------------------------------
      
      async function ensureSalesChannel(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "sales_channel",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
        const existing = data.find(
          (channel: { name: string }) => channel.name === SALES_CHANNEL_NAME
        )
      
        if (existing) {
          ctx.logger.info(`Sales channel "${SALES_CHANNEL_NAME}" already exists.`)
          return existing.id as string
        }
      
        const {
          result: [channel],
        } = await createSalesChannelsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: {
            salesChannelsData: [
              { name: SALES_CHANNEL_NAME, description: "DevCart storefront" },
            ],
          },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created sales channel "${SALES_CHANNEL_NAME}".`)
        return channel.id
      }
      
      async function ensureStore(ctx: SeedContext, salesChannelId: string) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "store",
          fields: ["id", "name", "supported_currencies.currency_code"],
        })
      
        if (data.length) {
          return data[0] as { id: string; supported_currencies?: { currency_code?: string }[] }
        }
      
        const {
          result: [store],
        } = await createStoresWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: {
            stores: [
              {
                name: STORE_NAME,
                supported_currencies: CURRENCIES.map((currency_code) => ({
                  currency_code,
                  is_default: currency_code === DEFAULT_CURRENCY,
                })),
                default_sales_channel_id: salesChannelId,
              },
            ],
          },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created store "${STORE_NAME}".`)
        return store as { id: string; supported_currencies?: { currency_code?: string }[] }
      }
      
      async function ensurePublishableApiKey(ctx: SeedContext, salesChannelId: string) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "api_key",
          fields: ["id", "title", "type"],
        })
        const existing = data.find(
          (key: { type: string }) => key.type === "publishable"
        )
      
        if (existing) {
          ctx.logger.info(`Publishable API key "${existing.title}" already exists.`)
          return
        }
      
        const {
          result: [key],
        } = await createApiKeysWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: {
            api_keys: [
              {
                title: "DevCart Storefront",
                type: "publishable",
                created_by: "",
              },
            ],
          },
        })
      
        await linkSalesChannelsToApiKeyWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: { id: key.id, add: [salesChannelId] },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(
          "Created a publishable API key. Copy its token from Admin → Settings → API keys into NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDUSA_PUBLISHABLE_KEY."
        )
      }
      
      async function ensureRegion(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "region",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
        const existing = data.find(
          (region: { name: string }) => region.name === REGION_NAME
        )
      
        if (existing) {
          ctx.logger.info(`Region "${REGION_NAME}" already exists.`)
          return existing.id as string
        }
      
        const {
          result: [region],
        } = await createRegionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: {
            regions: [
              {
                name: REGION_NAME,
                currency_code: DEFAULT_CURRENCY,
                countries: COUNTRIES,
                payment_providers: ["pp_system_default"],
              },
            ],
          },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created region "${REGION_NAME}".`)
        return region.id as string
      }
      
      async function ensureTaxRegions(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "tax_region",
          fields: ["id", "country_code"],
        })
        const missing = COUNTRIES.filter(
          (country) =>
            !data.some(
              (region: { country_code: string }) => region.country_code === country
            )
        )
      
        if (!missing.length) {
          ctx.logger.info("Tax regions already exist.")
          return
        }
      
        await createTaxRegionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: missing.map((country_code) => ({
            country_code,
            provider_id: "tp_system",
          })),
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missing.length} tax region(s).`)
      }
      
      async function ensureStockLocation(ctx: SeedContext, salesChannelId: string) {
        const { data: existing } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "stock_location",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
        let stockLocationId = existing.find(
          (location) => location.name === STOCK_LOCATION_NAME
        )?.id
      
        if (!stockLocationId) {
          const {
            result: [location],
          } = await createStockLocationsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: {
              locations: [
                {
                  name: STOCK_LOCATION_NAME,
                  address: { city: "Copenhagen", country_code: "DK", address_1: "" },
                },
              ],
            },
          })
      
          stockLocationId = location.id
          ctx.logger.info(`Created stock location "${STOCK_LOCATION_NAME}".`)
        }
      
        // The links are read back from the graph, so an existing location and a newly
        // created one go through the same code.
        const { data: locations } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "stock_location",
          fields: ["id", "fulfillment_providers.id", "sales_channels.id"],
          filters: { id: stockLocationId },
        })
        const stockLocation = locations[0]
      
        if (!stockLocation) {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
            `Stock location ${stockLocationId} could not be read back.`
          )
        }
      
        const hasFulfillmentProvider = (
          stockLocation.fulfillment_providers ?? []
        ).some((provider) => provider?.id === FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID)
      
        if (!hasFulfillmentProvider) {
          await ctx.link.create({
            [Modules.STOCK_LOCATION]: { stock_location_id: stockLocation.id },
            [Modules.FULFILLMENT]: {
              fulfillment_provider_id: FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID,
            },
          })
        }
      
        // A sales channel can only sell what its stock locations hold.
        const hasSalesChannel = (stockLocation.sales_channels ?? []).some(
          (channel) => channel?.id === salesChannelId
        )
      
        if (!hasSalesChannel) {
          await linkSalesChannelsToStockLocationWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: { id: stockLocation.id, add: [salesChannelId] },
          })
        }
      
        return stockLocation.id
      }
      
      async function ensureFulfillmentSet(ctx: SeedContext, stockLocationId: string) {
        const { data: sets } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "fulfillment_set",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
        let fulfillmentSetId = sets.find(
          (set) => set.name === FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME
        )?.id
      
        if (!fulfillmentSetId) {
          const created = await ctx.container
            .resolve(Modules.FULFILLMENT)
            .createFulfillmentSets({
              name: FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME,
              type: "shipping",
              service_zones: [
                {
                  name: REGION_NAME,
                  geo_zones: COUNTRIES.map((country_code) => ({
                    country_code,
                    type: "country" as const,
                  })),
                },
              ],
            })
      
          fulfillmentSetId = created.id
          ctx.logger.info(`Created fulfillment set "${FULFILLMENT_SET_NAME}".`)
        }
      
        const { data: setsWithZones } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "fulfillment_set",
          fields: ["id", "service_zones.id"],
          filters: { id: fulfillmentSetId },
        })
        const serviceZoneId = setsWithZones[0]?.service_zones?.[0]?.id
      
        if (!serviceZoneId) {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
            `Fulfillment set ${fulfillmentSetId} has no service zone.`
          )
        }
      
        const { data: locations } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "stock_location",
          fields: ["id", "fulfillment_sets.id"],
          filters: { id: stockLocationId },
        })
        const alreadyLinked = (locations[0]?.fulfillment_sets ?? []).some(
          (set) => set?.id === fulfillmentSetId
        )
      
        if (!alreadyLinked) {
          await ctx.link.create({
            [Modules.STOCK_LOCATION]: { stock_location_id: stockLocationId },
            [Modules.FULFILLMENT]: { fulfillment_set_id: fulfillmentSetId },
          })
        }
      
        return serviceZoneId
      }
      
      async function ensureShippingProfile(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "shipping_profile",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
      
        if (data.length) {
          return data[0].id as string
        }
      
        const {
          result: [profile],
        } = await createShippingProfilesWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: {
            data: [{ name: DEFAULT_SHIPPING_PROFILE_NAME, type: "default" }],
          },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created shipping profile "${DEFAULT_SHIPPING_PROFILE_NAME}".`)
        return profile.id
      }
      
      async function ensureShippingOptions(
        ctx: SeedContext,
        serviceZoneId: string,
        shippingProfileId: string,
        currencyCodes: string[],
        regionId: string
      ) {
        const { data } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "shipping_option",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
        const missing = SHIPPING_OPTIONS.filter(
          (option) =>
            !data.some((existing: { name: string }) => existing.name === option.name)
        )
      
        if (!missing.length) {
          ctx.logger.info("Shipping options already exist.")
          return
        }
      
        await createShippingOptionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: missing.map((option) => ({
            name: option.name,
            price_type: "flat" as const,
            provider_id: FULFILLMENT_PROVIDER_ID,
            service_zone_id: serviceZoneId,
            shipping_profile_id: shippingProfileId,
            type: {
              label: option.label,
              description: option.description,
              code: option.code,
            },
            prices: [
              ...currencyCodes.map((currency_code) => ({
                currency_code,
                amount: option.amount,
              })),
              { region_id: regionId, amount: option.amount },
            ],
            rules: [
              { attribute: "enabled_in_store", value: "true", operator: "eq" as const },
              { attribute: "is_return", value: "false", operator: "eq" as const },
            ],
          })),
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missing.length} shipping option(s).`)
      }
      
      // --- Catalogue reference data ------------------------------------------------
      
      type CatalogueRefs = {
        salesChannelId: string
        shippingProfileId: string
        categories: Map<string, string>
        collections: Map<string, string>
        tags: Map<string, string>
        sharedOptions: Map<string, string>
      }
      
      async function ensureCatalogueRefs(
        ctx: SeedContext,
        salesChannelId: string,
        shippingProfileId: string
      ): Promise<CatalogueRefs> {
        const { data: categories } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_category",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
        const missingCategories = CATEGORIES.filter(
          (category) =>
            !categories.some(
              (existing: { name: string }) => existing.name === category.name
            )
        )
      
        if (missingCategories.length) {
          await createProductCategoriesWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: {
              product_categories: missingCategories.map((category) => ({
                name: category.name,
                handle: category.handle,
                is_active: true,
              })),
            },
          })
          ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missingCategories.length} category(ies).`)
        }
      
        const { data: collections } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_collection",
          fields: ["id", "title"],
        })
        const missingCollections = COLLECTIONS.filter(
          (collection) =>
            !collections.some(
              (existing: { title: string }) => existing.title === collection.title
            )
        )
      
        if (missingCollections.length) {
          await createCollectionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: { collections: missingCollections },
          })
          ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missingCollections.length} collection(s).`)
        }
      
        const { data: tags } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_tag",
          fields: ["id", "value"],
        })
        const missingTags = TAGS.filter(
          (tag) => !tags.some((existing: { value: string }) => existing.value === tag)
        )
      
        if (missingTags.length) {
          await createProductTagsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: { product_tags: missingTags.map((value) => ({ value })) },
          })
          ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missingTags.length} tag(s).`)
        }
      
        const { data: options } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_option",
          fields: ["id", "title", "is_exclusive"],
          filters: { is_exclusive: false },
        })
        const missingOptions = SHARED_OPTIONS.filter(
          (option) =>
            !options.some((existing: { title: string }) => existing.title === option.title)
        )
      
        if (missingOptions.length) {
          await createProductOptionsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: {
              product_options: missingOptions.map((option) => ({
                ...option,
                is_exclusive: false,
              })),
            },
          })
          ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missingOptions.length} shared option(s).`)
        }
      
        const { data: allCategories } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_category",
          fields: ["id", "name"],
        })
        const { data: allCollections } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_collection",
          fields: ["id", "title"],
        })
        const { data: allTags } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_tag",
          fields: ["id", "value"],
        })
        const { data: allOptions } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_option",
          fields: ["id", "title"],
          filters: { is_exclusive: false },
        })
      
        return {
          salesChannelId,
          shippingProfileId,
          categories: new Map<string, string>(
            allCategories.map(
              (row: { name: string; id: string }) => [row.name, row.id] as [string, string]
            )
          ),
          collections: new Map<string, string>(
            allCollections.map(
              (row: { title: string; id: string }) =>
                [row.title, row.id] as [string, string]
            )
          ),
          tags: new Map<string, string>(
            allTags.map(
              (row: { value: string; id: string }) => [row.value, row.id] as [string, string]
            )
          ),
          sharedOptions: new Map<string, string>(
            allOptions.map(
              (row: { title: string; id: string }) =>
                [row.title, row.id] as [string, string]
            )
          ),
        }
      }
      
      /**
       * Deletes the starter's placeholder products. Skipped when the store has any
       * order, because order history should never be touched by a seed script.
       */
      async function removeLegacyProducts(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data: orders } = await ctx.query.graph({ entity: "order", fields: ["id"] })
      
        if (orders.length) {
          ctx.logger.warn(
            "The store has orders, so the starter placeholder products were left alone. Remove them from the admin if you no longer want them."
          )
          return []
        }
      
        const { data: products } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product",
          fields: ["id", "handle", "title", "deleted_at"],
        })
        const legacy = products.filter(
          (product) =>
            !product.deleted_at &&
            LEGACY_HANDLES.includes(product.handle ?? "") &&
            (product.title ?? "").startsWith("Medusa ")
        )
      
        if (!legacy.length) {
          return []
        }
      
        await deleteProductsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: { ids: legacy.map((product) => product.id) },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(
          `Deleted ${legacy.length} starter placeholder product(s): ${legacy
            .map((product) => product.handle)
            .join(", ")}.`
        )
      
        return legacy.map((product) => product.id)
      }
      
      /**
       * The starter's own categories, which the catalogue does not use. Only removed
       * once no live product points at them, so nothing is left dangling.
       */
      async function removeLegacyCategories(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const { data: categories } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product_category",
          fields: ["id", "handle", "deleted_at", "products.id", "products.deleted_at"],
        })
        const legacy = categories.filter(
          (category) =>
            !category.deleted_at &&
            LEGACY_CATEGORY_HANDLES.includes(category.handle ?? "") &&
            !(category.products ?? []).some((product) => !product?.deleted_at)
        )
      
        if (!legacy.length) {
          return
        }
      
        await deleteProductCategoriesWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: legacy.map((category) => category.id),
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(
          `Deleted ${legacy.length} starter category(ies): ${legacy
            .map((category) => category.handle)
            .join(", ")}.`
        )
      }
      
      async function ensureProducts(
        ctx: SeedContext,
        refs: CatalogueRefs,
        currencyCodes: string[]
      ) {
        const { data: existing } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product",
          fields: ["id", "handle"],
        })
        const taken = new Set(
          existing.map((product: { handle: string }) => product.handle)
        )
        const missing = CATALOGUE.filter((item) => !taken.has(item.handle))
      
        if (!missing.length) {
          ctx.logger.info("Every catalogue product already exists.")
          return
        }
      
        const products: CreateProductDTO[] = missing.map((item) => ({
          title: item.title,
          subtitle: item.subtitle,
          description: item.description,
          handle: item.handle,
          status: ProductStatus.PUBLISHED,
          thumbnail: item.images[0],
          images: item.images.map((url) => ({ url })),
          weight: item.weight,
          shipping_profile_id: refs.shippingProfileId,
          collection_id: item.collections
            .map((title) => refs.collections.get(title))
            .find((id): id is string => Boolean(id)),
          category_ids: [refs.categories.get(item.category)].filter(
            (id): id is string => Boolean(id)
          ),
          tag_ids: item.tags
            .map((tag) => refs.tags.get(tag))
            .filter((id): id is string => Boolean(id)),
          sales_channels: [{ id: refs.salesChannelId }],
          // A shared option is linked by id so the storefront's option filter keeps
          // working; anything else is created for this product alone.
          options: item.options.map((option) => {
            const sharedId = refs.sharedOptions.get(option.title)
      
            return sharedId
              ? { id: sharedId }
              : { title: option.title, values: option.values, is_exclusive: true }
          }),
          variants: planVariants(item).map((variant) => ({
            title: variant.title,
            sku: variant.sku,
            options: variant.options,
            prices: currencyCodes.map((currency_code) => ({
              currency_code,
              amount: item.price[currency_code],
            })),
          })),
        }))
      
        // Batched so one bad product cannot roll the whole catalogue back.
        const BATCH_SIZE = 8
      
        for (let start = 0; start < products.length; start += BATCH_SIZE) {
          await createProductsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
            input: { products: products.slice(start, start + BATCH_SIZE) },
          })
          ctx.logger.info(
            `Created ${Math.min(start + BATCH_SIZE, products.length)}/${products.length} product(s).`
          )
        }
      }
      
      async function ensureInventoryLevels(
        ctx: SeedContext,
        stockLocationId: string
      ) {
        const { data: items } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "inventory_item",
          fields: ["id", "sku", "location_levels.location_id"],
        })
        const stock = planStock()
        const missing = items.filter(
          (item) =>
            !(item.location_levels ?? []).some(
              (level) => level?.location_id === stockLocationId
            )
        )
      
        if (!missing.length) {
          ctx.logger.info("Inventory levels already exist for every variant.")
          return
        }
      
        await createInventoryLevelsWorkflow(ctx.container).run({
          input: {
            inventory_levels: missing.map(
              (item: { id: string; sku?: string | null }) => ({
                location_id: stockLocationId,
                inventory_item_id: item.id,
                stocked_quantity: stock.get(item.sku ?? "") ?? DEFAULT_STOCK,
              })
            ),
          },
        })
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Created ${missing.length} inventory level(s).`)
      }
      
      /**
       * `product.created` is emitted on the local event bus and handled
       * asynchronously, so a short-lived `medusa exec` process can exit before the
       * catalogue reaches the search index — which is what the store page reads.
       * Replaying the events here is awaited, and ingestion upserts, so it is safe to
       * run over everything.
       */
      async function reindexSearch(ctx: SeedContext, deletedProductIds: string[]) {
        const search = ctx.container.resolve(Modules.SEARCH)
        const INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE = 25
      
        if (deletedProductIds.length) {
          await search.ingest({
            name: "product.deleted",
            data: deletedProductIds.map((id) => ({ id })),
          })
        }
      
        const { data: products } = await ctx.query.graph({
          entity: "product",
          fields: ["id"],
        })
      
        for (let start = 0; start < products.length; start += INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE) {
          const chunk = products.slice(start, start + INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE)
      
          await search.ingest({
            name: "product.created",
            data: chunk.map((product: { id: string }) => ({ id: product.id })),
          })
        }
      
        ctx.logger.info(`Reindexed ${products.length} product(s) for search.`)
      }
      
      // --- Entry point -------------------------------------------------------------
      
      export default async function seed({ container }: ExecArgs) {
        const ctx = createContext(container)
      
        ctx.logger.info("Seeding DevCart demo data...")
      
        const salesChannelId = await ensureSalesChannel(ctx)
        const store = await ensureStore(ctx, salesChannelId)
        const currencyCodes = (store.supported_currencies ?? [])
          .map((currency) => currency?.currency_code)
          .filter((code): code is string => Boolean(code))
      
        if (!currencyCodes.length) {
          ctx.logger.warn("The store has no supported currencies; prices were skipped.")
        }
      
        await ensurePublishableApiKey(ctx, salesChannelId)
        const regionId = await ensureRegion(ctx)
        await ensureTaxRegions(ctx)
      
        const stockLocationId = await ensureStockLocation(ctx, salesChannelId)
        const serviceZoneId = await ensureFulfillmentSet(ctx, stockLocationId)
        const shippingProfileId = await ensureShippingProfile(ctx)
        await ensureShippingOptions(
          ctx,
          serviceZoneId,
          shippingProfileId,
          currencyCodes,
          regionId
        )
      
        const refs = await ensureCatalogueRefs(ctx, salesChannelId, shippingProfileId)
        const deletedProductIds = await removeLegacyProducts(ctx)
        await removeLegacyCategories(ctx)
      
        await ensureProducts(ctx, refs, currencyCodes)
        await ensureInventoryLevels(ctx, stockLocationId)
        await reindexSearch(ctx, deletedProductIds)
      
        ctx.logger.info(
          `Done. ${CATALOGUE.length} DevCart products across ${CATEGORIES.length} categories and ${COLLECTIONS.length} collections.`
        )
      }
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: apps/backend/src/scripts/seed-demo-products.ts
  content: |
      /**
       * Demo data only — creates 50 published products so the store page's
       * pagination and option facets have something to work with. Safe to delete
       * along with the products it creates; nothing in the app depends on it.
       *
       *   npx medusa exec ./src/scripts/seed-demo-products.ts
       *
       * Re-running it is a no-op for anything it already created: every product uses
       * a deterministic handle, and existing handles are skipped.
       */
      import {
        createCollectionsWorkflow,
        createProductOptionsWorkflow,
        createProductTagsWorkflow,
        createProductsWorkflow,
      } from '@medusajs/medusa/core-flows'
      import {
        ContainerRegistrationKeys,
        MedusaError,
        Modules,
        ProductStatus,
      } from '@medusajs/framework/utils'
      import type { ExecArgs } from '@medusajs/framework/types'
      
      const PRODUCT_COUNT = 50
      const HANDLE_PREFIX = 'demo'
      /** Products are created in batches so one failure doesn't roll back all 50. */
      const BATCH_SIZE = 10
      /** Caps the variant count per product, since options multiply. */
      const MAX_VARIANTS = 12
      /** Products per awaited search-ingestion call. */
      const INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE = 25
      
      /**
       * Deterministic PRNG (mulberry32). Keeps re-runs identical, so the same handle
       * always describes the same product.
       */
      function makeRandom(seed: number) {
        let state = seed
      
        return () => {
          state = (state + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0
          let t = Math.imul(state ^ (state >>> 15), 1 | state)
          t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t
          return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
        }
      }
      
      const ADJECTIVES = [
        'Vintage', 'Classic', 'Relaxed', 'Tailored', 'Oversized',
        'Everyday', 'Heritage', 'Essential', 'Cropped', 'Lightweight',
      ]
      const MATERIALS = ['Cotton', 'Linen', 'Merino', 'Denim', 'Fleece', 'Twill']
      const TYPES = [
        'Tee', 'Hoodie', 'Sweatshirt', 'Shorts', 'Joggers',
        'Overshirt', 'Cap', 'Socks', 'Tote', 'Beanie',
      ]
      
      const COLLECTIONS = ['Summer Essentials', 'Winter Layers', 'Everyday Basics', 'Limited Run']
      const TAGS = ['sale', 'new-arrival', 'organic', 'unisex', 'bestseller', 'last-chance']
      
      /**
       * Extra shared options, so the store page's option facet shows more than the
       * Size and Color the initial seed creates.
       */
      const EXTRA_OPTIONS = [
        { title: 'Material', values: ['Cotton', 'Linen', 'Merino', 'Fleece'] },
        { title: 'Fit', values: ['Regular', 'Slim', 'Relaxed'] },
        { title: 'Sleeve', values: ['Short', 'Long'] },
      ]
      
      /** Real Medusa demo images, so the grid isn't full of placeholders. */
      const IMAGES = [
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/tee-black-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/tee-white-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/sweatshirt-vintage-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/sweatpants-gray-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/shorts-vintage-front.png',
        'https://medusa-public-images.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/coffee-mug.png',
      ]
      
      type SharedOption = { id: string; title: string; values: string[] }
      
      export default async function seedDemoProducts({ container }: ExecArgs) {
        const logger = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LOGGER)
        const query = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY)
        const random = makeRandom(20260831)
      
        const pick = <T>(items: T[]): T => items[Math.floor(random() * items.length)]
        const pickSome = <T>(items: T[], max: number): T[] => {
          const count = Math.floor(random() * (max + 1))
          return [...items].sort(() => random() - 0.5).slice(0, count)
        }
      
        // ---- Prerequisites that already exist in the project ----------------------
      
        const { data: salesChannels } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'sales_channel',
          fields: ['id', 'name'],
        })
        const { data: shippingProfiles } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'shipping_profile',
          fields: ['id'],
        })
        const { data: categories } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_category',
          fields: ['id', 'name'],
        })
        const { data: stores } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'store',
          fields: ['id', 'supported_currencies.currency_code'],
        })
      
        const salesChannel = salesChannels[0]
        const shippingProfile = shippingProfiles[0]
      
        if (!salesChannel || !shippingProfile) {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
            'No sales channel or shipping profile found. Run the initial data seed first.'
          )
        }
      
        const currencyCodes: string[] = (
          stores[0]?.supported_currencies ?? []
        )
          .map((currency) => currency?.currency_code)
          .filter((code): code is string => Boolean(code))
      
        if (!currencyCodes.length) {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
            'The store has no supported currencies.'
          )
        }
      
        logger.info(
          `Seeding into "${salesChannel.name}" with currencies: ${currencyCodes.join(', ')}`
        )
      
        // ---- Collections, tags and extra options --------------------------------
      
        const { data: existingCollections } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_collection',
          fields: ['id', 'title'],
        })
        const missingCollections = COLLECTIONS.filter(
          (title) => !existingCollections.some((collection) => collection.title === title)
        )
      
        if (missingCollections.length) {
          await createCollectionsWorkflow(container).run({
            input: { collections: missingCollections.map((title) => ({ title })) },
          })
          logger.info(`Created ${missingCollections.length} collection(s)`)
        }
      
        const { data: allCollections } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_collection',
          fields: ['id', 'title'],
        })
      
        const { data: existingTags } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_tag',
          fields: ['id', 'value'],
        })
        const missingTags = TAGS.filter(
          (value) => !existingTags.some((tag) => tag.value === value)
        )
      
        if (missingTags.length) {
          await createProductTagsWorkflow(container).run({
            input: { product_tags: missingTags.map((value) => ({ value })) },
          })
          logger.info(`Created ${missingTags.length} tag(s)`)
        }
      
        const { data: allTags } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_tag',
          fields: ['id', 'value'],
        })
      
        // Shared (non-exclusive) options, the way the initial seed defines them.
        const { data: existingOptions } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_option',
          fields: ['id', 'title', 'values.value'],
          filters: { is_exclusive: false },
        })
      
        const missingOptions = EXTRA_OPTIONS.filter(
          (option) => !existingOptions.some((existing) => existing.title === option.title)
        )
      
        if (missingOptions.length) {
          await createProductOptionsWorkflow(container).run({
            input: { product_options: missingOptions },
          })
          logger.info(`Created ${missingOptions.length} shared option(s)`)
        }
      
        const { data: optionRows } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product_option',
          fields: ['id', 'title', 'values.value'],
          filters: { is_exclusive: false },
        })
      
        const sharedOptions: SharedOption[] = optionRows
          .map((option) => ({
            id: option.id as string,
            title: option.title as string,
            values: (option.values ?? [])
              .map((value) => value?.value)
              .filter((value): value is string => Boolean(value)),
          }))
          .filter((option) => option.values.length > 0)
      
        const sizeOption = sharedOptions.find((option) => option.title === 'Size')
      
        if (!sizeOption) {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
            'No shared "Size" option found. Run the initial data seed first.'
          )
        }
      
        // ---- Build the products -------------------------------------------------
      
        const { data: alreadySeeded } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product',
          fields: ['handle'],
        })
        const takenHandles = new Set(
          alreadySeeded.map((product) => product.handle).filter(Boolean)
        )
      
        const products: Record<string, unknown>[] = []
      
        for (let index = 0; index < PRODUCT_COUNT; index++) {
          // Derived from the index, never from the PRNG. Skipping a product consumes
          // fewer random numbers than building one, so a handle that depended on the
          // PRNG would shift after the first skip and the script would create
          // duplicates instead of recognising its own products.
          const type = TYPES[index % TYPES.length]
          const handle = `${HANDLE_PREFIX}-${index + 1}-${type.toLowerCase()}`
      
          if (takenHandles.has(handle)) {
            continue
          }
      
          const title = `${pick(ADJECTIVES)} ${pick(MATERIALS)} ${type}`
      
          // Size is always present; the rest vary so the facet has uneven counts.
          const chosenOptions = [
            sizeOption,
            ...pickSome(
              sharedOptions.filter((option) => option.title !== 'Size'),
              2
            ),
          ]
      
          // Cartesian product of the chosen options' values, capped.
          let combinations: Record<string, string>[] = [{}]
      
          for (const option of chosenOptions) {
            const next: Record<string, string>[] = []
      
            for (const combination of combinations) {
              for (const value of option.values) {
                if (next.length >= MAX_VARIANTS) {
                  break
                }
                next.push({ ...combination, [option.title]: value })
              }
            }
      
            combinations = next
          }
      
          const collection = pick(allCollections)
          const chosenTags = pickSome(allTags, 3)
          const chosenCategories = pickSome(categories, 2)
          const thumbnail = pick(IMAGES)
          const basePrice = 10 + Math.floor(random() * 90)
      
          products.push({
            title,
            handle,
            subtitle: `${type} — demo data`,
            description: `A ${title.toLowerCase()} generated to fill out the demo catalogue. Not a real product.`,
            status: ProductStatus.PUBLISHED,
            thumbnail,
            images: [{ url: thumbnail }],
            weight: 300 + Math.floor(random() * 500),
            shipping_profile_id: shippingProfile.id,
            collection_id: collection?.id,
            tag_ids: chosenTags.map((tag) => tag.id as string),
            category_ids: chosenCategories.map((category) => category.id as string),
            sales_channels: [{ id: salesChannel.id }],
            options: chosenOptions.map((option) => ({ id: option.id })),
            variants: combinations.map((combination) => ({
              title: Object.values(combination).join(' / '),
              sku: `${handle.toUpperCase()}-${Object.values(combination).join('-').toUpperCase()}`,
              options: combination,
              prices: currencyCodes.map((currency_code) => ({
                amount: basePrice,
                currency_code,
              })),
            })),
          })
        }
      
        if (!products.length) {
          logger.info('Every demo product already exists. Nothing to do.')
          return
        }
      
        // ---- Create them --------------------------------------------------------
      
        let created = 0
      
        for (let start = 0; start < products.length; start += BATCH_SIZE) {
          const batch = products.slice(start, start + BATCH_SIZE)
      
          await createProductsWorkflow(container).run({
            input: { products: batch as never },
          })
      
          created += batch.length
          logger.info(`Created ${created}/${products.length} demo products`)
        }
      
        // ---- Make sure the search index caught up -------------------------------
      
        // `product.created` is emitted on the local event bus and handled
        // asynchronously, so a short-lived `medusa exec` process can exit before the
        // last batch is ingested. Replaying the ingestion here is awaited, and
        // `consume` upserts, so it is safe to run over every product.
        const search = container.resolve(Modules.SEARCH)
        const { data: allProducts } = await query.graph({
          entity: 'product',
          fields: ['id'],
        })
      
        for (let start = 0; start < allProducts.length; start += INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE) {
          const chunk = allProducts.slice(start, start + INGEST_CHUNK_SIZE)
      
          await search.ingest({
            name: 'product.created',
            data: chunk.map((product) => ({ id: product.id })),
          } as never)
        }
      
        logger.info(`Search index caught up for ${allProducts.length} product(s).`)
        logger.info('Done. Open the store page to see the new products.')
      }
```

````
  content: |
      Or run both apps together from the root:
      
      ```bash
      pnpm run dev
      ```
      
      ## 8. Seed data
      
      The database needs its Medusa migrations applied before it can be seeded. On a fresh database,
      `pnpm run dev` runs `medusa develop`, which applies migrations during startup. If preparing the
      catalogue before starting the backend, run `pnpm exec medusa db:migrate` from `apps/backend` first.
      Then seed from the repository root:
      
      ```bash
      pnpm run backend:seed            # from the repository root
      # or, from apps/backend:
      pnpm run seed                    # = medusa exec ./src/scripts/seed.ts
      ```
      
      It creates a store with EUR/USD, the Europe region and its tax regions, a sales channel with a
      publishable key, a warehouse with a fulfillment set and two shipping options, then the DevCart
      catalogue: 5 categories, 3 collections, 5 tags, a shared Size and Color option, and 23 products with
      variants, prices and stock.
      
      - **Re-runnable.** Every step looks for what it is about to create first, so a second run adds
        nothing. Add a product to `CATALOGUE` in `src/scripts/seed.ts` and a re-run creates only that one.
      - **It replaces the starter's placeholder products.** The four products `initial-data-seed.ts`
        creates are deleted, along with their now-empty categories. That deletion is skipped automatically
        if the store has any order, so order history is never touched.
      - **The turbo task is not cached** (`turbo.json` sets `"cache": false` for `seed`). Caching would
        turn a second `pnpm run backend:seed` into a replay of the first run's log with no database work.
      - `src/scripts/seed-demo-products.ts` still exists as an optional bulk filler (50 generated products)
        for exercising pagination. It is not needed for the DevCart catalogue.
      
      After seeding, the admin dashboard at <http://localhost:9000/app> lists the products, and
      <http://localhost:8000/dk/store> lists them in the storefront.
      
      ## Verification checklist
      
      With both apps running:
      
      1. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:9000/health` prints `200`.

      # DevCart — Roadmap tracker
      
      `docs/PROJECT_SPEC.md` is the ground truth for what to build and in what order. This file only tracks
      progress against it: what is done, what is in flight, what is left. If this file and the spec disagree,
      the spec wins.
      
      Legend: `[x]` done and verified · `[~]` in progress / partially done · `[ ]` not started · `[!]` blocked
      
      Last updated: P1.0 done and verified (re-runnable seed with the DevCart catalogue). Phase 1 continues
      with C1–C5.
      
      ---
      
      ## Phase 0 — Foundation
      
      Exit criteria: fresh clone + `docs/SETUP.md` → both apps run; CI green.
      
      - [x] **P0.1** Inspect starter; report on structure, versions, integrations, gaps. Design plan in `docs/DESIGN.md`.
      - [x] **P0.2** Document exact local commands in `docs/SETUP.md`.
      - [x] **P0.3** `docker-compose.yml` (Postgres, Redis; Meilisearch behind an opt-in profile).
      - [x] **P0.4** `.env.template` files updated; `.gitignore` covers secrets.
      - [x] **P0.5** Starter branding removed; store name/metadata from env.
      - [x] **P0.6** CI skeleton: install, lint, typecheck, build for both apps.
      
      **Phase 0 exit criteria met:** both apps run locally from the documented commands, and lint,
      typecheck and build all pass for both apps from the repository root (the same commands CI runs).
      
      ## Phase 1 — Core Store MVP
      
      Tasks: seed data (§5.6) → C1–C5 → K1–K5 → A1–A2 → responsive + states pass.
      
      - [x] **P1.0** `src/scripts/seed.ts`: DevCart catalogue (23 products, 5 categories, 3 collections), re-runnable (§5.6). Run with `pnpm run backend:seed`. Verified against a live database: first run creates everything, second run is a no-op, storefront and admin both show the catalogue.
      - [ ] **C1** Homepage — hero, featured products, category links, collection section.
      - [ ] **C2** Product listing — grid, image/title/price, loading + empty states.
      - [ ] **C3** Category & collection pages — resolve by handle, 404 for unknown handle.
      - [ ] **C4** Product detail — gallery, variant selectors, per-variant price, stock state.
      - [ ] **C5** Sort & filter — newest/price, category, price range, reflected in URL.
      - [ ] **K1** Cart — add/remove/quantity, persists across reload, stock errors handled.
````

> _Reasoning_
> **Addressing event-driven ingestion**
> 
> I need to mention that the event-driven ingestion emits expected errors before the index is initialized, and a manual reindexing happens afterward. If the seed is supposed to avoid console errors, it’s not meeting that goal, especially if we consider backend console errors. Instead of suppressing event errors silently, I should ensure the search index is active before products are created. Running a search reindex first will help bootstrap an empty index, allowing the product creation to trigger events properly.**Optimizing indexing process**
> 
> I could reindex before creating products to avoid event bus errors, especially if there are no initial products, which would set the active index to zero. I need to ensure the index is bootstrapped before deleting legacy products and their categories. It’s crucial to reindex before removing those old products, which will prevent errors. After deleting the products, I should reindex again to finalize things. It’s a solid plan to call `reindexSearch(ctx)` before and after deletion to log placeholders and ensure everything is properly indexed.**Evaluating search index readiness**
> 
> I’m focusing on the current database situation, where I need to create an `ensureSearchIndexReady` function. This function should list checks and return if ready; otherwise, it should call `reindexSearch`. This function also needs to handle listing and validating. 
> 
> Then, I need to make sure to remove any data after ensuring the index is fresh. I’ll have to account for possible asynchronous errors during product create events. 
> 
> Finally, I’ll ensure to update and verify the source after making full checks on the database.

The fresh run passed, but it revealed noisy asynchronous event errors while the search index was still uninitialized. I’m tightening the seed order: initialize the index before product changes on a fresh DB, then do a final rebuild and verify it’s ready. That avoids relying on a successful exit code while background ingestion is failing.

````
       * seed and a later full rebuild, including products deleted by this script.
       */
      async function reindexSearch(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const search = ctx.container.resolve(Modules.SEARCH)
        const result = await search.reindex({ index: "product" })
      
        await assertSearchIndexReady(ctx)
        ctx.logger.info(
          `Reindexed the product search index (${result.indexes.join(", ")}); status is ready.`
        )
      }
      
      async function assertSearchIndexReady(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const search = ctx.container.resolve(Modules.SEARCH)
        const indexDetails = await search.listIndexes()
        const productIndex = indexDetails.find((index) => index.name === "product")
      
        if (productIndex?.status !== "ready") {
          throw new MedusaError(
            MedusaError.Types.UNEXPECTED_STATE,
            `Product search index is not ready (status: ${productIndex?.status ?? "missing"}).`
          )
        }
      }
      
      /**
       * The event subscriber runs as products change. On a fresh install, seed the
       * empty/starter index first so those events do not race an index with no active
       * version. The final reindex then catches every write and deletion in the run.
       */
      async function ensureSearchIndexReady(ctx: SeedContext) {
        const search = ctx.container.resolve(Modules.SEARCH)
        const indexDetails = await search.listIndexes()
        const productIndex = indexDetails.find((index) => index.name === "product")
      
        if (productIndex?.status === "ready") {
          return
        }
      
        ctx.logger.info("Initializing the product search index before catalogue changes.")
        await reindexSearch(ctx)
      }
      
      // --- Entry point -------------------------------------------------------------
      
      export default async function seed({ container }: ExecArgs) {
        const ctx = createContext(container)
      
        ctx.logger.info("Seeding DevCart demo data...")
      
        const salesChannelId = await ensureSalesChannel(ctx)
        const store = await ensureStore(ctx, salesChannelId)
        const currencyCodes = (store.supported_currencies ?? [])
          .map((currency) => currency?.currency_code)
          .filter((code): code is string => Boolean(code))
      
        if (!currencyCodes.length) {
          ctx.logger.warn("The store has no supported currencies; prices were skipped.")
        }
      
        await ensurePublishableApiKey(ctx, salesChannelId)
        const regionId = await ensureRegion(ctx)
        await ensureTaxRegions(ctx)
      
        const stockLocationId = await ensureStockLocation(ctx, salesChannelId)
        const serviceZoneId = await ensureFulfillmentSet(ctx, stockLocationId)
        const shippingProfileId = await ensureShippingProfile(ctx)
        await ensureShippingOptions(
          ctx,
          serviceZoneId,
          shippingProfileId,
          currencyCodes,
          regionId
        )
      
        const refs = await ensureCatalogueRefs(ctx, salesChannelId, shippingProfileId)
        await ensureSearchIndexReady(ctx)
        await removeLegacyProducts(ctx)
        await removeLegacyCategories(ctx)
      
        await ensureProducts(ctx, refs, currencyCodes)
        await ensureInventoryLevels(ctx, stockLocationId)
        await reindexSearch(ctx)
      
        ctx.logger.info(
          `Done. ${CATALOGUE.length} DevCart products across ${CATEGORIES.length} categories and ${COLLECTIONS.length} collections.`
        )

      ```bash

      ## 8. Seed data
      
      The database needs its Medusa migrations applied before it can be seeded. On a fresh database,
      `pnpm run dev` runs `medusa develop`, which applies migrations during startup. If preparing the
      catalogue before starting the backend, run `pnpm exec medusa db:migrate` from `apps/backend` first.
      Then seed from the repository root:
      
      ```bash
      pnpm run backend:seed            # from the repository root
      # or, from apps/backend:
      pnpm run seed                    # = medusa exec ./src/scripts/seed.ts
      ```
      
      It creates a store with EUR/USD, the Europe region and its tax regions, a sales channel with a
      publishable key, a warehouse with a fulfillment set and two shipping options, then the DevCart
      catalogue: 5 categories, 3 collections, 5 tags, a shared Size and Color option, and 23 products with
      variants, prices and stock.
      
      - **Re-runnable.** Every step looks for what it is about to create first, so a second run adds
        nothing. Add a product to `CATALOGUE` in `src/scripts/seed.ts` and a re-run creates only that one.
      - **It replaces the starter's placeholder products.** The four products `initial-data-seed.ts`
        creates are deleted, along with their now-empty categories. That deletion is skipped automatically
        if the store has any order, so order history is never touched.
      - **The turbo task is not cached** (`turbo.json` sets `"cache": false` for `seed`). Caching would
        turn a second `pnpm run backend:seed` into a replay of the first run's log with no database work.
      - `src/scripts/seed-demo-products.ts` still exists as an optional bulk filler (50 generated products)
        for exercising pagination. It is not needed for the DevCart catalogue.
      
      After seeding, the admin dashboard at <http://localhost:9000/app> lists the products, and
      <http://localhost:8000/dk/store> lists them in the storefront.
      
      ## Verification checklist
      
      With both apps running:
      
      1. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:9000/health` prints `200`.
      2. <http://localhost:9000/app> loads the admin dashboard and the login succeeds.
      3. <http://localhost:8000> loads the storefront, with the store name in the navigation and browser tab.
````

````
      # AGENT SPEC: E-Commerce Store (MedusaJS v2 + Next.js)
      
      > **AUDIENCE: AI coding agent.** Read this entire file before doing anything. This is your source of truth for what to build, in what order, and how to behave. Re-read the relevant section before starting each task.
      Name of this ecommerce website: **DevCart**
      
      ---
      
      ## 0. PRIME DIRECTIVES
      
      1. **Follow the phases in order (§9).** Do not start Phase N+1 until Phase N acceptance criteria all pass.
      2. **Work on ONE task at a time.** Finish it, verify it, then report. Do not bundle unrelated changes.
      3. **Never guess APIs.** For any Medusa or Stripe API, first look in (a) existing code in this repo, (b) installed package types in `node_modules`, (c) official docs (docs.medusajs.com). If unsure, say so and ask.
      4. **Medusa v2 only.** Do NOT write Medusa v1 patterns (v1-style services/entities/repositories/loaders/`medusa-config.js` plugins). See §3.
      5. **Reuse what the starter already has.** Before building any feature, check whether `medusajs/dtc-starter` already implements it. Extend, don't duplicate.
      6. **Do not edit `node_modules` or Medusa core.** All custom logic goes in modules, workflows, subscribers, API routes, links, jobs, and admin extensions.
      7. **Never commit secrets.** Use `.env`; keep `.env.template` updated with placeholder values for every new variable.
      8. **After every change, run verification (§8.2).** If it fails, fix it. If it fails twice with the same cause, STOP and report the exact error plus your diagnosis. Do not rewrite large areas as a fix.
      9. **Do not install a new dependency without stating the reason** and checking that no installed package already does the job.
      10. **Keep changes minimal and scoped.** Do not refactor, rename, or reformat unrelated files.
      11. **Ask when ambiguous.** If a requirement conflicts with the starter's structure or is unclear, ask one concise question rather than assuming.
      
      ---
      
      ## 1. PROJECT DEFINITION
      
      - **What:** A complete headless e-commerce store: browse → cart → checkout (Stripe test mode) → order confirmation → account/order history, plus admin management.
      - **Purpose:** Portfolio project. Quality, correctness, and cleanliness matter more than feature count.
      - **Scope policy:** Ship MVP features (🟢) fully before any 🟡 or 🔵 feature.
      - **Owner:** Non-expert in web dev. Write clear, conventional, well-commented code. Prefer simple, readable solutions over clever ones. Explain non-obvious decisions in short code comments or in your task report.
      
      ---
      
      ## 2. TECH STACK (authoritative)
      
      | Layer | Technology |
      |-------|-----------|
      | Backend | MedusaJS v2, Node.js, TypeScript (strict) |
      | DB | PostgreSQL |
      | Cache / events | Redis |
      | Storefront | Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS |
      | API client | Medusa JS SDK |
      | Payments | Stripe (test mode) via Medusa Stripe payment provider |
      | Email | Resend (via a Medusa notification provider/module) |
      | Search | Meilisearch (Phase 2) |
      | Storage | S3-compatible (R2/S3/MinIO) for production; local file provider acceptable in dev |
      | Validation | Zod |
      | Tests | Jest (backend), Playwright (E2E) |
      | CI | GitHub Actions |
      | Local infra | Docker Compose (Postgres, Redis, Meilisearch) |
      | Deploy | Vercel (storefront), Railway/Render/Medusa Cloud (backend), Neon/Supabase (DB), Upstash (Redis) |
      
      **Step 0 of the project:** inspect the starter and write a short report listing which of the above it already includes (CMS, search, email, etc.). Treat the starter's existing choices as authoritative where they differ from this table, and flag the differences.
      
      ---
      
      ## 3. MEDUSA v2 RULES (MANDATORY)
      
      Use these constructs for custom backend work:
      
      | Need | Use |
      |------|-----|
      | New data model / domain logic | **Custom module** in `backend/src/modules/<name>/` (model, service, `index.ts`, migrations) |
      | Multi-step business logic with rollback | **Workflow** in `backend/src/workflows/` (steps + `createWorkflow`) |
      | Side effects on events (`order.placed`, etc.) | **Subscriber** in `backend/src/subscribers/` |
      | New HTTP endpoints | **API route** in `backend/src/api/{store|admin}/.../route.ts` with Zod validation middleware |
      | Relating data across modules | **Module Link** in `backend/src/links/` |
      | Scheduled work | **Scheduled job** in `backend/src/jobs/` |
      | Admin UI additions | **Admin widget/route** in `backend/src/admin/` |
      | Third-party service integration | **Provider module** (payment, notification, file, search wrapper) |
      
      **Forbidden:**
      - Medusa v1 APIs and patterns.
      - Direct SQL against Medusa core tables from storefront or ad-hoc scripts (use services/query).
      - Editing Medusa core packages.
      - Business logic inside API route handlers beyond orchestration; put it in workflows/services.
      
      **Always:** register new modules in `medusa-config.ts`; generate and run migrations (`npx medusa db:generate <module>` then `npx medusa db:migrate`); use the Query API / module services for reads.
      
      ---
      
      ## 4. STOREFRONT RULES (Next.js)
      
      - App Router. **Server Components by default.** Add `"use client"` only for interactivity (cart drawer, forms, gallery, Stripe Elements).
      - All Medusa calls go through a single SDK client in `storefront/src/lib/`. Do not scatter raw `fetch` calls.
      - Every data-driven UI MUST implement: **loading state, empty state, error state.**
      - Use `next/image` for images. Provide `alt` text.
      - Fully responsive, mobile-first (breakpoints: 360 / 768 / 1280 verified).
      - Accessibility baseline: semantic HTML, labelled form fields, visible focus, keyboard-operable controls, sufficient contrast.
      - SEO baseline: per-page `generateMetadata`, Open Graph tags, `sitemap.ts`, `robots.ts`, JSON-LD `Product` on product pages.
      - No hardcoded backend URLs, keys, or region IDs. Use env vars.
      - Country/region handling: follow the starter's existing region approach; do not invent a parallel one.
      
      ---
      
      ## 5. FEATURE SPECIFICATION
      
      Legend: 🟢 MVP · 🟡 Phase 2 · 🔵 Stretch. Each feature lists **acceptance criteria (AC)**. A feature is done only when all AC pass.
      
      ### 5.1 Catalog & Discovery
      
      | ID | Pri | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
      |----|-----|---------|---------------------|
      | C1 | 🟢 | Homepage | Hero section, featured products, category links, collection section; data from Medusa (or CMS if the starter has one); responsive |
      | C2 | 🟢 | Product listing | Grid with pagination or infinite scroll; shows image, title, price; empty + loading states |
      | C3 | 🟢 | Category & collection pages | Routes resolve by handle; show only matching products; 404 for unknown handle |
      | C4 | 🟢 | Product detail | Image gallery, variant selectors (options → variant), correct price per variant, stock state (in stock / out of stock), add-to-cart disabled when unavailable |
      | C5 | 🟢 | Sort & filter | Sort by newest / price asc / price desc; filter by category and price range; state reflected in URL query params |
      | C6 | 🟡 | Search | Meilisearch index of products; typo-tolerant instant results; reindex on product create/update/delete via subscribers |
      | C7 | 🟡 | Related products | Product page shows ≥4 related items (same category/collection), excluding current |
      | C8 | 🔵 | Reviews & ratings | See §5.5 |
      
      ### 5.2 Cart & Checkout
      
      | ID | Pri | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
      |----|-----|---------|---------------------|
      | K1 | 🟢 | Cart | Add, remove, change quantity; persists across reload (cart ID cookie); totals update correctly; handles out-of-stock errors gracefully |
      | K2 | 🟢 | Checkout steps | Email → shipping address → shipping method → payment → review; validation on every step; can go back without data loss |
      | K3 | 🟢 | Guest + logged-in checkout | Both flows complete; logged-in users get saved address prefill |
      | K4 | 🟢 | Stripe payment | PaymentIntent via Medusa payment session; Stripe Elements UI; success creates order; declined card shows a clear error and leaves cart intact |
      | K5 | 🟢 | Order confirmation | Page shows order number, items, totals, address; accessible right after checkout |
      | K6 | 🟡 | Promo codes | Apply/remove code in cart/checkout; totals reflect discount; invalid code shows error |
      | K7 | 🟡 | Stripe webhook | Webhook endpoint verified; handles late/missed completion safely (idempotent) |
      | K8 | 🔵 | Multi-region / multi-currency | Region switch changes currency and prices |
      
      ### 5.3 Customer Account
      
      | ID | Pri | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
      |----|-----|---------|---------------------|
      | A1 | 🟢 | Register / login / logout | Works with Medusa auth; errors shown for bad credentials/duplicate email; protected routes redirect to login |
      | A2 | 🟢 | Order history | List + detail page for the logged-in customer only |
      | A3 | 🟡 | Saved addresses | Add, edit, delete, set default |
      | A4 | 🟡 | Profile & password reset | Edit name/phone; reset-password email flow end-to-end |
      | A5 | 🔵 | Wishlist | See §5.5 |
      
      ### 5.4 Email (🟡 Phase 2)
      
      | ID | Feature | AC |
      |----|---------|----|
      | E1 | Order confirmation email | Subscriber on `order.placed` sends email via Resend with order summary; failure is logged and does NOT break order creation |
      | E2 | Password reset email | Link works and expires |
      | E3 | Shipment notification | Sent when a fulfillment is created/shipped |
      
      Emails: HTML + plain-text fallback; simple, consistent template; templates stored in `backend/src/modules/<notification>/templates/`.
      
      ### 5.5 Custom Backend Features (portfolio differentiators — implement 2 minimum, in Phase 3)
      
      **Option A — Product Reviews (🟡 preferred)**
      - Custom module `review`: fields `id`, `product_id`, `customer_id`, `rating` (1–5), `title`, `body`, `status` (`pending|approved|rejected`), timestamps.
      - Link review ↔ product and review ↔ customer using Module Links.
      - Store API: `GET /store/products/:id/reviews` (approved only, paginated), `POST /store/products/:id/reviews` (authenticated customer, Zod-validated, one review per customer per product).
      - Admin API + widget: list, approve, reject reviews.
      - Storefront: star summary, review list, review form (logged-in only).
      - Tests: module service tests + API route tests.
      
      **Option B — Wishlist (🔵)**
      - Custom module `wishlist`, linked to customer and product variant/product.
      - Store API: list/add/remove (authenticated).
      - Storefront: heart toggle on product card/page; wishlist page.
      
      **Option C — Low-stock alert (🔵)**
      - Scheduled job checks inventory below a configurable threshold; sends email to admin address via the notification provider; avoids duplicate alerts within 24h.
      
      **Option D — Admin sales dashboard widget (🔵)**
      - Admin route showing revenue, order count, top products for a date range using Query API.
      
      ### 5.6 Admin (Medusa Admin — configuration tasks, not custom code unless noted)
      
      - 🟢 Seed: regions, currencies, shipping options, stock location, sales channel, publishable API key, 15–30 realistic products with images, 4–6 categories, 2–3 collections. Put in a re-runnable seed script `backend/src/scripts/seed.ts` (extend the starter's seed if it exists).
      - 🟢 Verify admin can: create/edit products, manage inventory, view/fulfill/cancel/refund orders, view customers.
      - 🟡 Promotions configured and testable.
      
      ---
      
      ## 6. REPOSITORY LAYOUT (target)
      
      Adapt to the starter's actual structure; do not reorganize the starter without approval.
      
      ```
      .
      ├── backend/
      │   ├── src/
      │   │   ├── api/{store,admin}/
      │   │   ├── modules/
      │   │   ├── workflows/
      │   │   ├── subscribers/
      │   │   ├── jobs/
      │   │   ├── links/
      │   │   ├── admin/
      │   │   └── scripts/seed.ts
      │   ├── medusa-config.ts
      │   └── .env.template
      ├── storefront/
      │   ├── src/{app,modules,lib,styles}
      │   └── .env.template
      ├── docker-compose.yml
      ├── .github/workflows/ci.yml
      ├── docs/
      └── README.md  (this file)
      ```
      
      ---
      
      ## 7. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
      
      Maintain these in `.env.template` files (placeholders only). Add any new variable to the template in the same commit that introduces it.
      
      **backend**
      ```
      DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, STORE_CORS, ADMIN_CORS, AUTH_CORS,
      JWT_SECRET, COOKIE_SECRET,
      STRIPE_API_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM,
      MEILISEARCH_HOST, MEILISEARCH_ADMIN_KEY,
      S3_URL, S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, S3_REGION
      ```
      
      **storefront**
      ```
      NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDUSA_PUBLISHABLE_KEY,
      NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_REGION,
      NEXT_PUBLIC_MEILISEARCH_HOST, NEXT_PUBLIC_MEILISEARCH_SEARCH_KEY
      ```
      
      Rules: use only the exact names the starter already uses where they exist; never expose secret keys via `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`.
      
      ---
      
      ## 8. WORKING PROTOCOL
      
      ### 8.1 Per-task loop
      1. **Restate** the task in 1–2 lines and name the roadmap ID(s) (e.g., `C4`, `K2`).
      2. **Inspect** the relevant existing files. List what you found.
      3. **Plan** the change as a short list of files to create/modify. Wait for approval if the change touches >5 files or adds a dependency.
      4. **Implement** minimally.
      5. **Verify** (§8.2).
      6. **Report** using §8.3.
      
      ### 8.2 Verification commands (run what exists; add missing scripts)
      ```
      # backend
      npm run build
      npx tsc --noEmit
      npm run lint            # if configured
      npm run test:unit / test:integration:*   # relevant tests
      
      # storefront
      npm run lint
      npx tsc --noEmit
      npm run build
      ```
      Plus a manual check list for the feature (exact steps for the owner to click through).
      
      ### 8.3 Task report format
      ```
      TASK: <ID + name>
      STATUS: done | blocked | partial
      FILES CHANGED: <list>
      NEW ENV VARS / DEPENDENCIES: <list or none>
      HOW TO TEST: <numbered manual steps>
      VERIFICATION RESULT: <commands run + pass/fail>
      KNOWN ISSUES / DECISIONS: <short>
      SUGGESTED COMMIT MESSAGE: <conventional commit>
      ```
      
      ### 8.4 Git conventions
      - Work on a branch per feature: `feat/<id>-<slug>`, `fix/...`, `chore/...`.
      - Conventional Commits: `feat(storefront): add variant selector (C4)`.
      - Do not commit: `.env`, `node_modules`, build output, local DB dumps.
      - Propose a commit after each verified task; do not squash unrelated work together.
      
      ### 8.5 Failure protocol
      - Error → read full message → check docs/types/existing code → fix.
      - Same error twice → STOP. Report: exact error, what you tried, your hypothesis, and the options you see.
      - Never respond to a failure by deleting and regenerating large parts of working code.
      - Never disable lint/type checks or tests to make something pass.
      
      ---
      
      ## 9. ROADMAP (execute in order)
      
      ### PHASE 0 — Foundation
      **Tasks**
      - P0.1 Inspect starter; produce report (structure, versions, included integrations, missing items vs this spec).
      - P0.2 Make backend + storefront run locally from clean clone; document exact commands in `docs/SETUP.md`.
      - P0.3 Add/verify `docker-compose.yml` (Postgres, Redis; Meilisearch optional now).
      - P0.4 Add `.env.template` files; ensure `.gitignore` covers secrets.
      - P0.5 Remove or rename starter placeholder branding; set store name/metadata via env/config.
      - P0.6 Add CI skeleton: install, lint, typecheck, build for both apps.
      
      **Exit criteria:** fresh clone + `docs/SETUP.md` → both apps run; CI green.
      
      ### PHASE 1 — Core Store MVP
      **Tasks:** seed data (§5.6) → C1–C5 → K1–K5 → A1–A2 → responsive + states pass.
      
      **Exit criteria:** In test mode, a new visitor can: browse, pick a variant, add to cart, check out as guest with `4242 4242 4242 4242`, see confirmation; register, buy again, see both orders in history; admin sees the orders and can fulfill one. No console errors; `npm run build` passes on both apps.
      
      ### PHASE 2 — Commerce Completeness
      **Tasks:** E1–E3 → K6, K7 → A3, A4 → C6, C7 → SEO baseline (§4) → sitemap/robots/JSON-LD.
      
      **Exit criteria:** emails delivered in test; promo code works; search returns typo-tolerant results; reset-password flow works; structured data validates.
      
      ### PHASE 3 — Differentiators & Polish
      **Tasks:** implement ≥2 options from §5.5 (start with Reviews) → accessibility pass → performance pass (Lighthouse Performance/Accessibility/SEO ≥ 90 on home, listing, product) → dark mode (optional).
      
      **Exit criteria:** custom modules have tests; admin extension works; Lighthouse targets met.
      
      ### PHASE 4 — Testing & Deployment
      **Tasks:**
      - P4.1 Backend tests for custom modules/workflows/routes.
      - P4.2 Playwright E2E: (1) guest purchase, (2) register+login+order history, (3) search, (4) failed payment.
      - P4.3 CI runs lint, types, tests, build; E2E on main or nightly.
      - P4.4 Production config: backend (server + worker mode if applicable per Medusa docs), DB migrations on deploy, Redis, S3 storage, CORS, Stripe webhook URL, domains.
      - P4.5 Deploy storefront to Vercel; backend to chosen host; run production seed; smoke-test full purchase.
      - P4.6 Write `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` with exact steps and a rollback note.
      
      **Exit criteria:** live URLs work end-to-end in Stripe test mode.
      
      ### PHASE 5 — Documentation
      **Tasks:** generate `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (diagram + module/workflow/subscriber inventory), `docs/DECISIONS.md` (key choices and why), `docs/TESTING.md`, and a **separate human-facing `README.human.md`** (pitch, screenshots placeholders, live links, setup, features). Do this only when asked.
      
      ---
      
      ## 10. ARCHITECTURE REFERENCE
      
      ```
      Browser → Next.js Storefront (Vercel)
                    │  Medusa JS SDK (Store API, publishable key)
                    ▼
               Medusa Backend (Node) ──► PostgreSQL
                    │                 ──► Redis (events, workflows, cache)
                    │                 ──► Stripe (payments; webhook → backend)
                    │                 ──► Resend (notifications)
                    │                 ──► Meilisearch (search index)
                    │                 ──► S3/R2 (files)
               Medusa Admin Dashboard (served by backend at /app)
      ```
      
      **Checkout sequence (must be preserved):**
      1. Create/retrieve cart (region-aware) → add line items.
      2. Set email + shipping/billing address.
      3. List and set shipping method.
      4. Initiate payment session (Stripe) → get `client_secret`.
      5. Confirm payment client-side with Stripe Elements.
      6. Complete cart server-side → order created.
      7. `order.placed` event → subscriber sends confirmation email.
      8. Stripe webhook acts as an idempotent safety net.
      
      **Event → handler map (target):**
      | Event | Handler |
      |-------|---------|
      | `order.placed` | send confirmation email |
      | `product.created/updated/deleted` | update Meilisearch index |
      | `fulfillment.created` (or shipment event per docs) | send shipment email |
      | `auth.password_reset` | send reset email |
      
      (Verify exact event names against Medusa docs/installed version before implementing.)
      
      ---
      
      ## 11. CODE QUALITY STANDARDS
      
      - TypeScript `strict`; no `any` unless justified in a comment.
      - Validate all external input (API bodies, query params) with Zod.
      - Small functions, descriptive names, no dead code, no commented-out blocks.
      - Handle and log errors; never swallow them silently. Side-effect failures (email, search) must not break core commerce flows.
      - No secrets, tokens, or personal data in logs.
      - Prefer existing utilities/components over new ones. Keep UI components reusable and in the storefront's `modules/` convention.
      - Comments explain *why*, not *what*.
      
      ---
      
      ## 12. SECURITY & PERFORMANCE CHECKLIST (apply continuously)
      
      - CORS restricted to known origins in production.
      - Secure cookies, strong `JWT_SECRET`/`COOKIE_SECRET` in production.
      - Stripe webhook signature verified.
      - Authenticated routes check customer ownership of resources (orders, addresses, reviews).
      - `npm audit` clean of high/critical issues (or documented).
      - Images optimized; product pages cached/revalidated sensibly; avoid N+1 API calls on listing pages.
      
      ---
      
      ## 13. DEFINITION OF DONE (project)
      
      - [ ] All 🟢 features pass AC.
      - [ ] Phase 1–4 exit criteria met.
      - [ ] CI green; tests cover custom modules and the main purchase flow.
      - [ ] Lighthouse ≥ 90 (Performance, Accessibility, SEO) on key pages.
      - [ ] Deployed; live full purchase works in Stripe test mode.
      - [ ] `.env.template`, `docs/SETUP.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` are accurate.
      - [ ] No secrets in repo history.
      
      ---
      
      ## 14. FIRST ACTION
      
      Begin with **P0.1**: 
      Read the frontend-design skill. Propose a design plan for this store (subject and audience, 4–6 named hex colors, typefaces and roles, layout concept, principles). Save it as docs/DESIGN.md. Wait for my approval before building any page.
      Inspect the repository, then output a report containing:
      1. Directory structure (2 levels deep).
      2. Medusa version and key package versions.
      3. Which features/integrations from §2 and §5 already exist in the starter.
      4. What is missing or differs from this spec.
      5. Any risks or questions.
      
      Do not write or modify code until the owner approves the report.

      progress against it: what is done, what is in flight, what is left. If this file and the spec disagree,
      the spec wins.
      
      Legend: `[x]` done and verified · `[~]` in progress / partially done · `[ ]` not started · `[!]` blocked
      
      Last updated: P1.0 done and verified (re-runnable seed with the DevCart catalogue). Phase 1 continues
      with C1–C5.
      
      ---

      typecheck and build all pass for both apps from the repository root (the same commands CI runs).
      
      ## Phase 1 — Core Store MVP
      
      Tasks: seed data (§5.6) → C1–C5 → K1–K5 → A1–A2 → responsive + states pass.
      
      - [x] **P1.0** `src/scripts/seed.ts`: DevCart catalogue (23 products, 5 categories, 3 collections), re-runnable (§5.6). Run with `pnpm run backend:seed`. Verified against a fresh migrated database: first run creates the catalogue and search index, second run leaves the catalogue counts unchanged; Store API and storefront routes were checked against the running instance.
      - [ ] **C1** Homepage — hero, featured products, category links, collection section.
      - [ ] **C2** Product listing — grid, image/title/price, loading + empty states.

        InstantSearch adapter. Per spec §2 the starter's choice is authoritative, so Meilisearch is dropped.
````
