- path: apps/storefront/src/app/[countryCode]/(main)/store/page.tsx
  content: |
      import { Metadata } from "next"
      import { notFound } from "next/navigation"
      
      import { getRegion } from "@lib/data/regions"
      import StoreTemplate from "@modules/store/templates"
      
      export const metadata: Metadata = {
        title: "Store",
        description: "Explore all of our products.",
      }
      
      export default async function StorePage(props: {
        params: Promise<{ countryCode: string }>
      }) {
        const { countryCode } = await props.params
        const region = await getRegion(countryCode)
      
        if (!region) {
          notFound()
        }
      
        return <StoreTemplate currencyCode={region.currency_code} />
      }
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/store/templates/index.tsx
  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import type { SearchClient } from "instantsearch.js"
      import { Configure, InstantSearch } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import { PRODUCT_INDEX_NAME, searchClient } from "@lib/search-client"
      import StoreHits from "@modules/store/components/store-hits"
      import StoreRefinements from "@modules/store/components/store-refinements"
      import StoreSearchBox from "@modules/store/components/store-search-box"
      
      const PRODUCT_LIMIT = 12
      
      const StoreTemplate = ({ currencyCode }: { currencyCode: string }) => {
        return (
          <div className="py-6 content-container" data-testid="category-container">
            <div className="mb-8 text-2xl-semi">
              <h1 data-testid="store-page-title">All products</h1>
            </div>
      
            <div className="flex flex-col small:flex-row small:items-start">
              <InstantSearch
                indexName={PRODUCT_INDEX_NAME}
                searchClient={searchClient as unknown as SearchClient}
                routing
                future={{ preserveSharedStateOnUnmount: true }}
              >
                <Configure hitsPerPage={PRODUCT_LIMIT} />
                <StoreRefinements currencyCode={currencyCode} />
                <div className="w-full min-w-0">
                  <StoreSearchBox />
                  <StoreHits
                    hitsPerPage={PRODUCT_LIMIT}
                    currencyCode={currencyCode}
                  />
                </div>
              </InstantSearch>
            </div>
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default StoreTemplate
      
  referencedBy: {}

- path: docs/PROJECT_SPEC.md
  content: |
      # AGENT SPEC: E-Commerce Store (MedusaJS v2 + Next.js)
      
      > **AUDIENCE: AI coding agent.** Read this entire file before doing anything. This is your source of truth for what to build, in what order, and how to behave. Re-read the relevant section before starting each task.
      Name of this ecommerce website: **DevCart**
      
      ---
      
      ## 0. PRIME DIRECTIVES
      
      1. **Follow the phases in order (§9).** Do not start Phase N+1 until Phase N acceptance criteria all pass.
      2. **Work on ONE task at a time.** Finish it, verify it, then report. Do not bundle unrelated changes.
      3. **Never guess APIs.** For any Medusa or Stripe API, first look in (a) existing code in this repo, (b) installed package types in `node_modules`, (c) official docs (docs.medusajs.com). If unsure, say so and ask.
      4. **Medusa v2 only.** Do NOT write Medusa v1 patterns (v1-style services/entities/repositories/loaders/`medusa-config.js` plugins). See §3.
      5. **Reuse what the starter already has.** Before building any feature, check whether `medusajs/dtc-starter` already implements it. Extend, don't duplicate.
      6. **Do not edit `node_modules` or Medusa core.** All custom logic goes in modules, workflows, subscribers, API routes, links, jobs, and admin extensions.
      7. **Never commit secrets.** Use `.env`; keep `.env.template` updated with placeholder values for every new variable.
      8. **After every change, run verification (§8.2).** If it fails, fix it. If it fails twice with the same cause, STOP and report the exact error plus your diagnosis. Do not rewrite large areas as a fix.
      9. **Do not install a new dependency without stating the reason** and checking that no installed package already does the job.
      10. **Keep changes minimal and scoped.** Do not refactor, rename, or reformat unrelated files.
      11. **Ask when ambiguous.** If a requirement conflicts with the starter's structure or is unclear, ask one concise question rather than assuming.
      
      ---
      
      ## 1. PROJECT DEFINITION
      
      - **What:** A complete headless e-commerce store: browse → cart → checkout (Stripe test mode) → order confirmation → account/order history, plus admin management.
      - **Purpose:** Portfolio project. Quality, correctness, and cleanliness matter more than feature count.
      - **Scope policy:** Ship MVP features (🟢) fully before any 🟡 or 🔵 feature.
      - **Owner:** Non-expert in web dev. Write clear, conventional, well-commented code. Prefer simple, readable solutions over clever ones. Explain non-obvious decisions in short code comments or in your task report.
      
      ---
      
      ## 2. TECH STACK (authoritative)
      
      | Layer | Technology |
      |-------|-----------|
      | Backend | MedusaJS v2, Node.js, TypeScript (strict) |
      | DB | PostgreSQL |
      | Cache / events | Redis |
      | Storefront | Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS |
      | API client | Medusa JS SDK |
      | Payments | Stripe (test mode) via Medusa Stripe payment provider |
      | Email | Resend (via a Medusa notification provider/module) |
      | Search | Meilisearch (Phase 2) |
      | Storage | S3-compatible (R2/S3/MinIO) for production; local file provider acceptable in dev |
      | Validation | Zod |
      | Tests | Jest (backend), Playwright (E2E) |
      | CI | GitHub Actions |
      | Local infra | Docker Compose (Postgres, Redis, Meilisearch) |
      | Deploy | Vercel (storefront), Railway/Render/Medusa Cloud (backend), Neon/Supabase (DB), Upstash (Redis) |
      
      **Step 0 of the project:** inspect the starter and write a short report listing which of the above it already includes (CMS, search, email, etc.). Treat the starter's existing choices as authoritative where they differ from this table, and flag the differences.
      
      ---
      
      ## 3. MEDUSA v2 RULES (MANDATORY)
      
      Use these constructs for custom backend work:
      
      | Need | Use |
      |------|-----|
      | New data model / domain logic | **Custom module** in `backend/src/modules/<name>/` (model, service, `index.ts`, migrations) |
      | Multi-step business logic with rollback | **Workflow** in `backend/src/workflows/` (steps + `createWorkflow`) |
      | Side effects on events (`order.placed`, etc.) | **Subscriber** in `backend/src/subscribers/` |
      | New HTTP endpoints | **API route** in `backend/src/api/{store|admin}/.../route.ts` with Zod validation middleware |
      | Relating data across modules | **Module Link** in `backend/src/links/` |
      | Scheduled work | **Scheduled job** in `backend/src/jobs/` |
      | Admin UI additions | **Admin widget/route** in `backend/src/admin/` |
      | Third-party service integration | **Provider module** (payment, notification, file, search wrapper) |
      
      **Forbidden:**
      - Medusa v1 APIs and patterns.
      - Direct SQL against Medusa core tables from storefront or ad-hoc scripts (use services/query).
      - Editing Medusa core packages.
      - Business logic inside API route handlers beyond orchestration; put it in workflows/services.
      
      **Always:** register new modules in `medusa-config.ts`; generate and run migrations (`npx medusa db:generate <module>` then `npx medusa db:migrate`); use the Query API / module services for reads.
      
      ---
      
      ## 4. STOREFRONT RULES (Next.js)
      
      - App Router. **Server Components by default.** Add `"use client"` only for interactivity (cart drawer, forms, gallery, Stripe Elements).
      - All Medusa calls go through a single SDK client in `storefront/src/lib/`. Do not scatter raw `fetch` calls.
      - Every data-driven UI MUST implement: **loading state, empty state, error state.**
      - Use `next/image` for images. Provide `alt` text.
      - Fully responsive, mobile-first (breakpoints: 360 / 768 / 1280 verified).
      - Accessibility baseline: semantic HTML, labelled form fields, visible focus, keyboard-operable controls, sufficient contrast.
      - SEO baseline: per-page `generateMetadata`, Open Graph tags, `sitemap.ts`, `robots.ts`, JSON-LD `Product` on product pages.
      - No hardcoded backend URLs, keys, or region IDs. Use env vars.
      - Country/region handling: follow the starter's existing region approach; do not invent a parallel one.
      
      ---
      
      ## 5. FEATURE SPECIFICATION
      
      Legend: 🟢 MVP · 🟡 Phase 2 · 🔵 Stretch. Each feature lists **acceptance criteria (AC)**. A feature is done only when all AC pass.
      
      ### 5.1 Catalog & Discovery
      
      | ID | Pri | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
      |----|-----|---------|---------------------|
      | C1 | 🟢 | Homepage | Hero section, featured products, category links, collection section; data from Medusa (or CMS if the starter has one); responsive |
      | C2 | 🟢 | Product listing | Grid with pagination or infinite scroll; shows image, title, price; empty + loading states |
      | C3 | 🟢 | Category & collection pages | Routes resolve by handle; show only matching products; 404 for unknown handle |
      | C4 | 🟢 | Product detail | Image gallery, variant selectors (options → variant), correct price per variant, stock state (in stock / out of stock), add-to-cart disabled when unavailable |
      | C5 | 🟢 | Sort & filter | Sort by newest / price asc / price desc; filter by category and price range; state reflected in URL query params |
      | C6 | 🟡 | Search | Meilisearch index of products; typo-tolerant instant results; reindex on product create/update/delete via subscribers |
      | C7 | 🟡 | Related products | Product page shows ≥4 related items (same category/collection), excluding current |
      | C8 | 🔵 | Reviews & ratings | See §5.5 |
      
      ### 5.2 Cart & Checkout
      
      | ID | Pri | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
      |----|-----|---------|---------------------|
      | K1 | 🟢 | Cart | Add, remove, change quantity; persists across reload (cart ID cookie); totals update correctly; handles out-of-stock errors gracefully |
      | K2 | 🟢 | Checkout steps | Email → shipping address → shipping method → payment → review; validation on every step; can go back without data loss |
      | K3 | 🟢 | Guest + logged-in checkout | Both flows complete; logged-in users get saved address prefill |
      | K4 | 🟢 | Stripe payment | PaymentIntent via Medusa payment session; Stripe Elements UI; success creates order; declined card shows a clear error and leaves cart intact |
      | K5 | 🟢 | Order confirmation | Page shows order number, items, totals, address; accessible right after checkout |
      | K6 | 🟡 | Promo codes | Apply/remove code in cart/checkout; totals reflect discount; invalid code shows error |
      | K7 | 🟡 | Stripe webhook | Webhook endpoint verified; handles late/missed completion safely (idempotent) |
      | K8 | 🔵 | Multi-region / multi-currency | Region switch changes currency and prices |
      
      ### 5.3 Customer Account
      
      | ID | Pri | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
      |----|-----|---------|---------------------|
      | A1 | 🟢 | Register / login / logout | Works with Medusa auth; errors shown for bad credentials/duplicate email; protected routes redirect to login |
      | A2 | 🟢 | Order history | List + detail page for the logged-in customer only |
      | A3 | 🟡 | Saved addresses | Add, edit, delete, set default |
      | A4 | 🟡 | Profile & password reset | Edit name/phone; reset-password email flow end-to-end |
      | A5 | 🔵 | Wishlist | See §5.5 |
      
      ### 5.4 Email (🟡 Phase 2)
      
      | ID | Feature | AC |
      |----|---------|----|
      | E1 | Order confirmation email | Subscriber on `order.placed` sends email via Resend with order summary; failure is logged and does NOT break order creation |
      | E2 | Password reset email | Link works and expires |
      | E3 | Shipment notification | Sent when a fulfillment is created/shipped |
      
      Emails: HTML + plain-text fallback; simple, consistent template; templates stored in `backend/src/modules/<notification>/templates/`.
      
      ### 5.5 Custom Backend Features (portfolio differentiators — implement 2 minimum, in Phase 3)
      
      **Option A — Product Reviews (🟡 preferred)**
      - Custom module `review`: fields `id`, `product_id`, `customer_id`, `rating` (1–5), `title`, `body`, `status` (`pending|approved|rejected`), timestamps.
      - Link review ↔ product and review ↔ customer using Module Links.
      - Store API: `GET /store/products/:id/reviews` (approved only, paginated), `POST /store/products/:id/reviews` (authenticated customer, Zod-validated, one review per customer per product).
      - Admin API + widget: list, approve, reject reviews.
      - Storefront: star summary, review list, review form (logged-in only).
      - Tests: module service tests + API route tests.
      
      **Option B — Wishlist (🔵)**
      - Custom module `wishlist`, linked to customer and product variant/product.
      - Store API: list/add/remove (authenticated).
      - Storefront: heart toggle on product card/page; wishlist page.
      
      **Option C — Low-stock alert (🔵)**
      - Scheduled job checks inventory below a configurable threshold; sends email to admin address via the notification provider; avoids duplicate alerts within 24h.
      
      **Option D — Admin sales dashboard widget (🔵)**
      - Admin route showing revenue, order count, top products for a date range using Query API.
      
      ### 5.6 Admin (Medusa Admin — configuration tasks, not custom code unless noted)
      
      - 🟢 Seed: regions, currencies, shipping options, stock location, sales channel, publishable API key, 15–30 realistic products with images, 4–6 categories, 2–3 collections. Put in a re-runnable seed script `backend/src/scripts/seed.ts` (extend the starter's seed if it exists).
      - 🟢 Verify admin can: create/edit products, manage inventory, view/fulfill/cancel/refund orders, view customers.
      - 🟡 Promotions configured and testable.
      
      ---
      
      ## 6. REPOSITORY LAYOUT (target)
      
      Adapt to the starter's actual structure; do not reorganize the starter without approval.

      .
      ├── backend/
      │   ├── src/
      │   │   ├── api/{store,admin}/

  content: |
      # DevCart — Design Plan
      
      Status: **proposal, awaiting owner approval.** No page is built from this yet.
      
      ## 1. Subject, audience, and job
      
      The spec names the store **DevCart** but does not define what it sells, so this is a proposal.
      
      - **Subject:** a small direct-to-consumer brand selling merchandise for people who build software — apparel (tees, hoodies, caps, totes) plus desk objects (mugs, keycaps, notebooks, stickers). Everything is drawn from software-making culture: version numbers, changelogs, compiler and terminal culture, hardware and keyboards.
      - **Audience:** developers, computer-science students, and engineering teams buying personal items or small team swag. They read Latin text in English, know what a keyboard shortcut is, and are unimpressed by generic tech-bro marketing. They buy on the strength of the joke, the typography, and the print quality.
      - **Primary job:** make it easy to find one product, understand exactly what it is and what it costs, and check out in a few steps. Personality lives in the catalogue, not in the checkout.
      
      The seed data in this repository is already apparel (tee, sweatshirt, sweatpants, shorts) with generic "Medusa" titles. The demo catalogue will be rewritten to fit the DevCart brand in Phase 1; the item types stay the same.
      
      ## 2. Colour — riso inks on uncoated stock
      
      DevCart's catalogue is printed merchandise, so the palette is built from actual risograph ink behaviour: flat, slightly translucent inks, limited to one or two per impression, misregistering by a hair against each other. That constraint is the identity. It is also deliberately not the warm-cream-plus-terracotta look, and not near-black-plus-acid-green.
      
      | Token | Hex | Role |
      |-------|-----|------|
      | `stock` | `#E8E9E3` | Page background. Cool uncoated paper, not a warm cream. |
      | `ink` | `#17181B` | Body text, rules, plate borders. The "black" plate. |
      | `riso-blue` | `#006DAE` | Primary brand colour: links, primary buttons, focus ring. |
      | `riso-pink` | `#FB008E` | The accent. Large display text on stock, fills, markers. |
      | `riso-yellow` | `#FFD400` | Fill only. Highlight behind ink text, used rarely. |
      | `riso-green` | `#007942` | State: in stock, order confirmed. Text or fill. |
      
      **AA adjustment.** `riso-blue`, `riso-pink` and `riso-green` are darkened from the raw riso ink values (`#0078BF`, `#FF48B0`, `#00A95C`) so that every permitted text usage meets WCAG AA. Hue is preserved in each case. §2.1 records the measurements; `stock`, `ink` and `riso-yellow` are unchanged.
      
      Rules of use:
      
      - **Two inks per view, maximum.** `ink` + `riso-blue` is the default impression. `riso-pink` is the second ink, and it earns its place by marking something specific (an on-sale price, the current filter, the hero headline).
      - **Overprint, not shadow.** Where two inks meet, use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` so the overlap darkens like real ink. This replaces drop shadows entirely — no soft grey card shadows anywhere.
      - Yellow and green never carry meaning on their own; they always sit next to a word that says the same thing.
      
      ### 2.1 Contrast, measured
      
      Ratios are WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance contrast ratios against the token pairs actually used. AA needs 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (24px+, or 19px+ bold) and for non-text markers and boundaries.
      
      | Foreground | Background | Ratio | AA normal text | AA large text / markers |
      |---|---|---|---|---|
      | `ink` | `stock` | 14.54:1 | pass | pass |
      | `stock` | `ink` | 14.54:1 | pass | pass |
      | `ink` | `riso-yellow` | 12.40:1 | pass | pass |
      | `ink` | `riso-pink` | 4.64:1 | pass | pass |
      | `riso-blue` | `stock` | 4.53:1 | pass | pass |
      | `stock` | `riso-blue` | 4.53:1 | pass | pass |
      | `riso-green` | `stock` | 4.51:1 | pass | pass |
      | `stock` | `riso-green` | 4.51:1 | pass | pass |
      | `riso-pink` | `stock` | 3.13:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `stock` | `riso-pink` | 3.13:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `ink` | `riso-green` | 3.22:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `ink` | `riso-blue` | 3.21:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `riso-green` | `ink` | 3.22:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `blue` | `ink` | 3.21:1 | **fail** | pass |
      | `riso-yellow` | `stock` | 1.17:1 | **fail** | **fail** |
      
      Rules that follow from the table, and which the base components enforce:
      
      - **`riso-pink` is never text below 24px.** It passes AA only as large display type, as a fill, or as a marker (3:1 for non-text). No body copy, no links, no form labels, no button labels.
      - **Never `stock` on `riso-pink`** (3.13:1). Text on a pink fill is `ink` (4.64:1).
      - **Never `ink` on `riso-blue`** (3.21:1). Text on a blue fill is `stock` (4.53:1).
      - **Never `ink` on `riso-green`; use `stock` on green** (4.51:1). `riso-green` as text on `stock` is fine.
      - **`riso-yellow` is a fill, never text**, and only ever behind `ink` (12.40:1).
      - `riso-blue` and `riso-green` as text on `stock` both clear normal-text AA, so links and state labels may use them directly.
      
      ## 3. Typography
      
      Two families plus one data face. Not Inter, not Space Grotesk, not a system stack.
      
      - **Display — Bricolage Grotesque** (variable, Google Fonts). Headlines, the hero, product titles, category names. It has a slightly irregular poster-grotesque character that suits printed merchandise and looks unlike a default UI font. Used at large sizes with tight tracking, and only at large sizes.
      - **Body / UI — IBM Plex Sans.** Paragraphs, labels, buttons, forms, navigation. Engineering heritage that fits the subject and stays legible at 14–16px, which is where a store's real reading happens.
      - **Data — IBM Plex Mono.** Reserved for content that is genuinely machine data: SKUs, spec tables ("100% cotton / 240 gsm"), order numbers, and code-like product names. Not used for eyebrows, nav labels, or decorative captions.
      
      Type scale (1.25 ratio, base 16px): 14 / 16 / 20 / 25 / 31 / 39 / 49 / 61. Body line length capped at ~72 characters; display lines at ~40.
      
      Weights: Bricolage Grotesque 700 for display; IBM Plex Sans 400 for body, 600 for buttons and labels. Normal sentence case everywhere — no all-caps labels.
      
      ## 4. Layout — the press sheet
      
      The page is treated as a print sheet, not a stack of floating cards. A visible hairline grid and small corner registration marks define the content area; every element is aligned to that grid.
      
      - Content is **left-aligned** on a centred max-width column of 1280px, with a lopsided editorial rhythm: the 12-column grid is divided roughly 7/5 rather than 6/6, so nothing sits dead centre.
      - Product cards are **plates**: square corners, a hairline `ink` border, the image on `stock`, and the title/price set below in a fixed type block. No border-radius, no shadow, no gradient. One consistent square edge is the system; rounded corners are never introduced.
      - **No numbered markers** except where something really is a sequence — order status (placed → paid → shipped) and checkout steps. Product plates are not numbered.
      - Sections are separated by rules and whitespace, not by alternating background colours.
      - Mobile (360 / 768 / 1280) collapses the grid to one and two columns; the alignment stays left.
      
      ### Home
      
      ```
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      | DevCart        Shop  Collections  About      Search  Cart |
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      |                                                          |
      |  Merch for                                               |
      |  people who        [ hero: product photo with            |
      |  build software    riso-pink and riso-blue plates        |
      |                    offset against it ]                   |
      |  [ Shop new ]  [ Browse all ]                             |
      |                                                          |
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      |  New this drop                                            |
      |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+           |
      |  | plate  |  | plate  |  | plate  |  | plate  |           |
      |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+           |
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      |  Collections:  Everyday  /  Desk  /  Limited Run          |
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      ```
      
      ### Listing (`/store`, category, collection)
      
      ```
      +----------------------------------------------------------+
      |  All products                 [ search ]                  |
      +---------------+------------------------------------------+
      | Sort          |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+       |
      |  Newest       |  | plate  |  | plate  |  | plate  |       |
      | Category      |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+       |
      |  [x] Shirts   |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+       |
      | Price         |  | plate  |  | plate  |  | plate  |       |
      |  |----o----|  |  +--------+  +--------+  +--------+       |
      +---------------+------------------------------------------+
      |                    <  1 2 3  >                            |
      ```
      
      ### Product
      
      ```
      +-------------------------------+--------------------------+
      |  [ gallery: main image ]      |  Hoodie                  |
      |  +----+ +----+ +----+         |  EUR 45.00   in stock    |
      |  |    | |    | |    |         |                          |
      |  +----+ +----+ +----+         |  Size  [S] [M] [L] [XL]  |
      |                               |  Colour [ink] [pink]     |
      |                               |  [ Add to cart ]         |
      |                               |  ---------------------   |
      |                               |  Specs (mono table)      |
      |                               |  SKU  DC-HOOD-INK-M      |
      +-------------------------------+--------------------------+
      ```
      
      ## 5. Principles
      
      1. **Ink is scarce.** Two colours per screen, one of them loud. If a third appears, something above it gets removed.
      2. **The grid is visible and load-bearing.** Rules, registration marks, and plate edges carry real structure; they are not decoration. Removing them should break the layout's legibility, not just its mood.
      3. **Type is the image.** Display headlines are content and are set as such. No stock-photo hero collages, no gradient washes, no icon-and-heading card trios.
      4. **Products are editions.** Specs, SKUs and print details are shown as plain, useful facts — an honest product page is the brand's tone, not a marketing one.
      5. **Motion is mechanical and rare.** Motion answers a click: adding to cart, opening the cart drawer, switching a variant image. No scroll-triggered fade-up on every section, no hover lift on every card. See §5.1.
      
      ### 5.1 Deferred polish
      
      Three visual devices are **optional polish, built last** — after the pages and the commerce flows work, and only if they still earn their place:
      
      1. **Registration marks** — small corner crop marks on plates and page sections.
      2. **Overprint** — `mix-blend-mode: multiply` where two inks overlap.
      3. **Settle-into-register** — the single page-load animation where plates align, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`.
      
      Until then, plates use plain hairline borders and no blend modes. The base components must look finished without any of these, so none of them may be load-bearing.
      6. **Copy is plain.** Sentence case, active voice, one job per string. The button says "Add to cart", the toast says "Added to cart". Empty cart says what to do next; an error says what failed and how to fix it. No filler, no exclamation marks.
      
      ## 6. Review against the brief
      
      Checked against the common generated-design defaults before building:
      
      - **Changed:** the original pass used a warm cream `#F4F1EA` background with a serif display and a clay accent. That is the single most recognisable generated palette, so the ground moved to a cool uncoated `stock` `#E8E9E3`, the display face to Bricolage Grotesque, and the accent to riso pink — a colour that comes from the subject's actual production method rather than from a mood board.
      - **Changed:** an early layout used rounded cards with soft shadows (the SaaS-card kit). Replaced with square hairline plates and multiply overprint, which is what printed merchandise actually looks like.
      - **Changed:** mono was initially going to label nav items and eyebrows. Cut back to machine data only, since mono-for-labels is a template tell and this brief does not need it.
      - **Changed:** the raw riso inks were kept for shape but darkened where they failed AA. Blue and green moved just far enough to clear 4.5:1 on `stock`; pink moved to 3.13:1 on stock while holding 4.64:1 for `ink` text on a pink fill. The exact riso values survive only as the hue reference in §2.
      - **Kept, because the brief justifies it:** tight display typography and hard grid edges — this is a print catalogue, and those are its real conventions, not a stylistic costume.
      
      ## 7. Decisions confirmed by the owner
      
      1. **Subject:** developer merchandise, as described in §1.
      2. **Name:** DevCart.
      3. **Mode:** light mode only for now; dark mode deferred (Phase 3 marks it optional).
      4. **Headlines:** sentence case everywhere, including the wireframes above.
      5. **Accessibility:** `riso-pink` and `riso-blue` must meet WCAG AA for any text usage; see §2.1.
      6. **Polish:** registration marks, overprint and the settle animation are deferred to last; see §5.1.

- path: apps/storefront/src/styles/globals.css
  content: |
      @import "tailwindcss/base";
      @import "tailwindcss/components";
      @import "tailwindcss/utilities";
      
      /*
       * DevCart theme tokens.
       *
       * Colours are stored as raw sRGB channels so Tailwind can build `rgb(... / <alpha-value>)`
       * utilities from them and opacity modifiers keep working. The hex value in each comment is
       * the source of truth for design work; docs/DESIGN.md §2.1 records the contrast ratios.
       */
      @layer base {
        :root {
          --dc-stock: 232 233 227; /* #E8E9E3 */
          --dc-ink: 23 24 27; /* #17181B */
          --dc-riso-blue: 0 109 174; /* #006DAE */
          --dc-riso-pink: 251 0 142; /* #FB008E */
          --dc-riso-yellow: 255 212 0; /* #FFD400 */
          --dc-riso-green: 0 121 66; /* #007942 */
      
          /* Spacing scale. `--dc-gutter` is the page edge, `--dc-section` the space
             between bands, `--dc-content` the max width of a reading column. */
          --dc-gutter: 1.5rem;
          --dc-section: 6rem;
          --dc-content: 80rem;
      
          /* The system is square. Kept as a variable so the value is stated once. */
          --dc-radius: 0px;
      
          /* Single focus treatment, reused by every interactive component. */
          --dc-focus-ring-width: 2px;
          --dc-focus-ring-offset: 2px;
        }
      }
      
      @layer base {
        /* The design is light-only; say so rather than following the OS preference. */
        html {
          color-scheme: light;
        }
      
        body {
          background-color: rgb(var(--dc-stock));
          color: rgb(var(--dc-ink));
        }
      
        /*
         * One visible focus ring for the whole system. Components do not repeat it
         * except where they paint their own background and need an offset colour.
         */
        :focus-visible {
          outline: var(--dc-focus-ring-width) solid rgb(var(--dc-riso-blue));
          outline-offset: var(--dc-focus-ring-offset);
        }
      }
      
      @layer utilities {
        /* Chrome, Safari and Opera */
        .no-scrollbar::-webkit-scrollbar {
          display: none;
        }
      
        .no-scrollbar::-webkit-scrollbar-track {
          background-color: transparent;
        }
      
        .no-scrollbar {
          -ms-overflow-style: none; /* IE and Edge */
          scrollbar-width: none; /* Firefox */
        }
      
        input:focus ~ label,
        input:not(:placeholder-shown) ~ label {
          @apply -translate-y-2 text-xsmall-regular;
        }
      
        input:focus ~ label {
          @apply left-0;
        }
      
        input:-webkit-autofill,
        input:-webkit-autofill:hover,
        input:-webkit-autofill:focus,
        textarea:-webkit-autofill,
        textarea:-webkit-autofill:hover,
        textarea:-webkit-autofill:focus,
        select:-webkit-autofill,
        select:-webkit-autofill:hover,
        select:-webkit-autofill:focus {
          border: 1px solid #212121;
          -webkit-text-fill-color: #212121;
          -webkit-box-shadow: 0 0 0px 1000px #fff inset;
          transition: background-color 5000s ease-in-out 0s;
        }
      
        input[type="search"]::-webkit-search-decoration,
        input[type="search"]::-webkit-search-cancel-button,
        input[type="search"]::-webkit-search-results-button,
        input[type="search"]::-webkit-search-results-decoration {
          -webkit-appearance: none;
        }
      }
      
      @layer components {
        .content-container {
          @apply max-w-[1440px] w-full mx-auto px-6;
        }
      
        .contrast-btn {
          @apply px-4 py-2 border border-black rounded-full hover:bg-black hover:text-white transition-colors duration-200 ease-in;
        }
      
        .text-xsmall-regular {
          @apply text-[10px] leading-4 font-normal;
        }
      
        .text-small-regular {
          @apply text-xs leading-5 font-normal;
        }
      
        .text-small-semi {
          @apply text-xs leading-5 font-semibold;
        }
      
        .text-base-regular {
          @apply text-sm leading-6 font-normal;
        }
      
        .text-base-semi {
          @apply text-sm leading-6 font-semibold;
        }
      
        .text-large-regular {
          @apply text-base leading-6 font-normal;
        }
      
        .text-large-semi {
          @apply text-base leading-6 font-semibold;
        }
      
        .text-xl-regular {
          @apply text-2xl leading-[36px] font-normal;
        }
      
        .text-xl-semi {
          @apply text-2xl leading-[36px] font-semibold;
        }
      
        .text-2xl-regular {
          @apply text-[30px] leading-[48px] font-normal;
        }
      
        .text-2xl-semi {
          @apply text-[30px] leading-[48px] font-semibold;
        }
      
        .text-3xl-regular {
          @apply text-[32px] leading-[44px] font-normal;
        }
      
        .text-3xl-semi {
          @apply text-[32px] leading-[44px] font-semibold;
        }
      }

      ---
      
      ## 8. WORKING PROTOCOL
      
      ### 8.1 Per-task loop
      1. **Restate** the task in 1–2 lines and name the roadmap ID(s) (e.g., `C4`, `K2`).
      2. **Inspect** the relevant existing files. List what you found.
      3. **Plan** the change as a short list of files to create/modify. Wait for approval if the change touches >5 files or adds a dependency.
      4. **Implement** minimally.
      5. **Verify** (§8.2).
      6. **Report** using §8.3.
      
      ### 8.2 Verification commands (run what exists; add missing scripts)
      ```
      # backend
      npm run build
      npx tsc --noEmit
      npm run lint            # if configured
      npm run test:unit / test:integration:*   # relevant tests
      
      # storefront
      npm run lint
      npx tsc --noEmit
      npm run build
      ```
      Plus a manual check list for the feature (exact steps for the owner to click through).
      
      ### 8.3 Task report format
      ```
      TASK: <ID + name>
      STATUS: done | blocked | partial
      FILES CHANGED: <list>
      NEW ENV VARS / DEPENDENCIES: <list or none>
      HOW TO TEST: <numbered manual steps>
      VERIFICATION RESULT: <commands run + pass/fail>
      KNOWN ISSUES / DECISIONS: <short>
      SUGGESTED COMMIT MESSAGE: <conventional commit>
      ```
      
      ### 8.4 Git conventions
      - Work on a branch per feature: `feat/<id>-<slug>`, `fix/...`, `chore/...`.
      - Conventional Commits: `feat(storefront): add variant selector (C4)`.
      - Do not commit: `.env`, `node_modules`, build output, local DB dumps.
      - Propose a commit after each verified task; do not squash unrelated work together.
      
      ### 8.5 Failure protocol
      - Error → read full message → check docs/types/existing code → fix.
      - Same error twice → STOP. Report: exact error, what you tried, your hypothesis, and the options you see.
      - Never respond to a failure by deleting and regenerating large parts of working code.
      - Never disable lint/type checks or tests to make something pass.
      
      ---
      
      ## 9. ROADMAP (execute in order)
      
      ### PHASE 0 — Foundation
      **Tasks**
      - P0.1 Inspect starter; produce report (structure, versions, included integrations, missing items vs this spec).
      - P0.2 Make backend + storefront run locally from clean clone; document exact commands in `docs/SETUP.md`.
      - P0.3 Add/verify `docker-compose.yml` (Postgres, Redis; Meilisearch optional now).
      - P0.4 Add `.env.template` files; ensure `.gitignore` covers secrets.
      - P0.5 Remove or rename starter placeholder branding; set store name/metadata via env/config.
      - P0.6 Add CI skeleton: install, lint, typecheck, build for both apps.
      
      **Exit criteria:** fresh clone + `docs/SETUP.md` → both apps run; CI green.
      
      ### PHASE 1 — Core Store MVP
      **Tasks:** seed data (§5.6) → C1–C5 → K1–K5 → A1–A2 → responsive + states pass.
      
      **Exit criteria:** In test mode, a new visitor can: browse, pick a variant, add to cart, check out as guest with `4242 4242 4242 4242`, see confirmation; register, buy again, see both orders in history; admin sees the orders and can fulfill one. No console errors; `npm run build` passes on both apps.
      
      ### PHASE 2 — Commerce Completeness
      **Tasks:** E1–E3 → K6, K7 → A3, A4 → C6, C7 → SEO baseline (§4) → sitemap/robots/JSON-LD.
      
      **Exit criteria:** emails delivered in test; promo code works; search returns typo-tolerant results; reset-password flow works; structured data validates.
      
      ### PHASE 3 — Differentiators & Polish
      **Tasks:** implement ≥2 options from §5.5 (start with Reviews) → accessibility pass → performance pass (Lighthouse Performance/Accessibility/SEO ≥ 90 on home, listing, product) → dark mode (optional).
      
      **Exit criteria:** custom modules have tests; admin extension works; Lighthouse targets met.
      
      ### PHASE 4 — Testing & Deployment
      **Tasks:**
      - P4.1 Backend tests for custom modules/workflows/routes.
      - P4.2 Playwright E2E: (1) guest purchase, (2) register+login+order history, (3) search, (4) failed payment.
      - P4.3 CI runs lint, types, tests, build; E2E on main or nightly.
      - P4.4 Production config: backend (server + worker mode if applicable per Medusa docs), DB migrations on deploy, Redis, S3 storage, CORS, Stripe webhook URL, domains.
      - P4.5 Deploy storefront to Vercel; backend to chosen host; run production seed; smoke-test full purchase.
      - P4.6 Write `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` with exact steps and a rollback note.
      
      **Exit criteria:** live URLs work end-to-end in Stripe test mode.
      
      ### PHASE 5 — Documentation
      **Tasks:** generate `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (diagram + module/workflow/subscriber inventory), `docs/DECISIONS.md` (key choices and why), `docs/TESTING.md`, and a **separate human-facing `README.human.md`** (pitch, screenshots placeholders, live links, setup, features). Do this only when asked.
      
      ---
      
      ## 10. ARCHITECTURE REFERENCE
      
      ```
      Browser → Next.js Storefront (Vercel)
                    │  Medusa JS SDK (Store API, publishable key)
                    ▼
               Medusa Backend (Node) ──► PostgreSQL
                    │                 ──► Redis (events, workflows, cache)
                    │                 ──► Stripe (payments; webhook → backend)
                    │                 ──► Resend (notifications)
                    │                 ──► Meilisearch (search index)
                    │                 ──► S3/R2 (files)
               Medusa Admin Dashboard (served by backend at /app)
      ```
      
      **Checkout sequence (must be preserved):**
      1. Create/retrieve cart (region-aware) → add line items.
      2. Set email + shipping/billing address.
      3. List and set shipping method.
      4. Initiate payment session (Stripe) → get `client_secret`.
      5. Confirm payment client-side with Stripe Elements.
      6. Complete cart server-side → order created.
      7. `order.placed` event → subscriber sends confirmation email.
      8. Stripe webhook acts as an idempotent safety net.
      
      **Event → handler map (target):**
      | Event | Handler |
      |-------|---------|
      | `order.placed` | send confirmation email |
      | `product.created/updated/deleted` | update Meilisearch index |
      | `fulfillment.created` (or shipment event per docs) | send shipment email |
      | `auth.password_reset` | send reset email |
      
      (Verify exact event names against Medusa docs/installed version before implementing.)
      
      ---
      
      ## 11. CODE QUALITY STANDARDS
      
      - TypeScript `strict`; no `any` unless justified in a comment.
      - Validate all external input (API bodies, query params) with Zod.
      - Small functions, descriptive names, no dead code, no commented-out blocks.
      - Handle and log errors; never swallow them silently. Side-effect failures (email, search) must not break core commerce flows.
      - No secrets, tokens, or personal data in logs.
      - Prefer existing utilities/components over new ones. Keep UI components reusable and in the storefront's `modules/` convention.
      - Comments explain *why*, not *what*.
      
      ---
      
      ## 12. SECURITY & PERFORMANCE CHECKLIST (apply continuously)
      
      - CORS restricted to known origins in production.
      - Secure cookies, strong `JWT_SECRET`/`COOKIE_SECRET` in production.
      - Stripe webhook signature verified.
      - Authenticated routes check customer ownership of resources (orders, addresses, reviews).
      - `npm audit` clean of high/critical issues (or documented).
      - Images optimized; product pages cached/revalidated sensibly; avoid N+1 API calls on listing pages.
      
      ---
      
      ## 13. DEFINITION OF DONE (project)
      
      - [ ] All 🟢 features pass AC.
      - [ ] Phase 1–4 exit criteria met.
      - [ ] CI green; tests cover custom modules and the main purchase flow.
      - [ ] Lighthouse ≥ 90 (Performance, Accessibility, SEO) on key pages.
      - [ ] Deployed; live full purchase works in Stripe test mode.
      - [ ] `.env.template`, `docs/SETUP.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` are accurate.
      - [ ] No secrets in repo history.
      
      ---

import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server"

const BACKEND_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL
const PUBLISHABLE_API_KEY = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDUSA_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
const DEFAULT_REGION = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_REGION || "dk"

const regionMapCache = {
  regionMap: new Map<string, HttpTypes.StoreRegion>(),
  regionMapUpdated: Date.now(),
}

async function getRegionMap(cacheId: string) {
  const { regionMap, regionMapUpdated } = regionMapCache

  if (!BACKEND_URL) {
    throw new Error(
      "Middleware.ts: Error fetching regions. Did you set up regions in your Medusa Admin and define a NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL environment variable."
    )
  }

  if (
    !regionMap.keys().next().value ||
    regionMapUpdated < Date.now() - 3600 * 1000
  ) {
    // Fetch regions from Medusa. We can't use the JS client here because middleware is running on Edge and the client needs a Node environment.
    const response = await fetch(`${BACKEND_URL}/store/regions`, {
      method: "GET",
      headers: {
        "x-publishable-api-key": PUBLISHABLE_API_KEY!,
      },
      next: {
        revalidate: 3600,
        tags: [`regions-${cacheId}`],
      },
      cache: "force-cache",
    })

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Backend returned ${response.status}`)
    }

    const json = await response.json()

    const { regions } = json

    if (!regions?.length) {
      return new Map<string, HttpTypes.StoreRegion>()
    }

    // Create a map of country codes to regions.
    regions.forEach((region: HttpTypes.StoreRegion) => {
      region.countries?.forEach((c) => {
        regionMapCache.regionMap.set(c.iso_2 ?? "", region)
      })
    })

    regionMapCache.regionMapUpdated = Date.now()
  }

  return regionMapCache.regionMap
}

{
  "path": "/tmp/devcart-responsive.mjs",
  "instructions": "Headless Chrome CDP check for horizontal overflow and section presence on the homepage at three widths.",
  "content": "// Verifies the DevCart homepage at the project's three reference widths using\n// raw CDP over Node's built-in WebSocket (no extra dependencies).\nimport { spawn } from \"node:child_process\"\n\nconst URL_TO_CHECK = process.argv[2] ?? \"http://localhost:8000/dk\"\nconst PORT = 9333\n\nconst chrome = spawn(\n  process.env.CHROME_BIN ?? \"google-chrome\",\n  [\n    \"--headless=new\",\n    \"--no-sandbox\",\n    \"--disable-gpu\",\n    \"--disable-dev-shm-usage\",\n    `--remote-debugging-port=${PORT}`,\n    \"about:blank\",\n  ],\n  { stdio: \"ignore\" }\n)\n\nconst sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms))\n\nasync function waitForTarget() {\n  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {\n    try {\n      const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)\n      const targets = await res.json()\n      const page = targets.find((t) => t.type === \"page\")\n      if (page?.webSocketDebuggerUrl) return page.webSocketDebuggerUrl\n    } catch {\n      // browser not up yet\n    }\n    await sleep(250)\n  }\n  throw new Error(\"Chrome DevTools endpoint never became ready\")\n}\n\nconst wsUrl = await waitForTarget()\nconst ws = new WebSocket(wsUrl)\nawait new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n  ws.onopen = resolve\n  ws.onerror = reject\n})\n\nlet nextId = 1\nconst pending = new Map()\nws.onmessage = (event) => {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data)\n  if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) {\n    const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(msg.id)\n    pending.delete(msg.id)\n    msg.error ? reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error))) : resolve(msg.result)\n  }\n}\n\nconst send = (method, params = {}) =>\n  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    const id = nextId++\n    pending.set(id, { resolve, reject })\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }))\n  })\n\nconst evaluate = async (expression) => {\n  const { result } = await send(\"Runtime.evaluate\", {\n    expression,\n    returnByValue: true,\n    awaitPromise: true,\n  })\n  return result.value\n}\n\nawait send(\"Page.enable\")\nawait send(\"Runtime.enable\")\n\nconst widths = [360, 768, 1280]\nconst report = []\n\nfor (const width of widths) {\n  await send(\"Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride\", {\n    width,\n    height: 900,\n    deviceScaleFactor: 1,\n    mobile: width < 768,\n  })\n  await send(\"Page.navigate\", { url: URL_TO_CHECK })\n  await sleep(4000)\n\n  const data = await evaluate(`(() => {\n    const overflow = [...document.querySelectorAll(\"body *\")]\n      .filter((el) => el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 1 && el.clientWidth > 0)\n      .slice(0, 5)\n      .map((el) => el.tagName.toLowerCase() + \".\" + String(el.className).slice(0, 60))\n    const rails = document.querySelectorAll('section[aria-labelledby^=\"collection-\"]')\n    const cards = rails[0] ? rails[0].querySelectorAll(\"li\").length : 0\n    return {\n      docScrollWidth: document.documentElement.scrollWidth,\n      innerWidth: window.innerWidth,\n      headings: [...document.querySelectorAll(\"h1,h2\")].map((h) => h.textContent.trim()),\n      categoryLinks: [...document.querySelectorAll('a[href*=\"/categories/\"]')].length,\n      collectionLinks: [...document.querySelectorAll('a[href*=\"/collections/\"]')].length,\n      rails: rails.length,\n      cardsInFirstRail: cards,\n      overflow,\n    }\n  })()`)\n\n  report.push({ width, ...data })\n}\n\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(report, null, 2))\nws.close()\nchrome.kill(\"SIGKILL\")\n"
}

- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/store/components/store-hits/index.tsx
  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import type { Hit } from "instantsearch.js"
      import { useEffect, useRef } from "react"
      import { useHits, useInstantSearch } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import useSearchSettled from "@lib/hooks/use-search-settled"
      import LocalizedClientLink from "@modules/common/components/localized-client-link"
      import { Text } from "@modules/common/components/ui"
      import Thumbnail from "@modules/products/components/thumbnail"
      import SkeletonProductGrid from "@modules/skeletons/templates/skeleton-product-grid"
      import SearchPagination from "./pagination"
      import HitPrice, { HitPricing } from "./price"
      
      type ProductHit = Hit<
        {
          title: string | null
          handle: string | null
          thumbnail: string | null
        } & HitPricing
      >
      
      type StoreHitsProps = {
        hitsPerPage: number
        currencyCode: string
      }
      
      const StoreHits = ({ hitsPerPage, currencyCode }: StoreHitsProps) => {
        const { items } = useHits<ProductHit>()
        const { status, error, indexUiState } = useInstantSearch()
        const { isSearching, hasNoResultsYet } = useSearchSettled()
      
        const { page, ...refinements } = indexUiState
        const currentPage = page ?? 1
        const refinementKey = JSON.stringify(refinements)
      
        const settled = useRef({ page: currentPage, refinementKey })
      
        useEffect(() => {
          if (!isSearching) {
            settled.current = { page: currentPage, refinementKey }
          }
        }, [isSearching, currentPage, refinementKey])
      
        const isPagingOnly =
          refinementKey === settled.current.refinementKey &&
          currentPage !== settled.current.page
      
        const showSkeleton = hasNoResultsYet || (isSearching && isPagingOnly)
      
        if (status === "error") {
          return (
            <Text
              className="py-16 text-center text-ui-fg-error"
              data-testid="products-error"
            >
              Couldn&apos;t load products
              {error?.message ? `: ${error.message}` : "."}
            </Text>
          )
        }
      
        return (
          <>
            {showSkeleton ? (
              <SkeletonProductGrid numberOfProducts={hitsPerPage} />
            ) : !items.length ? (
              <Text
                className="py-16 text-center text-ui-fg-subtle"
                data-testid="no-products"
              >
                No products matched these filters.
              </Text>
            ) : (
              <ul
                className="grid grid-cols-2 w-full small:grid-cols-3 medium:grid-cols-4 gap-x-6 gap-y-8"
                data-testid="products-list"
              >
                {items.map((hit) =>
                  hit.handle ? (
                    <li key={hit.objectID}>
                      <LocalizedClientLink
                        href={`/products/${hit.handle}`}
                        className="group"
                      >
                        <div data-testid="product-wrapper">
                          <Thumbnail thumbnail={hit.thumbnail} size="full" />
                          <div className="flex txt-compact-medium mt-4 justify-between">
                            <Text
                              className="text-ui-fg-subtle"
                              data-testid="product-title"
                            >
                              {hit.title}
                            </Text>
                            <HitPrice hit={hit} currencyCode={currencyCode} />
                          </div>
                        </div>
                      </LocalizedClientLink>
                    </li>
                  ) : null
                )}
              </ul>
            )}
            <SearchPagination />
          </>
        )
      }
      
      export default StoreHits

      "use client"
      
      import { useSortBy } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import FilterRadioGroup from "@modules/common/components/filter-radio-group"
      import {
        CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE,
        LABELS_ATTRIBUTE,
        getSortOptions,
      } from "./attributes"
      import CurrentRefinements from "./current-refinements"
      import OnSaleToggle from "./on-sale-toggle"
      import OptionRefinements from "./option-refinements"
      import PriceRange from "./price-range"
      import RefinementGroup from "./refinement-group"
      
      const SortProducts = ({ currencyCode }: { currencyCode: string }) => {
        const items = getSortOptions(currencyCode)
        const { currentRefinement, refine } = useSortBy({ items })
      
        return (
          <FilterRadioGroup
            title="Sort by"
            items={items}
            value={currentRefinement}
            handleChange={refine}
            data-testid="sort-by-container"
          />
        )
      }
      
      const StoreRefinements = ({ currencyCode }: { currencyCode: string }) => {
        return (
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-12 py-4 mb-8 small:px-0 pl-6 small:w-[250px] small:shrink-0 small:ml-[1.675rem]">
            <SortProducts currencyCode={currencyCode} />
            <CurrentRefinements currencyCode={currencyCode} />
            <OptionRefinements />
            <PriceRange currencyCode={currencyCode} />
            <OnSaleToggle currencyCode={currencyCode} />
            <RefinementGroup attribute={CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE} title="Category" />
            <RefinementGroup attribute={LABELS_ATTRIBUTE} title="Labels" />
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default StoreRefinements

- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/store/components/store-search-box/index.tsx
  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import { MagnifyingGlass, XMarkMini } from "@medusajs/icons"
      import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react"
      import { useSearchBox } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      const DEBOUNCE_MS = 250
      
      /**
       * Free-text search over the listing, refining the same InstantSearch state the
       * sidebar filters do. The input is held locally so typing stays responsive
       * while the query itself is debounced.
       */
      const StoreSearchBox = () => {
        const timer = useRef<number | undefined>(undefined)
      
        const queryHook = useCallback(
          (nextQuery: string, search: (value: string) => void) => {
            window.clearTimeout(timer.current)
            timer.current = window.setTimeout(() => search(nextQuery), DEBOUNCE_MS)
          },
          []
        )
      
        const { query, refine } = useSearchBox({ queryHook })
        const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState(query)
      
        useEffect(() => () => window.clearTimeout(timer.current), [])
      
        // Follow the query when it changes elsewhere — cleared with the filters, or
        // arriving from the URL on load, which `routing` restores after mount.
        useEffect(() => {
          setInputValue(query)
        }, [query])
      
        const clear = () => {
          window.clearTimeout(timer.current)
          setInputValue("")
          refine("")
        }
      
        return (
          <div className="mb-6 flex items-center gap-x-3 border-b border-ui-border-base">
            <MagnifyingGlass className="shrink-0 text-ui-fg-muted" />
            <input
              type="search"
              value={inputValue}
              onChange={(event) => {
                setInputValue(event.target.value)
                refine(event.target.value)
              }}
              placeholder="Search products"
              aria-label="Search products"
              className="txt-medium w-full bg-transparent py-3 text-ui-fg-base outline-none placeholder:text-ui-fg-muted [&::-webkit-search-cancel-button]:hidden"
              data-testid="store-search-input"
            />
            {inputValue && (
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={clear}
                aria-label="Clear search"
                className="shrink-0 text-ui-fg-muted hover:text-ui-fg-base"
                data-testid="store-search-clear"
              >
                <XMarkMini />
              </button>
            )}
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default StoreSearchBox
      
  referencedBy: {}

      import {
        createInstantSearchAdapter,
        type MedusaSdkLike,
      } from "@medusajs/instantsearch-adapter"
      
      import { sdk } from "@lib/config"
      
      export const PRODUCT_INDEX_NAME = "product"
      
      /**
       * The currencies the product index holds prices in, one field set each. Keep
       * in sync with `PRICE_CURRENCIES` in the backend's `src/search/product.ts`.
       */
      export const SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES = ["eur", "usd"]
      
      export type PriceField =
        | "min_price"
        | "max_price"
        | "original_price"
        | "on_sale"
      
      /**
       * The indexed currency to read prices in for a region. A region whose currency
       * the index doesn't hold falls back to the first one, so the listing still
       * shows a price rather than none.
       */
      export const indexedCurrency = (currencyCode: string) => {
        const code = currencyCode.toLowerCase()
        return SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES.includes(code)
          ? code
          : SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES[0]
      }
      
      export const priceAttribute = (field: PriceField, currencyCode: string) =>
        `${field}_${indexedCurrency(currencyCode)}`
      
      /**
       * Shared by the navbar search drawer and the store listing. An empty query
       * searches rather than short-circuiting, which is what the listing needs to
       * show every product before anything is refined.
       */
      export const { searchClient } = createInstantSearchAdapter({
        sdk: sdk as unknown as MedusaSdkLike,
        path: "/store/search",
        additionalSearchParameters: {
          search_options: {
            match_strategy: "last",
          },
        },
        // Range widgets read `facets_stats`, which the adapter only produces for
        // fields listed here. The price fields are declared with a `stats` facet on
        // the index, which is what makes the stats available at all.
        numericAttributes: SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES.flatMap((currency) => [
          `min_price_${currency}`,
          `max_price_${currency}`,
        ]),
      })

  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import { usePathname, useRouter, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation"
      import { useCallback, useMemo } from "react"
      
      import {
        OPTION_VALUE_QUERY_KEY,
        parseOptionValueIds,
      } from "@lib/util/product-option-filters"
      import OptionsPicker from "./options-picker"
      import SortProducts, { SortOptions } from "./sort-products"
      
      type RefinementListProps = {
        sortBy: SortOptions
        search?: boolean
        hideOptionsPicker?: boolean
        "data-testid"?: string
      }
      
      const RefinementList = ({
        sortBy,
        hideOptionsPicker = false,
        "data-testid": dataTestId,
      }: RefinementListProps) => {
        const router = useRouter()
        const pathname = usePathname()
        const searchParams = useSearchParams()
      
        const updateQueryParams = useCallback(
          (updater: (params: URLSearchParams) => void) => {
            const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString())
            updater(params)
      
            params.delete("page")
      
            const queryString = params.toString()
            const currentQuery = searchParams.toString()
            const nextPath = queryString ? `${pathname}?${queryString}` : pathname
            const currentPath = currentQuery
              ? `${pathname}?${currentQuery}`
              : pathname
      
            if (nextPath !== currentPath) {
              router.push(nextPath)
            }
          },
          [pathname, router, searchParams]
        )
      
        const setQueryParams = (name: string, value: string) =>
          updateQueryParams((params) => params.set(name, value))
      
        const selectedOptionValueIds = useMemo(
          () => parseOptionValueIds(searchParams),
          [searchParams]
        )
      
        const setOptionValueIds = (valueIds: string[]) =>
          updateQueryParams((params) => {
            params.delete(OPTION_VALUE_QUERY_KEY)
            valueIds.forEach((valueId) =>
              params.append(OPTION_VALUE_QUERY_KEY, valueId)
            )
          })
      
        return (
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-12 py-4 mb-8 small:px-0 pl-6 small:min-w-[250px] small:ml-[1.675rem]">
            <SortProducts
              sortBy={sortBy}
              setQueryParams={setQueryParams}
              data-testid={dataTestId}
            />
            {!hideOptionsPicker && (
              <OptionsPicker
                selectedValueIds={selectedOptionValueIds}
                setOptionValueIds={setOptionValueIds}
              />
            )}
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default RefinementList
      
  referencedBy: {}

reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error))) : resolve(msg.result)\n  }\n}\nconst send = (method, params = {}) =>\n  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    const id = nextId++\n    pending.set(id, { resolve, reject })\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }))\n  })\n\nawait send(\"Page.enable\")\nawait send(\"Runtime.enable\")\nawait send(\"Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride\", {\n  width,\n  height: 900,\n  deviceScaleFactor: 1,\n  mobile: width < 768,\n})\nawait send(\"Page.navigate\", { url })\nawait sleep(wait)\n\nconst { result } = await send(\"Runtime.evaluate\", {\n  expression: readFileSync(exprFile, \"utf8\"),\n  returnByValue: true,\n  awaitPromise: true,\n})\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(result.value, null, 2))\n\nws.close()\nchrome.kill(\"SIGKILL\")\n"

- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/design-system/components/plate/index.tsx
  content: |
      import clsx from "clsx"
      import { forwardRef, HTMLAttributes } from "react"
      
      /*
       * A plate is the shell every product appears in: a square, hairline-bordered
       * block with no shadow and no rounding. Registration marks and overprint are
       * deferred polish (docs/DESIGN.md §5.1) — a plate must look finished without them.
       */
      export type PlateProps = HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> & {
        as?: "div" | "article" | "li"
      }
      
      const PlateRoot = forwardRef<HTMLElement, PlateProps>(
        ({ className, as = "article", children, ...props }, ref) => {
          // `as` lets a plate be a grid item (`li`) or a standalone block without
          // duplicating the styling; ElementType keeps the ref valid across both.
          const Component = as as React.ElementType
      
          return (
            <Component
              ref={ref}
              className={clsx(
                "relative flex w-full flex-col rounded-square border border-ink bg-stock",
                className
              )}
              {...props}
            >
              {children}
            </Component>
          )
        }
      )
      PlateRoot.displayName = "Plate"
      
      /** Fixed-ratio image well. Keeps every plate in a grid the same height. */
      const PlateMedia = ({ className, children, ...props }: HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>) => (
        <div
          className={clsx("relative aspect-square w-full overflow-hidden bg-ink/5", className)}
          {...props}
        >
          {children}
        </div>
      )
      
      /** Text block below the media. */
      const PlateBody = ({ className, ...props }: HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>) => (
        <div className={clsx("flex flex-col gap-2 border-t border-ink p-4", className)} {...props} />
      )
      
      /** Product name. Display voice, sentence case. */
      const PlateTitle = ({ className, ...props }: HTMLAttributes<HTMLHeadingElement>) => (
        <h3
          className={clsx("font-display text-lead font-semibold leading-tight text-ink", className)}
          {...props}
        />
      )
      
      /** Price. Mono, because it is machine data and must align across a grid. */
      const PlatePrice = ({ className, ...props }: HTMLAttributes<HTMLParagraphElement>) => (
        <p className={clsx("font-mono text-small text-ink", className)} {...props} />
      )
      
      /** Secondary facts: stock state, SKU, material. */
      const PlateMeta = ({ className, ...props }: HTMLAttributes<HTMLParagraphElement>) => (
        <p className={clsx("text-small text-ink", className)} {...props} />
      )
      
      export const Plate = Object.assign(PlateRoot, {
        Media: PlateMedia,
        Body: PlateBody,
        Title: PlateTitle,
        Price: PlatePrice,
        Meta: PlateMeta,
      })

        weight?: "hairline" | "heavy"

       * A horizontal rule is real structure in this design — it separates bands and

      export const Rule = forwardRef<HTMLHRElement, RuleProps>(

- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/design-system/components/button/index.tsx
  content: |
      import clsx from "clsx"
      import { ButtonHTMLAttributes, forwardRef } from "react"
      
      export type ButtonVariant = "primary" | "secondary"
      export type ButtonSize = "small" | "medium" | "large"
      
      export type ButtonProps = ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & {
        variant?: ButtonVariant
        size?: ButtonSize
        /** Blocks the button and shows a spinner without shifting the layout. */
        loading?: boolean
      }
      
      /*
       * Colour choices are fixed by the contrast rules in docs/DESIGN.md §2.1:
       * `stock` on `riso-blue` is 4.53:1, so that pairing is the only blue fill.
       * `ink` is never placed on `riso-blue` (3.21:1).
       */
      const VARIANTS: Record<ButtonVariant, string> = {
        primary:
          "bg-riso-blue text-stock border border-riso-blue hover:bg-ink hover:border-ink " +
          "disabled:bg-riso-blue/40 disabled:border-transparent disabled:text-stock/80",
        secondary:
          "bg-transparent text-ink border border-ink hover:bg-ink hover:text-stock " +
          "disabled:border-ink/30 disabled:text-ink/40 disabled:hover:bg-transparent disabled:hover:text-ink/40",
      }
      
      const SIZES: Record<ButtonSize, string> = {
        small: "h-9 px-3 text-small",
        medium: "h-11 px-5 text-body",
        large: "h-14 px-7 text-lead",
      }
      
      const BASE =
        "inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-square font-sans font-semibold " +
        "transition-colors duration-150 disabled:cursor-not-allowed"
      
      export const Button = forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(
        (
          { className, variant = "primary", size = "medium", loading, disabled, children, ...props },
          ref
        ) => {
          return (
            <button
              ref={ref}
              type={props.type ?? "button"}
              // aria-busy tells assistive tech the action is running; `disabled` alone
              // just looks inert.
              aria-busy={loading || undefined}
              disabled={disabled || loading}
              className={clsx(BASE, VARIANTS[variant], SIZES[size], className)}
              {...props}
            >
              {loading && (
                <span
                  aria-hidden="true"
                  className="h-4 w-4 shrink-0 animate-spin rounded-full border-2 border-current border-t-transparent motion-reduce:animate-none"
                />
              )}
              {children}
            </button>
          )
        }
      )
      
      Button.displayName = "Button"

  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import { usePagination } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import { clx } from "@modules/common/components/ui"
      
      const SearchPagination = () => {
        const { pages, currentRefinement, nbPages, refine } = usePagination({
          padding: 2,
        })
      
        if (nbPages <= 1) {
          return null
        }
      
        const renderPage = (page: number) => (
          <button
            key={page}
            className={clx("txt-xlarge-plus text-ui-fg-muted", {
              "text-ui-fg-base hover:text-ui-fg-subtle": page === currentRefinement,
            })}
            disabled={page === currentRefinement}
            onClick={() => refine(page)}
          >
            {page + 1}
          </button>
        )
      
        const renderEllipsis = (key: string) => (
          <span
            key={key}
            className="txt-xlarge-plus text-ui-fg-muted items-center cursor-default"
          >
            ...
          </span>
        )
      
        const lastPage = nbPages - 1
      
        return (
          <div className="flex justify-center w-full mt-12">
            <div className="flex gap-3 items-end" data-testid="product-pagination">
              {!pages.includes(0) && renderPage(0)}
              {!pages.includes(0) && !pages.includes(1) && renderEllipsis("start")}
              {pages.map(renderPage)}
              {!pages.includes(lastPage) &&
                !pages.includes(lastPage - 1) &&
                renderEllipsis("end")}
              {!pages.includes(lastPage) && renderPage(lastPage)}
            </div>
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default SearchPagination
      
  referencedBy: {}

  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import { indexedCurrency, priceAttribute } from "@lib/search-client"
      import { convertToLocale } from "@lib/util/money"
      import { Text, clx } from "@modules/common/components/ui"
      
      /** The per-currency price fields a hit may carry, e.g. `min_price_eur`. */
      export type HitPricing = Record<string, unknown>
      
      type HitPriceProps = {
        hit: HitPricing
        currencyCode: string
      }
      
      const amount = (value: unknown) => (typeof value === "number" ? value : null)
      
      const HitPrice = ({ hit, currencyCode }: HitPriceProps) => {
        const currency_code = indexedCurrency(currencyCode)
        const min_price = amount(hit[priceAttribute("min_price", currencyCode)])
        const max_price = amount(hit[priceAttribute("max_price", currencyCode)])
        const original_price = amount(
          hit[priceAttribute("original_price", currencyCode)]
        )
        const on_sale = hit[priceAttribute("on_sale", currencyCode)] === true
      
        if (min_price === null) {
          return null
        }
      
        const format = (value: number) =>
          convertToLocale({ amount: value, currency_code })
      
        const max = max_price ?? min_price
        const isRange = max > min_price
      
        return (
          <div className="flex items-center gap-x-2" data-testid="product-price">
            {!isRange && on_sale && original_price !== null && (
              <Text
                className="line-through text-ui-fg-muted"
                data-testid="original-price"
              >
                {format(original_price)}
              </Text>
            )}
            <Text
              className={clx("text-ui-fg-muted", {
                "text-ui-tag-red-text": on_sale,
              })}
              data-testid="price"
            >
              {isRange ? `${format(min_price)} - ${format(max)}` : format(min_price)}
            </Text>
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default HitPrice

  content: |
      import { notFound } from "next/navigation"
      import { Suspense } from "react"
      
      import InteractiveLink from "@modules/common/components/interactive-link"
      import SkeletonProductGrid from "@modules/skeletons/templates/skeleton-product-grid"
      import RefinementList from "@modules/store/components/refinement-list"
      import { SortOptions } from "@modules/store/components/refinement-list/sort-products"
      import PaginatedProducts from "@modules/store/templates/paginated-products"
      import LocalizedClientLink from "@modules/common/components/localized-client-link"
      import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
      import { OptionValueIds } from "@lib/util/product-option-filters"
      
      export default function CategoryTemplate({
        category,
        sortBy,
        page,
        countryCode,
        optionValueIds,
      }: {
        category: HttpTypes.StoreProductCategory
        sortBy?: SortOptions
        page?: string
        countryCode: string
        optionValueIds?: OptionValueIds
      }) {
        const pageNumber = page ? parseInt(page) : 1
        const sort = sortBy || "created_at"
      
        if (!category || !countryCode) notFound()
      
        const parents = [] as HttpTypes.StoreProductCategory[]
      
        const getParents = (category: HttpTypes.StoreProductCategory) => {
          if (category.parent_category) {
            parents.push(category.parent_category)
            getParents(category.parent_category)
          }
        }
      
        getParents(category)
      
        return (
          <div
            className="flex flex-col small:flex-row small:items-start py-6 content-container"
            data-testid="category-container"
          >
            <RefinementList
              sortBy={sort}
              data-testid="sort-by-container"
              hideOptionsPicker
            />
            <div className="w-full">
              <div className="flex flex-row mb-8 text-2xl-semi gap-4">
                {parents &&
                  parents.map((parent) => (
                    <span key={parent.id} className="text-ui-fg-subtle">
                      <LocalizedClientLink
                        className="mr-4 hover:text-black"
                        href={`/categories/${parent.handle}`}
                        data-testid="sort-by-link"
                      >
                        {parent.name}
                      </LocalizedClientLink>
                      /
                    </span>
                  ))}
                <h1 data-testid="category-page-title">{category.name}</h1>
              </div>
              {category.description && (
                <div className="mb-8 text-base-regular">
                  <p>{category.description}</p>
                </div>
              )}
              {category.category_children && (
                <div className="mb-8 text-base-large">
                  <ul className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-2">
                    {category.category_children?.map((c) => (
                      <li key={c.id}>
                        <InteractiveLink href={`/categories/${c.handle}`}>
                          {c.name}
                        </InteractiveLink>
                      </li>
                    ))}
                  </ul>
                </div>
              )}
              <Suspense
                fallback={
                  <SkeletonProductGrid
                    numberOfProducts={category.products?.length ?? 8}
                  />
                }
              >
                <PaginatedProducts
                  sortBy={sort}
                  page={pageNumber}
                  categoryId={category.id}
                  countryCode={countryCode}
                  optionValueIds={optionValueIds}
                />
              </Suspense>
            </div>
          </div>
        )
      }
      
  referencedBy: {}
