- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/store/components/store-hits/index.tsx
  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import type { Hit } from "instantsearch.js"
      import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react"
      import { useHits, useInstantSearch } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import useSearchSettled from "@lib/hooks/use-search-settled"
      import { Button } from "@modules/design-system"
      import ProductCard from "@modules/products/components/product-card"
      import SkeletonProductGrid from "@modules/skeletons/templates/skeleton-product-grid"
      import SearchPagination from "./pagination"
      import HitPrice, { HitPricing } from "./price"
      
      type ProductHit = Hit<
        {
          title: string | null
          handle: string | null
          thumbnail: string | null
        } & HitPricing
      >
      
      type StoreHitsProps = {
        hitsPerPage: number
        currencyCode: string
      }
      
      /**
       * How long the grid waits for a first response before calling it a failure. A
       * search that only stalls keeps InstantSearch in a loading state with no error,
       * so the timeout is what turns "nothing ever arrives" into something the
       * customer can act on.
       */
      const RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000
      
      const StoreHits = ({ hitsPerPage, currencyCode }: StoreHitsProps) => {
        const { items } = useHits<ProductHit>()
        const { status, error, indexUiState, refresh } = useInstantSearch()
        const { isSearching, hasNoResultsYet } = useSearchSettled()
        const [timedOut, setTimedOut] = useState(false)
      
        const { page, ...refinements } = indexUiState
        const currentPage = page ?? 1
        const refinementKey = JSON.stringify(refinements)
      
        const settled = useRef({ page: currentPage, refinementKey })
      
        useEffect(() => {
          if (!isSearching) {
            settled.current = { page: currentPage, refinementKey }
          }
        }, [isSearching, currentPage, refinementKey])
      
        /*
         * Time the wait from when a query starts, not from the last status change: a
         * client that keeps retrying a dead endpoint keeps emitting status updates,
         * and a resettable timeout would never fire. Answering the query clears the
         * guard so the next failure gets its own countdown.
         */
        useEffect(() => {
          if (!hasNoResultsYet) {
            setTimedOut(false)
            return
          }
      
          const startedAt = Date.now()
          const timer = window.setInterval(() => {
            if (Date.now() - startedAt >= RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS) {
              window.clearInterval(timer)
              setTimedOut(true)
            }
          }, 500)
      
          return () => window.clearInterval(timer)
        }, [hasNoResultsYet, refinementKey])
      
        const isPagingOnly =
          refinementKey === settled.current.refinementKey &&
          currentPage !== settled.current.page
      
        const showSkeleton = !timedOut && (hasNoResultsYet || (isSearching && isPagingOnly))
      
        if (status === "error" || timedOut) {
          return (
            <div
              role="alert"
              className="flex flex-col items-start gap-4 border-y border-ink/20 py-12"
              data-testid="products-error"
            >
              <p className="text-ink">
                {status === "error" && error?.message
                  ? `Couldn't load products: ${error.message}`
                  : "Couldn't load products. The search service did not respond."}
              </p>
              <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => refresh()}>
                Try again
              </Button>
            </div>
          )
        }
      
        return (
          <>
            {showSkeleton ? (
              <SkeletonProductGrid numberOfProducts={hitsPerPage} />
            ) : !items.length ? (
              <p
                className="border-y border-ink/20 py-16 text-center text-ink/75"
                data-testid="no-products"
              >
                No products matched these filters.
              </p>
            ) : (
              <ul
                className="grid w-full grid-cols-2 gap-x-4 gap-y-8 small:grid-cols-3 small:gap-x-6"
                data-testid="products-list"
              >
                {items.map((hit) =>
                  hit.handle ? (
                    <ProductCard
                      key={hit.objectID}
                      as="li"
                      href={`/products/${hit.handle}`}
                      title={hit.title ?? "Untitled product"}
                      thumbnail={hit.thumbnail}
                      price={<HitPrice hit={hit} currencyCode={currencyCode} />}
                    />
                  ) : null
                )}
              </ul>
            )}
            <SearchPagination />
          </>
        )
      }
      
      export default StoreHits
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/store/components/store-hits/price.tsx
  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import { indexedCurrency, priceAttribute } from "@lib/search-client"
      import { convertToLocale } from "@lib/util/money"
      
      /** The per-currency price fields a hit may carry, e.g. `min_price_eur`. */
      export type HitPricing = Record<string, unknown>
      
      type HitPriceProps = {
        hit: HitPricing
        currencyCode: string
      }
      
      const amount = (value: unknown) => (typeof value === "number" ? value : null)
      
      /**
       * Prices off the search hit. Variants with different prices make the card show
       * a range, and a struck-through original price is the only sale marker the
       * design allows at this size (docs/DESIGN.md §2.1 keeps riso-pink for display type).
       */
      const HitPrice = ({ hit, currencyCode }: HitPriceProps) => {
        const currency_code = indexedCurrency(currencyCode)
        const min_price = amount(hit[priceAttribute("min_price", currencyCode)])
        const max_price = amount(hit[priceAttribute("max_price", currencyCode)])
        const original_price = amount(
          hit[priceAttribute("original_price", currencyCode)]
        )
        const on_sale = hit[priceAttribute("on_sale", currencyCode)] === true
      
        if (min_price === null) {
          return null
        }
      
        const format = (value: number) =>
          convertToLocale({ amount: value, currency_code })
      
        const max = max_price ?? min_price
        const isRange = max > min_price
      
        return (
          <span
            className="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-x-2"
            data-testid="product-price"
          >
            {!isRange && on_sale && original_price !== null && (
              <s className="text-ink/60" data-testid="original-price">
                {format(original_price)}
              </s>
            )}
            <span data-testid="price">
              {isRange ? `${format(min_price)} - ${format(max)}` : format(min_price)}
            </span>
          </span>
        )
      }
      
      export default HitPrice
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/store/components/store-refinements/index.tsx
  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import { useSortBy } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import FilterRadioGroup from "@modules/common/components/filter-radio-group"
      import {
        CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE,
        LABELS_ATTRIBUTE,
        getSortOptions,
      } from "./attributes"
      import CurrentRefinements from "./current-refinements"
      import OnSaleToggle from "./on-sale-toggle"
      import OptionRefinements from "./option-refinements"
      import PriceRange from "./price-range"
      import RefinementGroup from "./refinement-group"
      
      const SortProducts = ({ currencyCode }: { currencyCode: string }) => {
        const items = getSortOptions(currencyCode)
        const { currentRefinement, refine } = useSortBy({ items })
      
        return (
          <FilterRadioGroup
            title="Sort by"
            items={items}
            value={currentRefinement}
            handleChange={refine}
            data-testid="sort-by-container"
          />
        )
      }
      
      /*
       * The listing's sort and filters, as one labelled column beside the grid. Each
       * group is separated by a hairline rather than a card, and a group with nothing
       * to offer (no facets, no price spread) removes itself.
       */
      const StoreRefinements = ({ currencyCode }: { currencyCode: string }) => {
        return (
          <aside
            aria-label="Sort and filter"

- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/store/components/store-refinements/current-refinements.tsx
  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import { XMarkMini } from "@medusajs/icons"
      import { useClearRefinements, useCurrentRefinements } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import { indexedCurrency, priceAttribute } from "@lib/search-client"
      import { convertToLocale } from "@lib/util/money"
      import {
        CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE,
        LABELS_ATTRIBUTE,
        OPTION_VALUES_ATTRIBUTE,
      } from "./attributes"
      
      type Refinement = ReturnType<
        typeof useCurrentRefinements
      >["items"][number]["refinements"][number]
      
      /**
       * What a single refinement reads as on its chip. The raw label is the facet
       * value, which is the option's `Size:M` form for options and a bare `true` for
       * the on-sale toggle — neither says what it filters on out of context.
       */
      function refinementLabel(refinement: Refinement, currencyCode: string) {
        const { attribute, label, value, operator } = refinement
      
        if (attribute === OPTION_VALUES_ATTRIBUTE) {
          const separator = String(value).indexOf(":")
      
          return separator < 1
            ? label
            : `${String(value).slice(0, separator)}: ${String(value).slice(
                separator + 1
              )}`
        }
      
        if (attribute === priceAttribute("on_sale", currencyCode)) {
          return "On sale"
        }
      
        if (attribute === priceAttribute("min_price", currencyCode)) {
          const amount = convertToLocale({
            amount: Number(value),
            currency_code: indexedCurrency(currencyCode),
            maximumFractionDigits: 0,
          })
      
          return operator === "<=" || operator === "<"
            ? `Up to ${amount}`
            : `From ${amount}`
        }
      
        if (attribute === CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE) {
          return `Category: ${label}`
        }
      
        if (attribute === LABELS_ATTRIBUTE) {
          return `Label: ${label}`
        }
      
        return label
      }
      
      /**
       * Every active refinement as a chip that drops it, above the filters that set
       * them. The free-text query is excluded by the connector's own defaults, so
       * only what the sidebar controls shows up here.
       */
      const CurrentRefinements = ({ currencyCode }: { currencyCode: string }) => {
        const { items, refine } = useCurrentRefinements()
        const { canRefine: canClearAll, refine: clearAll } = useClearRefinements()
      
        const refinements = items.flatMap((item) => item.refinements)
      
        if (!refinements.length) {
          return null
        }
      
        return (
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-2" data-testid="current-refinements">
            <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
              <span className="text-small font-semibold text-ink">
                Applied filters
              </span>
              {canClearAll && (
                <button
                  type="button"
                  onClick={clearAll}
                  className="text-small text-riso-blue underline decoration-1 underline-offset-4 hover:text-ink"
                  data-testid="clear-refinements"
                >
                  Clear all
                </button>
              )}
            </div>
      
            <ul className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
              {refinements.map((refinement) => {
                const label = refinementLabel(refinement, currencyCode)
      
                return (
                  <li
                    key={`${refinement.attribute}:${refinement.operator ?? ""}:${
                      refinement.value
                    }`}
                  >
                    <button
                      type="button"
                      onClick={() => refine(refinement)}
                      aria-label={`Remove filter ${label}`}
                      className="flex min-h-10 items-center gap-1.5 border border-ink/40 px-3 text-small text-ink transition-colors hover:border-ink"
                      data-testid="remove-refinement"
                    >
                      {label}
                      <XMarkMini className="text-ink/60" />
                    </button>
                  </li>
                )
              })}
            </ul>
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default CurrentRefinements
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/design-system/components/input/index.tsx
  content: |
      import clsx from "clsx"
      import { forwardRef, InputHTMLAttributes } from "react"
      
      export type InputProps = Omit<InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>, "id"> & {
        /** Required: the label is associated with the field through this id. */
        id: string
        label: string
        /** Guidance shown below the field when there is no error. */
        hint?: string
        /**
         * Error message. Rendered in ink, not pink: `riso-pink` is 3.13:1 on `stock`
         * (docs/DESIGN.md §2.1) so it may only mark, never carry words. The pink
         * border is the marker; this text says what went wrong.
         */
        error?: string
      }
      
      export const Input = forwardRef<HTMLInputElement, InputProps>(
        ({ className, id, label, hint, error, disabled, ...props }, ref) => {
          const hintId = hint ? `${id}-hint` : undefined
          const errorId = error ? `${id}-error` : undefined
          const describedBy = errorId ?? hintId
      
          return (
            <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
              <label htmlFor={id} className="text-small font-semibold text-ink">
                {label}
              </label>
      
              <input
                ref={ref}
                id={id}
                disabled={disabled}
                aria-invalid={error ? true : undefined}
                aria-describedby={describedBy}
                className={clsx(
                  "h-11 w-full rounded-square border bg-stock px-3 text-body text-ink",
                  "placeholder:text-ink/60",
                  "disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:border-ink/30 disabled:bg-ink/5 disabled:text-ink/40",
                  error ? "border-riso-pink" : "border-ink",
                  className
                )}
                {...props}
              />
      
              {hint && !error && (
                <p id={hintId} className="text-small text-ink">
                  {hint}
                </p>
              )}
      
              {error && (
                <p id={errorId} className="text-small text-ink">
                  {error}
                </p>
              )}
            </div>
          )
        }
      )
      
      Input.displayName = "Input"
      
  referencedBy: {}

  content: |
      (async () => {
        // Runs right after navigation starts, so it can observe the first paint.
        const seen = { loader: false, loaderText: null, at: null }
        const started = performance.now()
        for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
          const loader = document.querySelector('[data-testid="products-list-loader"]')
          if (loader) {
            seen.loader = true
            seen.at = Math.round(performance.now() - started)
            seen.loaderText = loader.children.length + " placeholder plates"
            break
          }
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100))
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < 80; i++) {
          if (document.querySelector('[data-testid="products-list"]')) break
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100))
        }
        const cardCount = document.querySelector('[data-testid="products-list"]')?.children.length ?? 0
        const columns =
          document.querySelector('[data-testid="products-list"]') &&
          getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-testid="products-list"]'))
            .gridTemplateColumns.split(" ").length
        return {
          sawLoader: seen.loader,
          loaderAtMs: seen.at,
          loaderText: seen.loaderText,
          finalCardCount: cardCount,
          columns,
          docScrollWidth: document.documentElement.scrollWidth,
          innerWidth: window.innerWidth,
        }
      })()
      
  referencedBy: {}

- path: /tmp/cdp.mjs
  content: |
      // Usage: node /tmp/cdp.mjs <url> <exprFile> [width] [waitMs]
      import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
      import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
      
      const [url, exprFile, widthArg, waitArg, blockArg] = process.argv.slice(2)
      const width = Number(widthArg ?? 1280)
      const wait = Number(waitArg ?? 6000)
      const PORT = 9335
      
      const chrome = spawn(
        process.env.CHROME_BIN ?? "google-chrome",
        [
          "--headless=new",
          "--no-sandbox",
          "--disable-gpu",
          "--disable-dev-shm-usage",
          `--remote-debugging-port=${PORT}`,
          "about:blank",
        ],
        { stdio: "ignore" }
      )
      
      const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms))
      
      async function waitForTarget() {
        for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
          try {
            const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)
            const page = (await res.json()).find((t) => t.type === "page")
            if (page?.webSocketDebuggerUrl) return page.webSocketDebuggerUrl
          } catch {}
          await sleep(250)
        }
        throw new Error("Chrome DevTools endpoint never became ready")
      }
      
      const ws = new WebSocket(await waitForTarget())
      await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        ws.onopen = resolve
        ws.onerror = reject
      })
      
      let nextId = 1
      const pending = new Map()
      const events = []
      let intercepted = 0
      ws.onmessage = (event) => {
        const msg = JSON.parse(event.data)
        if (msg.method === "Runtime.consoleAPICalled") {
          events.push(
            msg.params.type + ": " + msg.params.args.map((a) => a.value ?? a.description ?? "").join(" ").slice(0, 300)
          )
        }
        if (msg.method === "Log.entryAdded") {
          events.push(msg.params.entry.level + ": " + String(msg.params.entry.text).slice(0, 300))
        }
        if (msg.method === "Fetch.requestPaused") {
          intercepted++
          // Answer the intercepted request with a 500, like a broken search API would.
          send("Fetch.fulfillRequest", {
            requestId: msg.params.requestId,
            responseCode: 500,
            responseHeaders: [{ name: "content-type", value: "application/json" }],
            body: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ message: "Internal Server Error" })).toString("base64"),
          }).catch(() => {})
          return
        }
        if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) {
          const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(msg.id)
          pending.delete(msg.id)
          msg.error ? reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error))) : resolve(msg.result)
        }
      }
      const send = (method, params = {}) =>
        new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
          const id = nextId++
          pending.set(id, { resolve, reject })
          ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }))
        })
      
      await send("Page.enable")
      await send("Runtime.enable")
      await send("Log.enable")
      if (blockArg) {
        await send("Network.enable")
        if (blockArg.startsWith("fail500:")) {
          await send("Fetch.enable", {
            patterns: [{ urlPattern: blockArg.slice("fail500:".length), requestStage: "Request" }],
          })
        } else {
          await send("Network.setBlockedURLs", { urls: [blockArg] })
        }
      }
      await send("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", {
        width,
        height: 900,
        deviceScaleFactor: 1,
        mobile: width < 768,
      })
      await send("Page.navigate", { url })
      await sleep(wait)
      
      const { result } = await send("Runtime.evaluate", {
        expression: readFileSync(exprFile, "utf8"),
        returnByValue: true,
        awaitPromise: true,
      })
      console.log(JSON.stringify(result.value, null, 2))
      if (blockArg) {
        console.error("intercepted requests: " + intercepted)
      }
      if (events.length) {
        console.error("page console/log:")
        events.slice(0, 12).forEach((e) => console.error("  " + e))
      }
      
      ws.close()
      chrome.kill("SIGKILL")

- path: /tmp/devcart-responsive.mjs
  content: |
      // Verifies the DevCart homepage at the project's three reference widths using
      // raw CDP over Node's built-in WebSocket (no extra dependencies).
      import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
      
      const URL_TO_CHECK = process.argv[2] ?? "http://localhost:8000/dk"
      const PORT = 9333
      
      const chrome = spawn(
        process.env.CHROME_BIN ?? "google-chrome",
        [
          "--headless=new",
          "--no-sandbox",
          "--disable-gpu",
          "--disable-dev-shm-usage",
          `--remote-debugging-port=${PORT}`,
          "about:blank",
        ],
        { stdio: "ignore" }
      )
      
      const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms))
      
      async function waitForTarget() {
        for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
          try {
            const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)
            const targets = await res.json()
            const page = targets.find((t) => t.type === "page")
            if (page?.webSocketDebuggerUrl) return page.webSocketDebuggerUrl
          } catch {
            // browser not up yet
          }
          await sleep(250)
        }
        throw new Error("Chrome DevTools endpoint never became ready")
      }
      
      const wsUrl = await waitForTarget()
      const ws = new WebSocket(wsUrl)
      await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        ws.onopen = resolve
        ws.onerror = reject
      })
      
      let nextId = 1
      const pending = new Map()
      ws.onmessage = (event) => {
        const msg = JSON.parse(event.data)
        if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) {
          const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(msg.id)
          pending.delete(msg.id)
          msg.error ? reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error))) : resolve(msg.result)
        }
      }
      
      const send = (method, params = {}) =>
        new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
          const id = nextId++
          pending.set(id, { resolve, reject })
          ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }))
        })
      
      const evaluate = async (expression) => {
        const { result } = await send("Runtime.evaluate", {
          expression,
          returnByValue: true,
          awaitPromise: true,
        })
        return result.value
      }
      
      await send("Page.enable")
      await send("Runtime.enable")
      
      const widths = [360, 768, 1280]
      const report = []
      
      for (const width of widths) {
        await send("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", {
          width,
          height: 900,
          deviceScaleFactor: 1,
          mobile: width < 768,
        })
        await send("Page.navigate", { url: URL_TO_CHECK })
        await sleep(4000)
      
        const data = await evaluate(`(() => {
          const overflow = [...document.querySelectorAll("body *")]
            .filter((el) => el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 1 && el.clientWidth > 0)
            .slice(0, 5)
            .map((el) => el.tagName.toLowerCase() + "." + String(el.className).slice(0, 60))
          const rails = document.querySelectorAll('section[aria-labelledby^="collection-"]')
          const cards = rails[0] ? rails[0].querySelectorAll("li").length : 0
          return {
            docScrollWidth: document.documentElement.scrollWidth,
            innerWidth: window.innerWidth,
            headings: [...document.querySelectorAll("h1,h2")].map((h) => h.textContent.trim()),
            categoryLinks: [...document.querySelectorAll('a[href*="/categories/"]')].length,
            collectionLinks: [...document.querySelectorAll('a[href*="/collections/"]')].length,
            rails: rails.length,
            cardsInFirstRail: cards,
            overflow,
          }
        })()`)
      
        report.push({ width, ...data })
      }
      
      console.log(JSON.stringify(report, null, 2))
      ws.close()
      chrome.kill("SIGKILL")

Object.keys(r.body.cart).slice(0, 5) : r.body,\n    })\n  )\n}\n\n// Does the product API agree about the variant's stock, and what does the cart\n// line item actually resolve for the same variant?\nconsole.log(\n  \"product variant inventory_quantity:\",\n  variant.inventory_quantity,\n  variant.manage_inventory,\n  variant.allow_backorder\n)\n\nconst cart = (await j(\"/store/carts\", {\n  method: \"POST\",\n  body: JSON.stringify({ region_id: region.id }),\n})).body.cart\nawait j(`/store/carts/${cart.id}/line-items`, {\n  method: \"POST\",\n  body: JSON.stringify({ variant_id: variant.id, quantity: 1 }),\n})\nconst withAll = await j(\n  `/store/carts/${cart.id}?fields=${encodeURIComponent(\"*items.variant\")}`\n)\nconst line = withAll.body.cart.items[0]\nconsole.log(\"line variant keys:\", Object.keys(line.variant ?? {}).sort().join(\",\"))\nconsole.log(\n  \"line variant inventory-ish:\",\n  JSON.stringify({\n    inventory_quantity: line.variant?.inventory_quantity,\n    inventory_items: line.variant?.inventory_items,\n    manage_inventory: line.variant?.manage_inventory,\n    allow_backorder: line.variant?.allow_backorder,\n    variant_id: line.variant_id,\n  })\n)\n\n// And the product API for the line item's variant id, as a fallback source.\nconst one = await j(\n  `/store/products/${line.product_id}?region_id=${region.id}&fields=*variants,+variants.inventory_quantity`\n)\nconsole.log(\n  \"product lookup per line:\",\n  one.status,\n  one.body?.product?.variants\n    ?.filter((v) => v.id === line.variant_id)\n    .map((v) => ({ id: v.id, qty: v.inventory_quantity }))\n)\n"

      import { Container, clx } from "@modules/common/components/ui"
      import Image from "next/image"
      import React from "react"
      
      import PlaceholderImage from "@modules/common/icons/placeholder-image"
      
      type ThumbnailProps = {
        thumbnail?: string | null
        images?: { url?: string }[] | null
        size?: "small" | "medium" | "large" | "full" | "square"
        isFeatured?: boolean
        className?: string
        "data-testid"?: string
      }
      
      const Thumbnail: React.FC<ThumbnailProps> = ({
        thumbnail,
        images,
        size = "small",
        isFeatured,
        className,
        "data-testid": dataTestid,
      }) => {
        const initialImage = thumbnail || images?.[0]?.url
      
        return (
          <Container
            className={clx(
              "relative w-full overflow-hidden p-4 bg-ui-bg-subtle shadow-elevation-card-rest rounded-large group-hover:shadow-elevation-card-hover transition-shadow ease-in-out duration-150",
              className,
              {
                "aspect-[11/14]": isFeatured,
                "aspect-[9/16]": !isFeatured && size !== "square",
                "aspect-[1/1]": size === "square",
                "w-[180px]": size === "small",
                "w-[290px]": size === "medium",
                "w-[440px]": size === "large",
                "w-full": size === "full",
              }
            )}
            data-testid={dataTestid}
          >
            <ImageOrPlaceholder image={initialImage} size={size} />
          </Container>
        )
      }
      
      const ImageOrPlaceholder = ({
        image,
        size,
      }: Pick<ThumbnailProps, "size"> & { image?: string }) => {
        return image ? (
          <Image
            src={image}
            alt="Thumbnail"
            className="absolute inset-0 object-cover object-center"
            draggable={false}
            quality={50}
            sizes="(max-width: 576px) 280px, (max-width: 768px) 360px, (max-width: 992px) 480px, 800px"
            fill
          />
        ) : (
          <div className="w-full h-full absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center">
            <PlaceholderImage size={size === "small" ? 16 : 24} />
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default Thumbnail
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/products/components/product-card/index.tsx
  content: |
      import Image from "next/image"
      import clsx from "clsx"
      
      import { Plate } from "@modules/design-system"
      import LocalizedClientLink from "@modules/common/components/localized-client-link"
      
      /*
       * The one product card in the storefront, built on the design-system plate so a
       * listing, a homepage rail and any other strip read as the same printed plate
       * (square corners, hairline ink border, image well, text block below).
       *
       * Price and meta are passed in rather than looked up here because their source
       * differs: server-rendered pages price a variant through `getProductPrice`,
       * while the search-driven listing reads the indexed price fields off a hit.
       */
      type ProductCardProps = {
        href: string
        title: string
        thumbnail?: string | null
        price?: React.ReactNode
        meta?: React.ReactNode
        /** Set on cards visible without scrolling so the image loads eagerly. */
        priority?: boolean
        /** `li` when the card is a grid item inside a list. */
        as?: "article" | "div" | "li"
        className?: string
      }
      
      const IMAGE_SIZES = "(max-width: 1024px) 50vw, (max-width: 1280px) 33vw, 25vw"
      
      const ProductCard = ({
        href,
        title,
        thumbnail,
        price,
        meta,
        priority,
        as = "article",
        className,
      }: ProductCardProps) => {
        return (
          <Plate as={as} className={clsx("group", className)}>
            <LocalizedClientLink
              href={href}
              className="flex flex-col focus-visible:outline-offset-[-2px]"
              data-testid="product-wrapper"
            >
              <Plate.Media>
                {thumbnail ? (
                  <Image
                    src={thumbnail}
                    alt={title}
                    fill
                    sizes={IMAGE_SIZES}
                    priority={priority}
                    className="object-cover object-center"
                  />
                ) : (
                  <span className="absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center text-small text-ink/60">
                    No image
                  </span>
                )}
              </Plate.Media>
              <Plate.Body>
                <Plate.Title data-testid="product-title">{title}</Plate.Title>
                {price ? <Plate.Price>{price}</Plate.Price> : null}
                {meta ? <Plate.Meta>{meta}</Plate.Meta> : null}
              </Plate.Body>
            </LocalizedClientLink>
          </Plate>
        )
      }
      
      export default ProductCard
      
  referencedBy: {}

      import clsx from "clsx"
      import {
        ButtonHTMLAttributes,
        forwardRef,
        HTMLAttributes,
        InputHTMLAttributes,
        LabelHTMLAttributes,
        TableHTMLAttributes,
        TdHTMLAttributes,
        ThHTMLAttributes,
      } from "react"
      
      // TODO: Add Toaster component back when needed for notifications
      
      // Re-export clsx as clx for compatibility
      export { clsx as clx }
      
      // Text Component
      type TextProps = HTMLAttributes<HTMLParagraphElement> & {
        as?: "p" | "span" | "div"
      }
      
      export const Text = forwardRef<HTMLParagraphElement, TextProps>(
        ({ className, as: Component = "p", children, ...props }, ref) => {
          return (
            <Component ref={ref} className={clsx("txt-medium", className)} {...props}>
              {children}
            </Component>
          )
        }
      )
      Text.displayName = "Text"

      const TableCell = forwardRef<HTMLTableCellElement, TableCellProps>(

      export const Table = Object.assign(TableRoot, {

      Checkbox.displayName = "Checkbox"

{
  "path": "apps/storefront/src/lib/util/medusa-error.ts",
  "instructions": "Translate the API's inventory error into copy the customer can act on.",
  "content": "type MedusaError = {\n  response?: {\n    data: { message?: string; code?: string } | string\n    status: number\n    headers: unknown\n  }\n  request?: unknown\n  message?: string\n  config?: { url: string; baseURL: string }\n}\n\n/*\n * Errors a customer can fix. The API's own wording (\"Some variant does not\n * have the required inventory\") says what broke but not what to do about it,\n * which is what docs/DESIGN.md §5.6 asks an error to say.\n */\nconst CUSTOMER_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {\n  insufficient_inventory:\n    \"There isn't enough stock left for that quantity. Lower it and try again.\",\n}\n\nexport default function medusaError(error: unknown): never {\n  const err = error as MedusaError\n  if (err.response) {\n    const u = new URL(err.config?.url ?? \"\", err.config?.baseURL ?? \"\")\n    console.error(\"Resource:\", u.toString())\n    console.error(\"Response data:\", err.response.data)\n    console.error(\"Status code:\", err.response.status)\n    console.error(\"Headers:\", err.response.headers)\n\n    const data = err.response.data\n    const code =\n      typeof data === \"object\" && data !== null ? data.code : undefined\n    const message =\n      typeof data === \"object\" && data !== null\n        ? data.message || String(data)\n        : data\n\n    if (code && CUSTOMER_MESSAGES[code]) {\n      throw new Error(CUSTOMER_MESSAGES[code])\n    }\n\n    throw new Error(message.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + message.slice(1) + \".\")\n  } else if (err.request) {\n    throw new Error(\"No response received: \" + String(err.request))\n  } else {\n    throw new Error(\"Error setting up the request: \" + err.message)\n  }\n}\n"
}

{
  "path": "apps/storefront/src/lib/util/stock.ts",
  "instructions": "Add a single rule for how many units of a variant remain buyable.",
  "content": "import { HttpTypes } from \"@medusajs/types\"\n\n/**\n * How many units of a variant a single line may hold: the inventory the product\n * API reports when the variant is tracked and cannot be back-ordered, or `null`\n * when stock is not a limit at all.\n *\n * The cart response carries no inventory (checked against the Store API: the\n * line item's variant has `manage_inventory` but no `inventory_quantity`), so\n * every caller reads this from a product variant instead.\n */\nexport const remainingUnits = (\n  variant: Pick<\n    HttpTypes.StoreProductVariant,\n    \"manage_inventory\" | \"allow_backorder\" | \"inventory_quantity\"\n  >\n): number | null => {\n  if (!variant.manage_inventory || variant.allow_backorder) {\n    return null\n  }\n\n  return Math.max(variant.inventory_quantity ?? 0, 0)\n}\n"
}

Returns an empty map rather than throwing: a cart page that cannot\n * reach the catalogue should still render the cart it already has.\n */\nexport const listVariantAvailability = async ({\n  productIds,\n  countryCode,\n  regionId,\n}: {\n  productIds: string[]\n  countryCode?: string\n  regionId?: string\n}): Promise<Record<string, number | null>> => {\n  const ids = Array.from(new Set(productIds.filter(Boolean)))\n\n  if (!ids.length) {\n    return {}\n  }\n\n  try {\n    const { response } = await listProducts({\n      queryParams: { id: ids, limit: 100 },\n      countryCode,\n      regionId,\n    })\n\n    return response.products.reduce<Record<string, number | null>>(\n      (availability, product) => {\n        for (const variant of product.variants ??   "content": "\"use client\"\n\nimport { useState } from \"react\"\n\nimport { deleteLineItem } from \"@lib/data/cart\"\nimport { Spinner, Trash } from \"@medusajs/icons\"\nimport { clx } from \"@modules/common/components/ui\"\n\nconst DeleteButton = ({\n  id,\n  children,\n  className,\n  \"data-testid\": dataTestId,\n}: {\n  id: string\n  children?: React.ReactNode\n  className?: string\n  \"data-testid\"?: string\n}) => {\n  const [isDeleting, setIsDeleting] = useState(false)\n  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)\n\n  /*\n   * A removal that fails has to say so: the line stays on screen, so without a\n   * message the click would look like it did nothing.\n   */\n  const handleDelete = async (id: string) => {\n    setError(null)\n    setIsDeleting(true)\n\n    try {\n      await deleteLineItem(id)\n    } catch (cause) {\n      setError(\n        cause instanceof Error && cause.message\n          ? cause.message\n          : \"Could not remove this item. Try again.\"\n      )\n      setIsDeleting(false)\n    }\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className={clx(\"flex flex-col gap-1\", className)}>\n      <button\n        type=\"button\"\n        aria-busy={isDeleting || undefined}\n        disabled={isDeleting}\n        className=\"flex w-fit items-center gap-1.5 text-ink/70 underline decoration-1 underline-offset-4 transition-colors hover:text-ink disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:text-ink/40\"\n        onClick={() => handleDelete(id)}\n        data-testid={dataTestId}\n      >\n        {isDeleting ? (\n          <Spinner className=\"animate-spin\" aria-hidden=\"true\" />\n        ) : (\n          <Trash aria-hidden=\"true\" />\n        )}\n        <span>{children}</span>\n      </button>\n\n      {error ? (\n        <p role=\"alert\" className=\"text-small text-ink\">\n          {error}\n        </p>\n      ) : null}\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n\nexport default DeleteButton\n"
}

  "content": "import { convertToLocale } from \"@lib/util/money\"\nimport { HttpTypes } from \"@medusajs/types\"\n\ntype LineItemPriceProps = {\n  item: HttpTypes.StoreCartLineItem | HttpTypes.StoreOrderLineItem\n  style?: \"default\" | \"tight\"\n  currencyCode: string\n}\n\n/**\n * A line's total. A reduced price keeps the original beside it, struck through:\n * the discount is real information, and `riso-pink` is not allowed as text at\n * this size (docs/DESIGN.md §2.1), so ink and a strike carry it instead.\n */\nconst LineItemPrice = ({\n  item,\n  currencyCode,\n}: LineItemPriceProps) => {\n  const originalPrice = item.original_total ?? 0\n  const currentPrice = item.total ?? 0\n  const hasReducedPrice = currentPrice < originalPrice\n\n  return (\n    <p className=\"flex items-baseline gap-2 font-mono text-body text-ink\">\n      {hasReducedPrice ? (\n        <s\n          className=\"text-small text-ink/60\"\n          data-testid=\"product-original-price\"\n        >\n          {convertToLocale({\n            amount: originalPrice,\n            currency_code: currencyCode,\n          })}\n        </s>\n      ) : null}\n      <span data-testid=\"product-price\">\n        {convertToLocale({ amount: currentPrice, currency_code: currencyCode })}\n      </span>\n    </p>\n  )\n}\n\nexport default LineItemPrice\n"

0, currency_code })\n\n  return (\n    <div data-testid=\"cart-totals\">\n      <dl className=\"flex flex-col gap-2 text-small text-ink\">\n        <div className=\"flex items-center justify-between gap-4\">\n          <dt>Subtotal (excl. shipping and taxes)</dt>\n          <dd className=\"font-mono\" data-testid=\"cart-subtotal\" data-value={item_subtotal || 0}>\n            {amount(item_subtotal)}\n          </dd>\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"flex items-center justify-between gap-4\">\n          <dt>Shipping</dt>\n          <dd className=\"font-mono\" data-testid=\"cart-shipping\" data-value={shipping_subtotal || 0}>\n            {amount(shipping_subtotal)}\n          </dd>\n        </div>\n        {!!discount_subtotal && (\n          <div className=\"flex items-center justify-between gap-4\">\n            <dt>Discount</dt>\n            <dd\n              className=\"font-mono text-riso-green\"\n              data-testid=\"cart-discount\"\n              data-value={discount_subtotal || 0}\n            >\n              -{amount(Math.abs(discount_subtotal))}\n            </dd>\n          </div>\n        )}\n        <div className=\"flex items-center justify-between gap-4\">\n          <dt>Taxes</dt>\n          <dd className=\"font-mono\" data-testid=\"cart-taxes\" data-value={tax_total || 0}>\n            {amount(tax_total)}\n          </dd>\n        </div>\n      </dl>\n\n      <Rule className=\"my-4\" weight=\"heavy\" />\n\n      <div className=\"flex items-baseline justify-between gap-4\">\n        <span className=\"text-body font-semibold\">Total</span>\n        <span\n          className=\"font-mono text-lead\"\n          data-testid=\"cart-total\"\n          data-value={total || 0}\n        >\n          {amount(total)}\n        </span>\n      </div>\n\n      <Rule className=\"mt-4\" />\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n\nexport default CartTotals\n"

{
  "path": "apps/storefront/src/modules/cart/templates/items.tsx",
  "instructions": "Rebuild the cart's line list, feeding each row its remaining stock.",
  "content": "import repeat from \"@lib/util/repeat\"\nimport { HttpTypes } from \"@medusajs/types\"\n\nimport Item from \"@modules/cart/components/item\"\n\ntype ItemsTemplateProps = {\n  cart?: HttpTypes.StoreCart\n  /** Units left per variant id; `null` where stock is not a limit. */\n  availability?: Record<string, number | null>\n}\n\n/** Placeholder row shown only if the cart has not resolved yet. */\nconst SkeletonRow = () => (\n  <li\n    className=\"flex gap-4 border-b border-ink/20 py-6\"\n    data-testid=\"cart-item-loader\"\n  >\n    <div className=\"h-20 w-20 shrink-0 animate-pulse bg-ink/10 small:h-24 small:w-24\" />\n    <div className=\"flex flex-1 flex-col gap-3\">\n      <div className=\"h-4 w-40 animate-pulse bg-ink/10\" />\n      <div className=\"h-4 w-24 animate-pulse bg-ink/10\" />\n      <div className=\"h-4 w-20 animate-pulse bg-ink/10\" />\n    </div>\n  </li>\n)\n\n/**\n * The cart's lines. Quantities come from the cart, but how many units are left\n * has to come from the product side — the cart payload does not carry inventory\n * — so the page resolves it once and hands the map down.\n */\nconst ItemsTemplate = ({ cart, availability = {} }: ItemsTemplateProps) => {\n  const items = cart?.items\n  const currencyCode = cart?.currency_code ?? \"\"\n\n  return (\n    <ul className=\"flex flex-col border-t border-ink/20\" data-testid=\"cart-items\">\n      {items\n        ? items\n            .slice()\n            .sort((a, b) => {\n              return (a.created_at ?? \"\") > (b.created_at ?? \"\") ? -1 : 1\n            })\n            .map((item) => (\n              <Item\n                key={item.id}\n                item={item}\n                currencyCode={currencyCode}\n                availableUnits={\n                  item.variant_id && item.variant_id in availability\n                    ? availability[item.variant_id]\n                    : undefined\n                }\n              />\n            ))\n        : repeat(5).map((index) => <SkeletonRow key={index} />)}\n    </ul>\n  )\n}\n\nexport default ItemsTemplate\n"
}

  "path": "apps/storefront/src/modules/cart/templates/summary.tsx",
  "instructions": "Rebuild the cart summary and block checkout when a quantity exceeds stock.",
  "content": "\"use client\"\n\nimport { HttpTypes } from \"@medusajs/types\"\n\nimport CartTotals from \"@modules/common/components/cart-totals\"\nimport LocalizedClientLink from \"@modules/common/components/localized-client-link\"\nimport { Rule, buttonClass } from \"@modules/design-system\"\nimport DiscountCode from \"@modules/checkout/components/discount-code\"\n\ntype SummaryProps = {\n  cart: HttpTypes.StoreCart\n  /** Units left per variant id; `null` where stock is not a limit. */\n  availability?: Record<string, number | null>\n}\n\nfunction getCheckoutStep(cart: HttpTypes.StoreCart) {\n  if (!cart?.shipping_address?.address_1 || !cart.email) {\n    return \"address\"\n  } else if (cart?.shipping_methods?.length === 0) {\n    return \"delivery\"\n  } else {\n    return \"payment\"\n  }\n}\n\nconst Summary = ({ cart, availability = {} }: SummaryProps) => {\n  const step = getCheckoutStep(cart)\n\n  /*\n   * A line can be left holding more units than the catalogue has: the stock can\n   * drop under it while the cart waits. Checkout would fail on it later, so the\n   * cart says what to fix and holds the button until it is fixed.\n   */\n  const linesOverStock = (cart.items ?? []).filter((item) => {\n    const available = item.variant_id ? availability[item.variant_id] : undefined\n\n    return typeof available === \"number\" && item.quantity > available\n  })\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"flex flex-col gap-4\">\n      <h2 className=\"font-display text-lead font-semibold text-ink\">Summary</h2>\n\n      <DiscountCode cart={cart} />\n\n      <Rule />\n\n      <CartTotals totals={cart} />\n\n      {linesOverStock.length > 0 ? (\n        <p\n          role=\"status\"\n          className=\"text-small font-semibold text-ink\"\n          data-testid=\"checkout-stock-warning\"\n        >\n          Some quantities are above what is left in stock. Lower them to\n          continue.\n        </p>\n      ) : null}\n\n      {linesOverStock.length > 0 ? (\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          disabled\n          className={buttonClass({ size: \"large\", className: \"w-full\" })}\n          data-testid=\"checkout-button\"\n        >\n          Go to checkout\n        </button>\n      ) : (\n        <LocalizedClientLink\n          href={\"/checkout?step=\" + step}\n          className={buttonClass({ size: \"large\", className: \"w-full\" })}\n          data-testid=\"checkout-button\"\n        >\n          Go to checkout\n        </LocalizedClientLink>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n\nexport default Summary\n"
}

  "content": "import { retrieveCart } from \"@lib/data/cart\"\nimport { retrieveCustomer } from \"@lib/data/customer\"\nimport { listVariantAvailability } from \"@lib/data/products\"\nimport CartTemplate from \"@modules/cart/templates\"\nimport { Metadata } from \"next\"\nimport { notFound } from \"next/navigation\"\n\nexport const metadata: Metadata = {\n  title: \"Cart\",\n  description: \"View your cart\",\n}\n\nexport default async function Cart() {\n  const cart = await retrieveCart().catch((error) => {\n    console.error(error)\n    return notFound()\n  })\n\n  const customer = await retrieveCustomer()\n\n  /*\n   * The cart holds quantities but not stock, so the caps and warnings on the\n   * line items are resolved from the products those lines point at. []\n\n  const availability = cart?.region_id\n    ? await listVariantAvailability({ productIds, regionId: cart.region_id })\n    : {}\n\n  return (\n    <CartTemplate\n      cart={cart}\n      customer={customer}\n      availability={availability}\n    />\n  )\n}\n"

      import clsx from "clsx"
      import React from "react"
      
      import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
      
      type OptionSelectProps = {
        option: HttpTypes.StoreProductOption
        current: string | undefined
        updateOption: (title: string, value: string) => void
        title: string
        disabled: boolean
        "data-testid"?: string
      }
      
      /*
       * A group of options (Size, Colour) as square chips. `aria-pressed` carries the
       * selection so it is not communicated by border colour alone.
       */
      const OptionSelect: React.FC<OptionSelectProps> = ({
        option,
        current,
        updateOption,
        title,
        "data-testid": dataTestId,
        disabled,
      }) => {
        const filteredOptions = (option.values ?? []).map((v) => v.value)
      
        return (
          <fieldset className="flex flex-col gap-2" data-testid={dataTestId}>
            <legend className="pb-1 text-small font-semibold text-ink">{title}</legend>
            <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
              {filteredOptions.map((v) => {
                const isSelected = v === current
      
                return (
                  <button
                    key={v}
                    type="button"
                    onClick={() => updateOption(option.id, v)}
                    aria-pressed={isSelected}
                    disabled={disabled}
                    className={clsx(
                      "min-h-11 min-w-12 border px-3 text-small font-semibold transition-colors",
                      isSelected
                        ? "border-ink bg-ink text-stock"
                        : "border-ink/40 bg-stock text-ink hover:border-ink",
                      disabled && "cursor-not-allowed opacity-60"
                    )}
                    data-testid="option-button"
                  >
                    {v}
                  </button>
                )
              })}
            </div>
          </fieldset>
        )
      }
      
      export default OptionSelect

- path: apps/storefront/src/lib/data/regions.ts
  content: |
      "use server"
      
      import { sdk } from "@lib/config"
      import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
      import { getCacheOptions } from "./cookies"
      
      export const listRegions = async () => {
        const next = {
          ...(await getCacheOptions("regions")),
        }
      
        return await sdk.client
          .fetch<{ regions: HttpTypes.StoreRegion[] }>(`/store/regions`, {
            method: "GET",
            next,
            cache: "force-cache",
          })
          .then(({ regions }) => regions)
      }
      
      export const retrieveRegion = async (id: string) => {
        const next = {
          ...(await getCacheOptions(["regions", id].join("-"))),
        }
      
        return await sdk.client
          .fetch<{ region: HttpTypes.StoreRegion }>(`/store/regions/${id}`, {
            method: "GET",
            next,
            cache: "force-cache",
          })
          .then(({ region }) => region)
      }
      
      const regionMap = new Map<string, HttpTypes.StoreRegion>()
      
      export const getRegion = async (countryCode: string) => {
        if (regionMap.has(countryCode)) {
          return regionMap.get(countryCode)
        }
      
        const regions = await listRegions()
      
        if (!regions) {
          return null
        }
      
        regions.forEach((region) => {
          region.countries?.forEach((c) => {
            regionMap.set(c?.iso_2 ?? "", region)
          })
        })
      
        const region = countryCode
          ? regionMap.get(countryCode)
          : regionMap.get("us")
      
        return region
      }
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: apps/storefront/src/lib/data/cookies.ts
  content: |
      import "server-only"
      import { cookies as nextCookies } from "next/headers"
      
      export const getAuthHeaders = async (): Promise<
        { authorization: string } | Record<string, never>
      > => {
        try {
          const cookies = await nextCookies()
          const token = cookies.get("_medusa_jwt")?.value
      
          if (!token) {
            return {}
          }
      
          return { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }
        } catch {
          return {}
        }
      }
      
      export const getCacheTag = async (tag: string): Promise<string> => {
        try {
          const cookies = await nextCookies()
          const cacheId = cookies.get("_medusa_cache_id")?.value
      
          if (!cacheId) {
            return ""
          }
      
          return `${tag}-${cacheId}`
        } catch {
          return ""
        }
      }
      
      export const getCacheOptions = async (
        tag: string
      ): Promise<{ tags: string[] } | Record<string, never>> => {
        if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
          return {}
        }
      
        const cacheTag = await getCacheTag(tag)
      
        if (!cacheTag) {
          return {}
        }
      
        return { tags: [`${cacheTag}`] }
      }
      
      // `sameSite: "lax"` rather than `"strict"`: the customer returns from a
      // redirect-based payment method (iDEAL, Bancontact, ...) via a cross-site
      // top-level navigation. A "strict" cookie is withheld on that navigation, so
      // the storefront would see a logged-out, cartless visitor and render a 404 for
      // the checkout page instead of resuming the order. "lax" is sent on top-level
      // GET navigations while still blocking cross-site subrequests.
      export const setAuthToken = async (token: string) => {
        const cookies = await nextCookies()
        cookies.set("_medusa_jwt", token, {
          maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7,
          httpOnly: true,
          sameSite: "lax",
          secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production",
        })
      }
      
      export const removeAuthToken = async () => {
        const cookies = await nextCookies()
        cookies.set("_medusa_jwt", "", {
          maxAge: -1,
        })
      }
      
      export type PendingCustomer = {
        email: string
        first_name?: string
        last_name?: string
        phone?: string
      }
      
      // During the email verification flow the customer record isn't created until
      // the customer verifies their email and logs in. We temporarily persist the
      // extra signup fields in a cookie so they survive the customer leaving to open
      // their inbox, and read them back when creating the customer at login.
      export const setPendingCustomer = async (customer: PendingCustomer) => {
        const cookies = await nextCookies()
        cookies.set("_medusa_pending_customer", JSON.stringify(customer), {
          maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24,
          httpOnly: true,
          sameSite: "strict",
          secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production",
        })
      }
      
      export const getPendingCustomer = async (): Promise<PendingCustomer | null> => {
        const cookies = await nextCookies()
        const value = cookies.get("_medusa_pending_customer")?.value
      
        if (!value) {
          return null
        }
      
        try {
          return JSON.parse(value) as PendingCustomer
        } catch {
          return null
        }
      }
      
      export const removePendingCustomer = async () => {
        const cookies = await nextCookies()
        cookies.set("_medusa_pending_customer", "", {
          maxAge: -1,
        })
      }
      
      export const getCartId = async () => {
        const cookies = await nextCookies()
        return cookies.get("_medusa_cart_id")?.value
      }
      
      // See the note on `setAuthToken`: `sameSite: "lax"` so the cart cookie survives
      // the cross-site return navigation from a redirect-based payment method.
      export const setCartId = async (cartId: string) => {
        const cookies = await nextCookies()
        cookies.set("_medusa_cart_id", cartId, {
          maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7,
          httpOnly: true,
          sameSite: "lax",
          secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production",
        })
      }
      
      export const removeCartId = async () => {
        const cookies = await nextCookies()
        cookies.set("_medusa_cart_id", "", {
          maxAge: -1,
        })
      }

> Critical finding: With stocked_quantity = 1 in the DB, the API *accepted* a quantity of 5. So the API's inventory check didn't see my DB change. Why?
> 
> Possibilities:
> 1. The cart update validates against **reservations/availability computed from a cached value**.
> 2. Medusa's inventory validation uses `inventory_item` levels from a cache (the inventory module may cache availability per request, not cross-request).
> 3. My psql UPDATE changed `stocked_quantity`, but the API computes availability from `inventory_level` rows joined with reservations... and maybe there are *multiple* inventory levels (e.g. a second location). stockNow=1 was read via the same join → 1 row.
> 4. Medusa's `inventory_quantity` on product variants is a *computed field* that may be cached in the product module's own cache? Hmm.
> 5. Maybe the update workflow's validation is bypassed when the line item already exists and simply adds the delta? No — earlier, setting 99 on a cart with stock 5 was rejected. So validation exists.
> 6. Perhaps my psql update happened but Medusa's DB connection sees a snapshot? No.
> 7. **Maybe the update path succeeded because the reservation for the existing line item counts**: available = stocked - reserved. With stocked=1 and reserved=2 (the cart's own reservation for 2 units), available = -1... it would still reject 5.
> 
> Hmm, what about the possibility that Medusa's inventory check uses `allow_backorder`... no, it's false.
> 
> Wait — maybe the DB update didn't actually affect the row the module reads: e.g. there could be a *second* inventory_level row (another location) with a big stock, and my join returned only the first row (stockNow=1 is the row I updated). Then the API's availability = sum/max across locations? In Medusa v2, a variant's available quantity depends on the sales channel/location: `inventory_quantity` = quantity available at the locations linked to the sales channel. If there are two locations (the seed creates a warehouse location; maybe also "default"), and the variant's inventory item has levels at both, then available might be computed from the location serving the cart's sales channel. If the other location has plenty, the API sees plenty.

  "instructions": "Split the translation out of the throw so mutations can return a message instead.",
  "content": "type MedusaError = {\n  response?: {\n    data: { message?: string; code?: string } | string\n    status: number\n    headers: unknown\n  }\n  request?: unknown\n  message?: string\n  config?: { url: string; baseURL: string }\n}\n\n/*\n * Errors a customer can fix. The API's own wording (\"Some variant does not\n * have the required inventory\") says what broke but not what to do about it,\n * which is what docs/DESIGN.md §5.6 asks an error to say.\n */\nconst CUSTOMER_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {\n  insufficient_inventory:\n    \"There isn't enough stock left for that quantity. Lower it and try again.\",\n}\n\n/**\n * What to show the customer for a failed request: the API's message, or plain\n * copy for the cases it words awkwardly.\n *\n * Server actions have to *return* this rather than throw it. Next replaces a\n * thrown error from a server action in a production build with \"An error\n * occurred in the Server Components render. The specific message is omitted in\n * production builds\" — measured on K1's rejected quantity change — so a thrown\n * message never reaches the customer.\n */\nexport default function medusaErrorMessage(error: unknown): string {\n  const err = error as MedusaError\n\n  if (err?.response) {\n    const u = new URL(err.config?.url ?? \"\", err.config?.baseURL ?? \"\")\n    console.error(\"Resource:\", u.toString())\n    console.error(\"Response data:\", err.response.data)\n    console.error(\"Status code:\", err.response.status)\n    console.error(\"Headers:\", err.response.headers)\n\n    const data = err.response.data\n    const code =\n      typeof data === \"object\" && data !== null ? data.code : undefined\n    const message =\n      typeof data === \"object\" && data !== null\n        ? data.message || String(data)\n        : data\n\n    if (code && CUSTOMER_MESSAGES[code]) {\n      return CUSTOMER_MESSAGES[code]\n    }\n\n    return message.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + message.slice(1) + \".\"\n  }\n\n  if (err?.request) {\n    return \"Could not reach the store. Check your connection and try again.\"\n  }\n\n  if (err instanceof Error && err.message) {\n    return err.message\n  }\n\n  return \"Something went wrong. Try again.\"\n}\n"
}

> Big progress. Now:
> 
> ✓ Stock change via Admin API is visible to the Store API (62ms).

```json
{
  "path": "apps/storefront/src/lib/util/medusa-error.ts",
  "instructions": "Translate API failures into customer copy using the message the SDK preserves.",
  "content": "/*\n * The SDK throws a `FetchError extends Error` that keeps the API's message and\n * status but drops the error `code` (see @medusajs/js-sdk's client), so these\n * translations key off Medusa's wording rather than a code.\n *\n * The API's own copy says what broke, not what to do about it, which is what\n * docs/DESIGN.md §5.6 asks an error to say.\n */\nconst CUSTOMER_MESSAGES: { match: RegExp; message: string }[] = [\n  {\n    match: /does not have the required inventory/i,\n    message:\n      \"There isn't enough stock left for that quantity. Lower it and try again.\",\n  },\n  {\n    match: /failed to fetch|fetch failed|network/i,\n    message: \"Could not reach the store. Check your connection and try again.\",\n  },\n]\n\n/**\n * What to show the customer for a failed request.\n *\n * Server actions have to *return* this rather than throw it: a production build\n * replaces a thrown error from a server action with \"An error occurred in the\n * Server Components render. The specific message is omitted in production\n * builds\", so a thrown message never reaches the customer (measured on K1's\n * rejected quantity change).\n */\nexport default function medusaErrorMessage(error: unknown): string {\n  const message =\n    error instanceof Error && error.message ? error.message : \"\"\n  const status = (error as { status?: number })?.status\n\n  if (!message) {\n    console.error(\"Store API request failed:\", error)\n    return \"Something went wrong. Try again.\"\n  }\n\n  console.error(\n    `Store API request failed${status ? ` (${status})` : \"\"}: ${message}`\n  )\n\n  const translation = CUSTOMER_MESSAGES.find((entry) =>\n    entry.match.test(message)\n  )\n\n  if (translation) {\n    return translation.message\n  }\n\n  return message.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + message.slice(1) + \".\"\n}\n\n/**\n * The throwing form, for the flows whose caller is a `try`/`catch` around a\n * server action that returns state (checkout, account, orders). Anything a\n * customer reads on a page should use the returned-message form instead.\n */\nexport function medusaError(error: unknown): never {\n  throw new Error(medusaErrorMessage(error))\n}\n"
}

      import {
        createInstantSearchAdapter,
        type MedusaSdkLike,
      } from "@medusajs/instantsearch-adapter"
      
      import { sdk } from "@lib/config"
      
      export const PRODUCT_INDEX_NAME = "product"
      
      /**
       * The currencies the product index holds prices in, one field set each. Keep
       * in sync with `PRICE_CURRENCIES` in the backend's `src/search/product.ts`.
       */
      export const SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES = ["eur", "usd"]
      
      export type PriceField =
        | "min_price"
        | "max_price"
        | "original_price"
        | "on_sale"
      
      /**
       * The indexed currency to read prices in for a region. A region whose currency
       * the index doesn't hold falls back to the first one, so the listing still
       * shows a price rather than none.
       */
      export const indexedCurrency = (currencyCode: string) => {
        const code = currencyCode.toLowerCase()
        return SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES.includes(code)
          ? code
          : SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES[0]
      }
      
      export const priceAttribute = (field: PriceField, currencyCode: string) =>
        `${field}_${indexedCurrency(currencyCode)}`
      
      /**
       * Shared by the navbar search drawer and the store listing. An empty query
       * searches rather than short-circuiting, which is what the listing needs to
       * show every product before anything is refined.
       */
      export const { searchClient } = createInstantSearchAdapter({
        sdk: sdk as unknown as MedusaSdkLike,
        path: "/store/search",
        additionalSearchParameters: {
          search_options: {
            match_strategy: "last",
          },
        },
        // Range widgets read `facets_stats`, which the adapter only produces for
        // fields listed here. The price fields are declared with a `stats` facet on
        // the index, which is what makes the stats available at all.
        numericAttributes: SEARCH_PRICE_CURRENCIES.flatMap((currency) => [
          `min_price_${currency}`,
          `max_price_${currency}`,
        ]),
      })

  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import * as Slider from "@radix-ui/react-slider"
      import { useEffect, useState } from "react"
      import { useRange } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import { indexedCurrency, priceAttribute } from "@lib/search-client"
      
      function formatAmount(amount: number, currency: string) {
        try {
          return new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, {
            style: "currency",
            currency: currency.toUpperCase(),
            maximumFractionDigits: 0,
          }).format(amount)
        } catch {
          // An unrecognised currency code shouldn't take the sidebar down.
          return `${Math.round(amount)} ${currency.toUpperCase()}`
        }
      }
      
      /**
       * Price filter over the region currency's `min_price_*` field, which is
       * declared `facetable({ types: ["stats"] })` — the stats facet is what
       * supplies the slider's bounds. Refines on release rather than per pixel.
       *
       * Hides itself when every remaining product costs the same (or there are no
       * stats yet), because there is nothing to slide between.
       */
      const PriceRange = ({ currencyCode }: { currencyCode: string }) => {
        const { start, range, canRefine, refine } = useRange({
          attribute: priceAttribute("min_price", currencyCode),
        })
        const currency = indexedCurrency(currencyCode)
        const format = (amount: number) => formatAmount(amount, currency)
      
        const min = Math.floor(range.min ?? 0)
        const max = Math.ceil(range.max ?? 0)
      
        // `start` holds ±Infinity for an unset bound, so fall back to the extremes.
        const from = Number.isFinite(start[0]) ? (start[0] as number) : min
        const to = Number.isFinite(start[1]) ? (start[1] as number) : max
      
        const [value, setValue] = useState<number[]>([from, to])
      
        // Follow the refinement when it changes elsewhere — clearing all filters, or
        // a bound arriving from the URL on load.
        useEffect(() => {
          setValue([from, to])
        }, [from, to])
      
        if (!canRefine || min >= max) {
          return null
        }
      
        return (
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
            <span className="text-small font-semibold text-ink">Price</span>
      
            <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 pt-2">
              <Slider.Root
                className="relative flex h-5 w-full touch-none select-none items-center"
                value={value}
                min={min}
                max={max}
                step={1}
                minStepsBetweenThumbs={0}
                onValueChange={setValue}
                // Only refine when the thumb is released, so dragging doesn't fire a
                // search per pixel.
                onValueCommit={(committed) => refine([committed[0], committed[1]])}
                aria-label="Price range"
                data-testid="price-range"
              >
                <Slider.Track className="relative h-0.5 w-full grow bg-ink/20">
                  <Slider.Range className="absolute h-full bg-riso-blue" />
                </Slider.Track>
                {value.map((_, index) => (
                  <Slider.Thumb
                    key={index}
                    className="block h-4 w-4 border border-ink bg-stock outline-none"
                    aria-label={index === 0 ? "Minimum price" : "Maximum price"}
                  />
                ))}
              </Slider.Root>
      
              <div className="flex items-center justify-between font-mono text-micro text-ink/70">
                <span>{format(value[0])}</span>
                <span>{format(value[1])}</span>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        )
      }
      
      export default PriceRange
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: apps/storefront/src/modules/store/components/store-refinements/on-sale-toggle.tsx
  content: |
      "use client"
      
      import { useToggleRefinement } from "react-instantsearch"
      
      import { priceAttribute } from "@lib/search-client"
      
      /**
       * Narrows to products whose calculated price is below their original in the
       * region's currency. Hides itself when nothing is discounted, which is the
       * case until a price list applies to some product.
       */
      const OnSaleToggle = ({ currencyCode }: { currencyCode: string }) => {
        const { value, refine, canRefine } = useToggleRefinement({
          attribute: priceAttribute("on_sale", currencyCode),
          on: true,
        })
      
        if (!canRefine) {
          return null
        }
      
        return (
          <label className="flex cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 text-small">
            <input
              type="checkbox"
              checked={value.isRefined}
              onChange={() => refine(value)}
              className="h-4 w-4 shrink-0 accent-riso-blue"
              data-testid="on-sale-toggle"
            />
            <span className="font-semibold text-ink">On sale only</span>
            {typeof value.count === "number" && (
              <span className="font-mono text-micro text-ink/60">
                {value.count}
              </span>
            )}
          </label>
        )
      }
      
      export default OnSaleToggle
      
  referencedBy: {}

So C5 is fully implemented and verified — nothing to redo there. (My first range probe used a malformed param and looked like a regression; `40:` is the correct InstantSearch syntax.)

## What the interrupted session left: K1 (cart) — now finished and verified

The K1 work in flight was the cart. It is complete, on the production build, verified against the Store API:

- **Add / quantity / remove / totals / persistence:** nav goes to `Cart (1)` and the drawer opens in 608 ms; after every mutation the page's subtotal, taxes, total and per-line totals equal the API's figures (5/5 steps), and the same cart cookie survives a reload. Empty state renders; 0 console errors.
- **Stock:** quantities are stock-derived (hoodie M offers 1–5, what the API reports). With stock moved via the Admin API, a rejected quantity leaves the line at what the cart holds with *"There isn't enough stock left for that quantity. Lower it and try again."*, a line holding 2 of 1 left is flagged and blocks checkout until lowered, and a prerendered product page reports the same rejection inline. Two runs agreed exactly; no overflow at 360/768/1280.

Four real defects surfaced during that verification and were fixed rather than documented away:

1. **Cached cart/stock reads vs. the write that follows** — a stale repaint in ~1 change in 10 (cart) and a stock cap that lagged a real drop. Both reads are now `no-store`.
2. **Production masks thrown server-action errors** — the customer was shown Next's "An error occurred in the Server Components render…". Cart mutations now return `{ ok, message }`; `medusa-error.ts` translates Medusa's wording (the SDK drops the error code).
3. **A select value outside its options could send quantity 0**, which the API reads as "delete this line" — now guarded.
4. **Not-quite-deterministic repaint** — `router.refresh()` after a successful mutation makes it deterministic.

Not run / limitations: `pnpm run test` (no storefront suite, backend untouched by this work, and no live DB test was needed); the promo-code, checkout, account and orders paths still **throw**, so their messages remain masked in production — K6/K2/A1 should adopt the same returned-result pattern (recorded in the roadmap). Cart mutations settle in 300–600 ms because each re-renders the layout; that belongs to the Phase 3 performance pass. Servers: backend untouched and running; the storefront on :8000 is the production build I made for this verification.
